beginner.m: A place is a point in space: a town, building, room, or even somewhere on a desk.
beginner.e: It's nice to see the whole family together in one place.

beginner.m: Your aunt is the sister of your mother or father.
beginner.e: After my parents died, we went to live with my aunt.

beginner.m: A meeting is when a group of people come together to talk about something important.
beginner.e: The meeting will be in the green room after lunch. I hope you'll be there.

beginner.m: When you organize something, you plan or arrange it.
beginner.e: The student organized his class notes.

beginner.m: If something is frightening, it causes fear, it is scary.
beginner.e: The ghost ride was so frightening that I screamed the entire time.

beginner.m: An earthquake is a natural event that causes the ground to shake up and down, and sometimes, may destroy buildings.
beginner.e: The earthquake ripped a crack in the road and destroyed half of the building that I live in.

beginner.m: You say "I'm sorry" when you have done something wrong and you feel bad.
beginner.e: I'm sorry that I lost your jacket last night.

beginner.m: If you confuse someone, they don't understand what you have said or done.
beginner.e: Instead of helping me to learn it, he just confused me more.

beginner.m: To take money or property without permission, sometimes with violence.
beginner.e: The police were called because there had been a bank robbery.

beginner.m: A toe is a little part of a foot, like a finger. A foot has 5 toes.
beginner.e: This shoe is too small -- it gives me pain in my toes.

beginner.m: Something is slow if it takes a long time to move. It is not fast.
beginner.e: A snail is a very slow animal. It moves slowly.

beginner.m: When something happens often, that means that it happens many times and frequently.
beginner.e: How often do you exercise?

beginner.m: The sky is what you see when you look up when you're not inside. It's blue with clouds in it. At night it's black with stars in it.
beginner.e: The night sky was full of stars.

beginner.m: The comparative form of late; more late.
beginner.e: She arrived later than me.

beginner.m: A part of something is one piece of it or a small amount of it.
beginner.e: Part of the page was gone, so I couldn't read it.

beginner.m: You use exactly when you want to say that something is 100% true, not just close.
beginner.e: The movie will start at exactly 7:02 PM.

beginner.m: If something is done widely, it is done to a great extent or a large amount; it is commonly done.
beginner.e: The man opened his arms widely to show how big the fish was.

beginner.m: When you meet someone, you get together with them.
beginner.e: I want to meet you.

beginner.m: A reporter is a person whose job is to learn and tell the news.
beginner.e: I would like to get a job as a reporter for the newspaper.

beginner.m: If someone is lovely, that person is very good to look at. A lovely person is someone that you might love if you saw her or him.
beginner.e: She is such a lovely girl.

beginner.m: Private is for only one person or a small number of people to see or know.
beginner.e: I don't want to tell you how much money I have; that's private.

beginner.m: If something is advanced it has moved beyond the start.
beginner.e: The course is suitable for both beginners and advanced students.

beginner.m: When someone remembers something, we call the thing they remember a memory.
beginner.e: I have very nice memories of the time when my children were young.

beginner.m: A dessert made of sugar and gelatin.
beginner.e: The children celebrated by eating bowls of jelly.

beginner.m: An idea is a concept or a thought.
beginner.e: It was a good idea.

beginner.m: If someone or something is noisy, it is loud and usually annoying.
beginner.e: Students are often noisy in class.

beginner.m: If something is thick, there is some distance from one side to the other.
beginner.e: The tree was too thick to put his arms around.

beginner.m: Evidence is facts or observations that support an idea.
beginner.e: If there is clear evidence for lying, he/she should be punished.

beginner.m: A kitchen is a room used for cooking food.
beginner.e: Bring me a kitchen knife.

beginner.m: When something is difficult, it is not easy.
beginner.e: It'll be difficult to get him to change his mind; he's really stubborn.

beginner.m: A crown is a round-shaped ring that kings and queens wear on the head. It is made of expensive metals. It might have jewels too.
beginner.e: The queen wore a fancy crown.

beginner.m: Boyfriend normally describes a boy or a young man, who is in a love relationship with another person, when they aren't married yet.
beginner.e: I didn't have a boyfriend, and I thought that it was because I was too fat.

beginner.m: If something is ideal, it is as good as you can imagine.
beginner.e: Metal roofs are ideal for catching rainwater.

beginner.m: Success is doing what you plan or want to do.
beginner.e: Getting 100% on the test gave him a feeling of success.

beginner.m: Something that is made by people instead of being made by nature.
beginner.e: The silk flowers were not real. They were artificial.

beginner.m: Very bad. So bad that people don't want to think about it.
beginner.e: When all the children were crying, it was just awful.

beginner.m: An author is the creator of a work; a writer.
beginner.e: I am the author of this article. I was the one who wrote it.

beginner.m: A fact is a piece of information that is true.
beginner.e: That is not just my idea, it is a fact.

beginner.m: A goal is something you want to do or be able to do.
beginner.e: I want to go to university and this will help me achieve that goal.

beginner.m: A collection is a group of things of the same type. They are usually special in some way.
beginner.e: He has one of the biggest collections of paintings by Van Gogh.

beginner.m: If you study something, you make an effort to learn it.
beginner.e: We study math at the school.

beginner.m: Worry means to feel troubled by, anxious, or uneasy about specific problems or the possibility of unpleasant things happening in the future.
beginner.e: While she cooked the food, she worried about her son who was writing an important test at school.

beginner.m: A machine used to talk to someone who is far away.
beginner.e: I need to find a telephone so I can tell my mother where I am.

beginner.m: A restaurant is a place where you can buy and eat food and drinks.
beginner.e: My wife and I went out to a small French restaurant in Toronto for dinner.

beginner.m: If something is brilliant, it gives off a lot of light.
beginner.e: He noticed a brilliant star in the sky.

beginner.m: When something is acceptable it is capable of being accepted or is worth being accepted.
beginner.e: You ideas are acceptable to the group.

beginner.m: An error is something which is accidentally not correct.
beginner.e: The bank made an error and gave me too much money.

beginner.m: When you know something, you have facts or ideas in your mind.
beginner.e: I know a little Spanish.

beginner.m: A copy of something looks or acts like it.
beginner.e: They took the diamond and replaced it with a cheap copy.

beginner.m: An instrument is any thing people hold in their hand and use to do something.
beginner.e: A hammer is a heavy instrument.

beginner.m: A cupboard is a piece of furniture with shelves to hold dishes, towels, food, etc.
beginner.e: He took cups, plates and saucers from the kitchen cupboards and stacked them on the table.

beginner.m: If something is your fault, you did something wrong or didn't do something right.
beginner.e: It's clear that both sides are at fault.

beginner.m: An effect is something that is caused by something else.
beginner.e: The effect of the change was small.

beginner.m: A hole is an empty space in an object or material.
beginner.e: They dug a hole in the ground for the tree.

beginner.m: If something or someone is energetic, they show or involve great activity or vitality.
beginner.e: Cosmic rays are energetic particles from outer space.

beginner.m: If something is personal, that means it is tied to you.
beginner.e: Don't make personal remarks.

beginner.m: To talk about something.
beginner.e: They discussed the issue.

beginner.m: A lock is a metal thing on a door (or on a window, drawer, etc.) that stops people from opening the door unless they have the right key to open it.
beginner.e: No one will take things from my house. I have a very strong lock on the door.

beginner.m: If you give someone advice, you tell them what you think they should do.
beginner.e: Thanks so much! I took your advice and it really helped me get the job.

beginner.m: A feature is a special or noticeable part of something.
beginner.e: One unusual feature of the town is the river in the middle of mainstreet.

beginner.m: If you want to do something, you think you would be happier if you did it.
beginner.e: He wants to know her name.

beginner.m: Rugby is a football game played with an oval shaped ball. Players can hold or kick the ball.
beginner.e: He was picked to play rugby in the school team.

beginner.m: A chicken is a bird that farmers raise for meat and eggs.
beginner.e: My father went out back, caught a chicken, cut off its head, and cleaned it for dinner.

beginner.m: A model is a something that is made to look or act like something else, usually being smaller or simpler than the original.
beginner.e: The company builds and sells detailed 3-D models of the human body.

beginner.m: Quality is goodness.
beginner.e: This cloth is full of quality.

beginner.m: Someone who is visiting.
beginner.e: I had a lot of visitors when I was in the hospital.

beginner.m: A pass is a piece of paper, plastic, etc. that allows somebody to enter a building, vehicle, or area.
beginner.e: We have a season's pass for the ski hill.

beginner.m: A phone is a tool for speaking to people who are far away.
beginner.e: The phone's ringing. Can you answer it?

beginner.m: Having big muscles; physically powerful.
beginner.e: Arnold is very strong.

beginner.m: A soldier is someone who is part of an army.
beginner.e: The soldier was shot in the war.

beginner.m: A lesson is a time when something is taught.
beginner.e: The Math lesson starts at 5:12.

beginner.m: A girlfriend is a girl or young woman who is in a romantic relationship with another person.
beginner.e: Jeremy had been having trouble with his girlfriend.

beginner.m: A bathroom is a room that has a bathtub or a shower.
beginner.e: In our house, the bathroom is very busy in the morning.

beginner.m: Air is a mixture of gases. It has no color or odor (smell)
beginner.e: We breathe air to live.

beginner.m: A rating is where something is on a scale of quality, popularity, value, etc.
beginner.e: He had a poor credit rating.

beginner.m: Dear is something that is precious or greatly valued to someone. They love the thing or the person.
beginner.e: My large stamp collection is very dear to me.

beginner.m: A jet is a stream of gas or liquid forced through a small opening.
beginner.e: A jet of water burst through the broken pipe.

beginner.m: A ruler is a device used for measuring things.
beginner.e: The ruler says that the shelf is 12 centimeters wide.

beginner.m: Leisure is time that is free from work or other duties, when a person can relax and do what they enjoy.
beginner.e: He looked forward to the holidays when he could read at his leisure.

beginner.m: A man is a male human.
beginner.e: The old man smiled at the child.

beginner.m: Paper is a material for writing and drawing on and is made from wood pulp.
beginner.e: She made a paper airplane.

beginner.m: A request the act of asking for something (sometimes in a formal way).
beginner.e: We didn't hear his request that we be quiet.

beginner.m: A card is a small, often rectangular piece of paper or plastic, usually with information.
beginner.e: We spent the afternoon playing card games.

beginner.m: A knife is a tool that cuts.
beginner.e: He ate with his knife and fork.

beginner.m: Art is creation by means of an art. Common examples of art are paintings and photographs, but songs and even buildings can be art, too.
beginner.e: The gallery has many pieces of art.

beginner.m: A ship is a large boat.
beginner.e: We sailed by ship from England to Italy.

beginner.m: Scenery is what you see when you look at the outdoor environment around you. It is a word used to describe places.
beginner.e: The scenery on the island is beautiful.

beginner.m: Sunshine is the light, rays, or warmth of the Sun.
beginner.e: We got ourselves warm in the sunshine.

beginner.m: Someone is reading when they are looking at a book or other writing and understanding what it says.
beginner.e: Have you read this book?

beginner.m: If you quit something, you stop doing it; that is, you do not do it any more.
beginner.e: Please quit bothering me!

beginner.m: A subject is a branch of knowledge in school, college or university, such as English, math, science, and history.
beginner.e: The subject of the class is English literature.

beginner.m: A chain is a series of round pieces of material joined together to make a line.
beginner.e: He got her a gold chain necklace for her birthday.

beginner.m: Someone that is lively is full of life and energy.
beginner.e: She had a lively conversation with her new boyfriend.

beginner.m: A cooker is a stove, or a pot, used to cook food.
beginner.e: We bought a new gas cooker.

beginner.m: If something appears a certain way, it looks or seems that way.
beginner.e: The problems appear likely to continue.

beginner.m: The part of the face that sticks out and is used for breathing and smelling things.
beginner.e: His nose is very big.

beginner.m: If someone is given to doing something, they do it regularly.
beginner.e: My father's given to making long speeches about when he was a boy.

beginner.m: A deal is a business agreement.
beginner.e: The company made a deal with the agents.

beginner.m: Something that is key, is an important or a main thing.
beginner.e: Accuracy is a key part of playing music.

beginner.m: The amount of money you need to pay to buy something.
beginner.e: The price of this book is ten dollars.

beginner.m: If you do something easily, you have no trouble doing it.
beginner.e: They won the game easily, 6–0.

beginner.m: A passenger is a person who is riding a vehicle—not the driver.
beginner.e: Both passenger trains and freight trains use the same tracks.

beginner.m: Of or about chemicals.
beginner.e: This test can detect small changes in the chemical composition of water.

beginner.m: A planet is one of the 8 bodies that orbit the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
beginner.e: Our planet is named Earth.

beginner.m: A discussion happens when two or more people share ideas about something, usually by talking.
beginner.e: There have been ongoing discussions about the new rules.

beginner.m: If you invent something, you make or design a new kind of thing.
beginner.e: Thomas Edison invented the electric light bulb.

beginner.m: A vote is a formal way of choosing things that are controlled by the majority.
beginner.e: Let's take a vote for a new president!

beginner.m: A wooden object is made of wood.
beginner.e: Please do not spill your drink on the wooden floor.

beginner.m: A button is a round object that can be pushed through clothing so that the clothing stays on.
beginner.e: Sarah's sweater doesn't work anymore because the buttons popped off.

beginner.m: The center of something, is the place that is as far from its outside as possible.
beginner.e: The president and his problems continue to take center stage in the news.

beginner.m: A novel is a long story.
beginner.e: I wrote a novel last November for National Novel Writing Month.

beginner.m: Accident means something that happens without a plan; unintentionally; inadvertently.
beginner.e: I dropped the glass by accident and it broke.

beginner.m: The part of the year when the weather is hot.
beginner.e: There is no school in the summer.

beginner.m: An orphan is someone who does not have parents. That is, their mother and father are both dead. This is most often used for a child.
beginner.e: We could not have children, so we adopted an orphan.

beginner.m: A gate is like a door in a fence. It opens to let people go through the fence.
beginner.e: Please open the gate for me; my hands are full.

beginner.m: When two or more people are discussing an idea that they do not agree on, they are having an argument. Often arguments are loud or angry.
beginner.e: I thought we should buy the red car. She thought we should buy the blue car. We had an argument about it.

beginner.m: The floor is the flat part at the bottom of a room. People stand on the floor.
beginner.e: Don't drop your milk on the floor.

beginner.m: If something is cold, it is low in temperature.
beginner.e: The wind made her hands cold.

beginner.m: Blood is a red liquid inside a person or animal's body that carries nutrients and oxygen to the other parts of the body.
beginner.e: I'm taking medication for high blood pressure.

beginner.m: Credit is an agreement to buy something and pay later.
beginner.e: We bought the new dining room table on credit.

beginner.m: A sample is a small amount of something to try or test it.
beginner.e: The nurse took a small blood sample.

beginner.m: A kite is an object made of light material that can use the wind to fly. They are held by a long string.
beginner.e: We went to the beach to fly a kite this summer.

beginner.m: Oak is a type of tree or the wood from one
beginner.e: My favorite tree is that oak in the park.

beginner.m: If something is unknown, nobody knows it.
beginner.e: Nothing was written down, and it was a long time ago, so his true date of birth is unknown.

beginner.m: A violin is a musical instrument played by moving a bow across the strings.
beginner.e: He has played the violin from when he was 6 years old.

beginner.m: A simple task is easy to do and easy to understand.
beginner.e: Baking this cake is very simple as it only has 3 steps.

beginner.m: To be gray in color.
beginner.e: That is a gray whale.

beginner.m: A being refers to a living thing.
beginner.e: You are a human being.

beginner.m: Knowledge is information that you know.
beginner.e: He shared his knowledge with you.

beginner.m: Winter is the coldest season of the year. In northern countries, December, January and February are winter months.
beginner.e: We like to go to Mexico in the winter.

beginner.m: Soup is a food usually made by boiling meat and vegetables in water to give the water flavour.
beginner.e: You can try our wide variety of soups.

beginner.m: A physical thing or activity is related to the body, or something you can touch.
beginner.e: The war didn't leave him with any physical injuries, but his mind was badly damaged.

beginner.m: The source of some material, an idea, a product, etc. is the place it came from originally.
beginner.e: CO₂ is the main source of global warming.

beginner.m: If you manage something, you organise and control it.
beginner.e: The other two teams were managed by their local area directors.

beginner.m: A type of small animal with an external skeleton and six legs.
beginner.e: Crickets, ants, ladybugs, and flies are insects.

beginner.m: The final thing is the last one.
beginner.e: Today is the final day to register for university.

beginner.m: A saw is a tool with sharp teeth used to cut something hard like wood.
beginner.e: The man used a saw to cut the wood into pieces.

beginner.m: If something is sweet, it tastes like sugar or fruit.
beginner.e: This cake is very sweet. I think you put much sugar in it.

beginner.m: A pool is hole that holds water. Usually, it is for people to swim in.
beginner.e: Our hotel had a large indoor pool.

beginner.m: A rumor is a story about somebody or something, that is told by other people, most of the time it is not true.
beginner.e: There is a rumor going around that John's been fired. Is it true?

beginner.m: If you think that something is or may be true, you feel that it is or may be true.
beginner.e: I think he's a doctor.

beginner.m: A bush is a plant that is a short tree.
beginner.e: I grow a few bushes.

beginner.m: A supermarket is a big store that sells groceries, as well as other common household things like clothing.
beginner.e: I bought bread and milk from the supermarket.

beginner.m: A clock is an instrument that tells you what the time is. A small clock which you carry is called a watch.
beginner.e: He was sleepy, and the clock said 11:32.

beginner.m: A flood happens when there has been a lot of rain in a short time and the water covers the ground.
beginner.e: The storm brought heavy rains, and the resulting flood caused $14 million in damage to crops.

beginner.m: A waitress is a woman who serves at a restaurant; a female waiter.
beginner.e: I'm trying to get the waitress to bring our bill but she isn't looking this way.

beginner.m: The part of an object that makes it slow down.
beginner.e: The crash was caused by the car's brakes failing.

beginner.m: Happy, content, satisfied.
beginner.e: I'm so pleased you were able to make it to my show.

beginner.m: If you swallow something you make it go through your mouth into your body (down your esophagus to your stomach). We swallow food and drinks.
beginner.e: Young children put small toys in their mouths and sometimes swallow them.

beginner.m: Support is something that keeps something up.
beginner.e: The posts in the house help support the roof.

beginner.m: A feeling of sympathy at the distress or suffering of someone or something.
beginner.e: It's a pity her friend died.

beginner.m: An attempt to find something.
beginner.e: The search for the stolen jewelry was unsuccessful.

beginner.m: A celebration is a gathering of people for fun and entertainment, usually like a party.
beginner.e: We held a birthday celebration for Jane last Sunday.

beginner.m: If you refer to something, you talk or write about it, usually in passing.
beginner.e: He referred to her only by her first name.

beginner.m: A tube is a long object with a hole from one end to the other. The ends may be closed or open.
beginner.e: Toothpaste comes in a tube.

beginner.m: If a person or animal is fat, it is big and heavy because it has too much fat.
beginner.e: I got really fat when I was in university because I ate every meal at McDonalds.

beginner.m: To pollute means add dirt and other harmful things to water, land or air.
beginner.e: The industry pollutes the air in this region.

beginner.m: An account is an arrangement with a bank or other company to do business.
beginner.e: I opened a bank account when I moved into town.

beginner.m: When you are sure about something, you are certain.
beginner.e: The student was sure that his answer was correct.

beginner.m: A fortune is a very large amount of money.
beginner.e: A million dollars is a fortune.

beginner.m: A raised flat surface.
beginner.e: He sat at the table to eat.

beginner.m: A cup is deep round container open at the top, normally used to drink out of.
beginner.e: I'll bring you another cup of tea.

beginner.m: Very nearly; not the same, but near to being the same.
beginner.e: I am almost ready to go. I will be ready very soon.

beginner.m: The edge of an opening, especially, the human mouth (often plural).
beginner.e: John licked his lips.

beginner.m: Something is natural if people didn't make it.
beginner.e: Animals, plants and rocks are natural things.

beginner.m: Honey is a sweet, thick liquid that is made by bees. It is usually golden or brown.
beginner.e: Add some honey to make it taste good.

beginner.m: A meal is the food you eat at regular times of the day. Breakfast, lunch, supper and dinner, are meals.
beginner.e: Thanks for dinner! I haven't had a good Italian meal like that for a long time.

beginner.m: A slice is a piece of something that has been sliced.
beginner.e: I like to have my sandwich with a couple slices of ham it in.

beginner.m: A chef is a person who is paid to cook.
beginner.e: The restaurant had a really good chef.

beginner.m: A section of a thing or place is a part of it.
beginner.e: The police closed one section of the road because of the accident.

beginner.m: A mistake is something that is done wrong or is incorrect.
beginner.e: There were only two mistakes on my test.

beginner.m: A sum is an amount of money, usually a large amount.
beginner.e: The company had been spending large sums on publicity and advertising.

beginner.m: A style is a specific look, design, or way of dressing or acting.
beginner.e: I don't understand why the styles in fashion magazines are always changing.

beginner.m: A place which sells things.
beginner.e: He bought a hat from the shop.

beginner.m: A horse is a hoofed mammal. It walks on four (4) legs. People often ride on horses.
beginner.e: The horse likes to eat oats.

beginner.m: If something is bad, it is not good.
beginner.e: Skipping school is a bad thing to do.

beginner.m: When someone is making a promise to a person, he is saying what he plans to do for that person.
beginner.e: Jane was angry that John broke his promise to take her out to the movies.

beginner.m: A wheel is a round thing (circle) on a cart or carriage or train or other machine that moves. A cart has four wheels that touch the road and turn.
beginner.e: The cart needs a very smooth road because it has little wheels.

beginner.m: When you develop something, you create or make it better.
beginner.e: The people who are best at anything have to develop their ability over time.

beginner.m: The truth is an idea which is correct or accepted as correct.
beginner.e: Don't lie to me. Tell me the truth.

beginner.m: A greedy person is someone who wants money or other items for himself and does not like to share.
beginner.e: My aunt is greedy because she keeps talking about money.

beginner.m: You win when you do better than other people.
beginner.e: I will win the game.

beginner.m: A duck is a bird that swims and says "quack!". It has a flat bill and webbed feet.
beginner.e: We saw three ducks in the park lake.

beginner.m: A little coloured square of paper that someone sticks to a letter when they want to send the letter.
beginner.e: The stamp goes in the upper right part of the outside of the letter.

beginner.m: When more than 2 things or people are together, they make a group.
beginner.e: A group of people went into the building.

beginner.m: Something that is done a lot or happens a lot; something that is ordinary
beginner.e: These are my everyday clothes.

beginner.m: A report is a description of something that has happened.
beginner.e: There was a recent report on the election.

beginner.m: If something is electric, it uses electricity.
beginner.e: We bought a new gas stove. It's much faster than our old electric one.

beginner.m: If you forbid someone from doing something, you do not allow them to do it; you disallow it.
beginner.e: The teacher forbids you from eating or drinking during the class.

beginner.m: If you are lost you do not know where you are. You might not know how to get home.
beginner.e: I was lost in the woods for a week.

beginner.m: A semester is half of a school year.
beginner.e: This semester I will be taking four subjects.

beginner.m: Something made of cloth that covers a foot and is able to go inside a shoe.
beginner.e: These socks don't fit my feet.

beginner.m: A cat is a domestic animal often kept as a pet; it has whiskers and likes to chase mice.
beginner.e: Our pet cat has just had kittens.

beginner.m: A map is an image of a place, usually with place names written in.
beginner.e: I've got a good street map of London.

beginner.m: Beauty is the quality of being nice to look at.
beginner.e: Beauty makes things attractive.

beginner.m: An event is anything that happens.
beginner.e: In the event that the machine breaks, read this to know what to do.

beginner.m: A sale is the act of selling something.
beginner.e: The president said the company is not for sale.

beginner.m: A job is an activity that you do, usually, regularly and for pay.
beginner.e: She got a good job as a manager in a book store.

beginner.m: The temperature of something is how hot or cold it is.
beginner.e: Today's temperature is 25°C.

beginner.m: A machine is a man-made object with moving parts.
beginner.e: This new machine is the fastest computer I've ever had.

beginner.m: The shape of a thing is its external form.
beginner.e: The cake was made into the shape of a car.

beginner.m: A family is a group of people with a blood or marriage relation.
beginner.e: My parents and my two brothers are my family.

beginner.m: A glove is a piece of clothing you wear on your hand to keep your hands warm or safe.
beginner.e: John is wearing gloves today because it's -5°C.

beginner.m: If someone or something is cute, it is attractive or pretty.
beginner.e: Baby cats are so cute.

beginner.m: A forest is an area covered with many trees, and sometimes by bushes and other plants.
beginner.e: Certain forests are so vast that people can easily be lost there.

beginner.m: A ride is a journey you take by riding.
beginner.e: It was a long ride from Canada to Mexico.

beginner.m: A track is a line on the ground or in space that people, animals or vehicles follow.
beginner.e: I raced on a 250-meter track in Call and won.

beginner.m: When things grow they get bigger or change in other ways over time.
beginner.e: Every day I grow better and better.

beginner.m: If you advise someone to do something, you tell them that they should do it.
beginner.e: I'd advise you to study for the exam.

beginner.m: Camping is the recreational activity of temporarily living in a tent.
beginner.e: Camping is a favorite summer activity.

beginner.m: A coin is money made of metal.
beginner.e: The United States makes several different coins including the penny, nickel, dime, and quarter.

beginner.m: If x is tight, it fits closely and strongly to y.
beginner.e: The police kept tight control during the speech.

beginner.m: A single thing is the only one.
beginner.e: In large baking dish, arrange chicken pieces in single layer.

beginner.m: Tennis is a sport where players use a racquet to hit a ball over a net. It can be played by two or four people.
beginner.e: The four girls spent the afternoon playing tennis.

beginner.m: A bloom is a flower.
beginner.e: The seeds you plant in the spring will give blooms from summer through fall.

beginner.m: You use usually to talk about what happens most of the time.
beginner.e: Usually they come by car so I don't think they'll walk.

beginner.m: A date is a particular day in a month or year.
beginner.e: Please write your birth date here.

beginner.m: A normal thing, or situation, is one that is not special.
beginner.e: A normal computer has a keyboard and a screen.

beginner.m: A picture is marks on a flat object, like paper, that show shapes, people, or things.
beginner.e: Mommy, I drew a picture of a cat.

beginner.m: A direction is a way to move or point.
beginner.e: Which direction is north?

beginner.m: Very, Really
beginner.e: That movie was quite good.

beginner.m: A house is a building that one family lives in.
beginner.e: The president lives in a house in Washington, called The White House.

beginner.m: If something changes greatly, the change is very big.
beginner.e: Expenses greatly exceeded revenues this year.

beginner.m: The structure of something is the way that it is put together.
beginner.e: The structure of her writing makes it very easy to understand.

beginner.m: Convenience is the quality of being easy to get and use.
beginner.e: The shop has a free car park for the convenience of its guests.

beginner.m: If x belongs to y, it is y's
beginner.e: The umbrella belongs to John; it's his.

beginner.m: A consequence is a result of an action, decision, etc., often a bad result.
beginner.e: The consequences of lying to your parents are usually bad.

beginner.m: If someone or something is ugly, it's not nice to look at.
beginner.e: Hughie had the same ugly face as his father and brother.

beginner.m: A way is how someone does something.
beginner.e: I do things my own way.

beginner.m: If A consists of B, then B is the thing or things that, together, make A.
beginner.e: His letter consisted of only three words.

beginner.m: If a person destroys something, they break it or make it not exist anymore.
beginner.e: The house was destroyed by the bomb.

beginner.m: A side is a straight edge of an object.
beginner.e: A square has four sides.

beginner.m: Colored orange
beginner.e: The construction workers wear orange shirts so that drivers can easily see them.

beginner.m: An object that takes pictures digitally or on film.
beginner.e: I took a picture of the mountain with my camera.

beginner.m: A sheep is an animal that people keep on farms and eat for food.
beginner.e: My grandfather has a sheep farm and we get all our wool there.

beginner.m: Something that is hot is high in temperature.
beginner.e: The sun is very hot.

beginner.m: If you build something, you make it out of pieces of other things.
beginner.e: It's not easy to find the people who build bombs.

beginner.m: To speak; any sound from a person's mouth.
beginner.e: He talks with him daily.

beginner.m: Flight is the act of flying: moving through the air using wings.
beginner.e: The flight of the bird was beautiful.

beginner.m: When the sky is cloudy, it is covered with clouds.
beginner.e: The sky quickly became cloudy and it started to rain.

beginner.m: The coast is the area of land closest to the sea.
beginner.e: The hotel was near the coast and their room had a balcony from which they could see the distant ocean.

beginner.m: Cream is the fatty part of milk.
beginner.e: Would you like some cream in your coffee?

beginner.m: If you explain something, you talk about it so that somebody can understand it.
beginner.e: He explained the difference between the two.

beginner.m: The comparative form of good; more good.
beginner.e: I am a better person than you are.

beginner.m: To represent is to stand in the place of; to act the part of (another).
beginner.e: A member of Congress represents his district in Congress.

beginner.m: If you click on something, you use a computer mouse and push a button.
beginner.e: The computer wants me to click this button.

beginner.m: A piece of cloth with which a person covers themselves.
beginner.e: The girl was covered with a blanket by her mother when she went to bed.

beginner.m: A female human.
beginner.e: My wife is a good woman.

beginner.m: Beans are the seeds of one family of plants that people often cook and eat.
beginner.e: Put the dried beans in water overnight. They should be soft and ready to cook in the morning.

beginner.m: Your brain is the part of your body that is inside your head.
beginner.e: He has serious brain damage from falling off of his bicycle and hitting his head.

beginner.m: If you write a book, an article, a computer program, a piece of music, etc., you create it.
beginner.e: My dream is to write a children's book.

beginner.m: If you are awake, you are not asleep.
beginner.e: It was 1:00 AM and Gerard was still awake.

beginner.m: Sport is physical exercise which involves players playing in a team.
beginner.e: What sport shall we play?

beginner.m: A headphone is a very little machine near a person's ear that makes sound.
beginner.e: The music on the person's headphones was so loud that he didn't know I was talking to him.

beginner.m: Having the largest amount of a characteristic in a group.
beginner.e: Tony is the most successful.

beginner.m: The population of a place is the people or animals that live there.
beginner.e: The population of a city is higher than that of a town.

beginner.m: Your eyes are the part of your head which you see with.
beginner.e: We saw the eyes of a big wolf.

beginner.m: A gas is a substance, such as air, that is not liquid or solid.
beginner.e: The sun is a giant ball of gas.

beginner.m: If you encourage someone, you make them feel that they want to, or can, do something.
beginner.e: I encouraged my son to audition for the school play.

beginner.m: An action is something that you do, or something that happens, especially with motion.
beginner.e: There was a huge difference between my thoughts and my actions.

beginner.m: A file is a set of papers or records on a specific issue, person, etc.
beginner.e: The letter should be in the file on the Herzog problem.

beginner.m: If a person or situation is confused, things are unclear or you do not understand.
beginner.e: The book is terrible. It's full of bad writing and confused examples.

beginner.m: A market is a place where many people come to buy and sell things.
beginner.e: It's time to take the cows to the market.

beginner.m: Labor is the work that people do, usually lifting, moving, building, etc. rather than desk work.
beginner.e: The cost of labor is higher than the cost of building materials.

beginner.m: A journey is a long trip.
beginner.e: Timothy left on a long journey.

beginner.m: To say a good word after someone gives something to you or after someone does something good for you.
beginner.e: She thanked him very much for the beautiful food he cooked for her.

beginner.m: Shampoo is liquid soap used for washing hair.
beginner.e: My favorite shampoo was on sale for half price at the store, so I bought a few bottles.

beginner.m: Clothes, such as shirts, pants, socks, etc. are things that people wear on their body to cover it.
beginner.e: He took off his clothes and got into the shower.

beginner.m: When you are good, you do the right things. That is, you do things that are kind or helpful. You do not do things that hurt people or are not honest.
beginner.e: He is a good person and would never steal.

beginner.m: A wave is the motion of water up and down.
beginner.e: The wind blew strongly on the water and made high waves.

beginner.m: Before a certain time (often now)
beginner.e: When we met, his first wife was already dead.

beginner.m: An interest is when a person wants to know more about someone or something or likes someone or something or likes to do something.
beginner.e: What are your interests?

beginner.m: A mammal with long ears.
beginner.e: Our pet rabbit liked vegetables and could run very fast.

beginner.m: Order is when things are where they should be.
beginner.e: I need to take some time to put my things in order.

beginner.m: A path is a way to get to a place. It is like a small road, often made of dirt.
beginner.e: That path leads into the woods.

beginner.m: An adult is a person who is of the legal age of majority.
beginner.e: Adult usually means a person who is in a legal sense either age 18 years or older.

beginner.m: Sick, not well. If you are ill, you have bad health, you might have a disease.
beginner.e: One boy died and the other is seriously ill in the hospital.

beginner.m: If it is rainy, it is a wet day with rain.
beginner.e: It was a rainy day, so he stayed inside where it was warm and dry.

beginner.m: An explanation is the words used to tell somebody how to do something or the reason for something.
beginner.e: The explanation was long and drawn-out.

beginner.m: Someone whose job is to raise animals or plants, often for food.
beginner.e: The farmers here plant crops to feed their families and to make a profit.

beginner.m: A feeling of wanting something that someone else has.
beginner.e: I could feel my envy growing as I watched him play with his children.

beginner.m: A thing that is yellow in color.
beginner.e: The yellow car moves fast.

beginner.m: If something is dark, is has no light.
beginner.e: The cave is very dark.

beginner.m: The background is what can be seen or heard behind other things that are closer or louder.
beginner.e: I was talking to Mary, but I heard the phone ringing in the background.

beginner.m: North is the direction towards the top of the Earth, opposite to south; If you are looking north, the sun sets on your left.
beginner.e: Canada is the biggest country in North America.

beginner.m: If you feel lonely, you feel sad because you are alone.
beginner.e: She was bored and lonely without her friends.

beginner.m: The ankle is the joint between the foot and the leg.
beginner.e: She sprained her ankle when she fell on the ice.

beginner.m: Metal is a hard material, often shiny and easy to conduct electricity. Gold, silver, and steel are examples of metals.
beginner.e: We replaced out our wood door with a stronger metal one.

beginner.m: An answer is something that someone says after another person asks (says) a question.
beginner.e: The answer to your question is "no".

beginner.m: A part of the head (or face) used for hearing.
beginner.e: My rabbit has two big ears.

beginner.m: Sounds that are played on musical instruments or sung with a certain rhythm and harmony, and forming melodies.
beginner.e: You cannot make any music with this trumpet, it is broken.

beginner.m: A chart is information that is organised in rows and columns or as a picture.
beginner.e: This week's bar chart shows the correct figures.

beginner.m: If something never happens, it does not happen at any time.
beginner.e: As a child I was told that I should never tell a lie.

beginner.m: If you are lucky, you have a lot of luck.
beginner.e: After getting married and winning $1 million on the same day, Susan felt very lucky.

beginner.m: An event is late if it happens after a specified time.
beginner.e: He was late to his appointment.

beginner.m: A list is a group of related words, often in some order, often to help you remember something.
beginner.e: Did you call everyone on the phone list?

beginner.m: A long vehicle with many cars that are joined together. A train runs on a track.
beginner.e: I took the train from Paris to Frankfurt.

beginner.m: A brand is a red-hot piece of wood in a fire.
beginner.e: Don't touch that brand!

beginner.m: The weather in a place is the air temperature, the number of clouds, and the amount of wind and rain or snow.
beginner.e: The radio says the hot summer weather is going to continue for a few more days.

beginner.m: A folder holds papers, usually with an writing on the top to show what is inside it.
beginner.e: I keep all my schoolwork in a yellow folder.

beginner.m: If something is done perfectly, it is done without mistake.
beginner.e: The car is perfectly aligned in the lot.

beginner.m: If you retire, you stop working, usually because of your age.
beginner.e: She recently retired after 25 years with the company.

beginner.m: A polite way of saying "woman".
beginner.e: Please direct this lady to the soft furnishings department.

beginner.m: Very old, usually hundreds or thousands or millions of years old.
beginner.e: He studied the ancient world.

beginner.m: A drama is a serious story for TV, stage, radio, etc.
beginner.e: The courtroom drama stars Melissa Gilbert as a young lawyer.

beginner.m: If food is off, it is not good to eat anymore.
beginner.e: The meat smells off.

beginner.m: Breakfast is the first meal that we eat in the morning.
beginner.e: I'm late for school. I don't have time for breakfast today.

beginner.m: A hard object that can be found on beaches.
beginner.e: I have a collection of colorful shells at home which I have collected when I visit the beach.

beginner.m: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it doesn't exist at all.
beginner.e: There's no lack of beaches in Hawai'i.

beginner.m: Just one or just a few; this and no other; no more than this.
beginner.e: These are the only coins I have.

beginner.m: A store is a building with many things in it, where people can exchange money for things.
beginner.e: He went to the store to get some milk.

beginner.m: If a person or animal dies, it stops living.
beginner.e: She died from illness.

beginner.m: When something is basic, it is simple.
beginner.e: Everyone in the army has to have basic training.

beginner.m: If an animal or plant is wild it is not tame. This means it lives in nature and people have not changed it.
beginner.e: Wolves and bears are wild animals.

beginner.m: When something moves slowly or does something slowly, it takes a very long time to do it.
beginner.e: He moved slowly, hoping that the bird wouldn't notice him.

beginner.m: A school is a place where you go to learn.
beginner.e: What grade are you in at school?

beginner.m: Something good or lucky happened.
beginner.e: Fortunately, I found my lost keys in the living room.

beginner.m: A pair is two things that go together.
beginner.e: Those two make a lovely pair, don't they.

beginner.m: Having a hole or opening, not closed.
beginner.e: The door was open.

beginner.m: A cinema is a building that shows movies.
beginner.e: The cinema in my town has two screens and has four showings every day.

beginner.m: The father of a person is the man who is one of that person's parents.
beginner.e: The father of Bill Smith IV is Bill Smith III.

beginner.m: Something done, a deed.
beginner.e: Going into the house on fire to help a child was a brave act.

beginner.m: The comparative form of bad; more bad.
beginner.e: The weather this winter is worse than last year.

beginner.m: When someone is teenage, that person is older than twelve years old, but younger than twenty years old.
beginner.e: During my teenage years, I had to fight for my own survival, as it was during the Great Depression.

beginner.m: A cap is a small hat.
beginner.e: He was wearing blue jeans and a ball cap.

beginner.m: A hit using the foot.
beginner.e: I gave the door a kick.

beginner.m: Somebody's return is when they come back.
beginner.e: They've planned a celebration for my return home.

beginner.m: If something is warm, it is a nice temperature between cool and hot.
beginner.e: She washed her face in the warm water.

beginner.m: The tip of something is the farthest point of it.
beginner.e: He followed the line on the map with his finger tip.

beginner.m: A village is a very small town.
beginner.e: He lives in a village in the middle of nowhere.

beginner.m: If something is deeply rooted, felt, held, etc., it is done to a deep extent or degree.
beginner.e: I deeply regret my behaviour.

beginner.m: If you are bored, you have nothing to do or there is nothing interesting.
beginner.e: I just get bored with doing the same thing over and over.

beginner.m: When a person or animal is social, it lives with others.
beginner.e: Dogs are social animals.

beginner.m: Plenty of something is a lot of it; more than enough of it.
beginner.e: Here! Take some more; there's plenty here.

beginner.m: Cash is money in the form of bills and coins, rather than checks/cheques or credit cards.
beginner.e: Payment is by cash, VISA, or MasterCard.

beginner.m: A program is a number of steps that are followed to reach a goal or end.
beginner.e: His new exercise program gets more difficult every week.

beginner.m: A prince is the son of the king and queen in a country, and brother of the princess. The prince can also be the husband of a princess.
beginner.e: Our great-great-great-great-grandfather is a prince.

beginner.m: If something is marvelous, it is extremely good or wonderful.
beginner.e: The play was marvelous; everyone cheered at the end.

beginner.m: If something is wet it has some water or other liquid on it.
beginner.e: I got completely wet in the rain.

beginner.m: A clerk is a person who keeps an organization's records.
beginner.e: I called the city clerk's office to see if they had a record of her birth.

beginner.m: Very quick; taking no time or almost no time, and being a surprise.
beginner.e: The car crash was very sudden.

beginner.m: A movie is a motion picture that tells a story and is shown on a screen or television.
beginner.e: That was a really good movie as the story was interesting.

beginner.m: A gas or liquid, normally water, which has been frozen (made solid)
beginner.e: Ice is the solid state of water.

beginner.m: Tomorrow is day after today.
beginner.e: Tomorrow is my day off.

beginner.m: You use basically to emphasize that what you are saying covers the most important parts of a topic, even if it's not 100% correct.
beginner.e: We can talk about the details later, but basically, I need you here every day at 9:00.

beginner.m: If something is your own it belongs to you or is about you (often used for emphasis).
beginner.e: I wish I had my own home.

beginner.m: A purpose is reason for doing something or for existing.
beginner.e: The main purpose of the visit was to see the new building.

beginner.m: To be alive; to have life.
beginner.e: He's not expected to live for more than a few months.

beginner.m: A period is a length of time.
beginner.e: During the first period, Germany scored two goals.

beginner.m: If you celebrate something, you do something special to show that you are happy about it.
beginner.e: Fans poured into the streets to celebrate after their team's victory.

beginner.m: Your self is the type of person you are, particularly the way you usually act, look or feel.
beginner.e: He looked so happy compared to his usual down self that Walter wondered if something was wrong.

beginner.m: A grade is a letter or number that you use to show how good something is. Usually, teachers use it to show how good a student's test or assignment is.
beginner.e: Our restaurant uses only the highest grade of meat.

beginner.m: An exam is a formal test, usually important and often at the end of a course.
beginner.e: Did you pass the English exam last week?

beginner.m: If two people are close, they have a good relationship, like friends, family or lovers.
beginner.e: She was quite close to her dad before he died.

beginner.m: Life is what makes a person, animal or plant grow and function.
beginner.e: Scientists want to learn if there is life on other planets.

beginner.m: An object that is used to hold or carry things inside it.
beginner.e: They put their cards in containers.

beginner.m: Something that is perfect has no mistakes, problems, or damage.
beginner.e: She answered him in perfect Japanese.

beginner.m: The chin is the lowest part of the face. It is the point of the jaw and the part of the face where beards grow.
beginner.e: My chin is below my mouth.

beginner.m: A pocket is a small empty space, usually in your clothes, usually to carry things in.
beginner.e: My cell phone is in the outside pocket of my bag.

beginner.m: If you eat something, usually food, you put it in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.
beginner.e: I always eat too much good when it's Thanksgiving.

beginner.m: An anniversary is a day that is an exact number of years since a special event.
beginner.e: Today is our tenth wedding anniversary.

beginner.m: If you rob something or someone, you steal from them.
beginner.e: He went to rob the bank.

beginner.m: Corn is a kind of grain, usually with large yellow seeds, that is often eaten (also called maize).
beginner.e: We will be eating corn tomorrow.

beginner.m: A bit is an amount, usually a small amount.
beginner.e: I see him quite a bit.

beginner.m: If something is free, it does not cost money to buy.
beginner.e: This loaf of bread is free. It costs $0.

beginner.m: If you are amused, you are entertained.
beginner.e: The children played a game while their amused parents watched.

beginner.m: If the first thing occurs after the second, thing the first thing follows a second thing.
beginner.e: Every year summer always follows spring.

beginner.m: If something happens, it starts or changes without a plan.
beginner.e: It may happen to rain today.

beginner.m: A gram is a basic measure of weight.
beginner.e: This food has 1 gram of sugar.

beginner.m: Training is the process of improving at or learning to do some task.
beginner.e: Did you learn much at the computer training yesterday?

beginner.m: If two things are opposite, they are the same kind but completely different from each other.
beginner.e: I don't think we can work together. We're too opposite.

beginner.m: A lamp is something that makes light (either from electricity or by burning fuel).
beginner.e: Oil lamps have wicks that can smoke as they burn.

beginner.m: Grace is free giving.
beginner.e: We were saved by the grace of God.

beginner.m: When you hide something, you put it where others will not find it.
beginner.e: I hide candy to keep it from my brother.

beginner.m: If you collect some things, you bring them together as a group.
beginner.e: The rain collected in a pool.

beginner.m: Period from dusk to midnight.
beginner.e: We eat a big meal in the evening.

beginner.m: A worker is a person who works, usually for money.
beginner.e: The workers are putting a new roof on the house.

beginner.m: If someone is mad, they are angry.
beginner.e: I am so mad at you for ruining my painting.

beginner.m: Extremely means to a very high degree.
beginner.e: It is extremely difficult to climb Mount Everest without oxygen tanks.

beginner.m: Joy is a feeling of great happiness and pleasure.
beginner.e: They will be a source of strength and joy in your life.

beginner.m: An armchair is a big comfortable chair which has a support on each side for your arms.
beginner.e: She was sitting in an armchair with blankets wrapped round her.

beginner.m: Frighten means a person or thing that makes someone feel afraid; to cause someone to have a fear.
beginner.e: You are shouting at me and frightening your daughters.

beginner.m: If something is big, it is large in size; tall, wide, long, or fat.
beginner.e: I would like a big glass of milk.

beginner.m: Lemonade is a cold drink made of lemons, water, and a lot of sugar.
beginner.e: I would like a cool glass of lemonade.

beginner.m: An expert is a person who knows more, or can do something better, than most people, usually because of special study or practice.
beginner.e: Zidane is an expert at penalty kicks.

beginner.m: If something disappears, it becomes impossible to see.
beginner.e: The boat disappeared beneath the waves.

beginner.m: To help someone learn something. To tell someone how to do something.
beginner.e: Mr. Smith teaches grade-five English and history.

beginner.m: A kit is a collection of tools.
beginner.e: Bill has a kit to fix toy cars.

beginner.m: A cookie is a small baked cake. It is usually round and flat. Cookies are sweet.
beginner.e: When I want to have something sweet, I'll usually eat a cookie.

beginner.m: A factory is a building where lots of things are made.
beginner.e: This factory makes one hundred cars every day.

beginner.m: Intelligence is the ability to think clearly and understand easily.
beginner.e: The school has special classes for student of low intelligence.

beginner.m: A bell is an object that is shaped like a cup that makes a ringing sound when hit.
beginner.e: The church bell is ringing.

beginner.m: The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes.
beginner.e: Your cheeks are really rosy today.

beginner.m: Tape is a long thin material, often with glue on one side or used for recording.
beginner.e: The band put three songs on tape.

beginner.m: If someone joins two or more things, they bring them together.
beginner.e: Their lives were joined.

beginner.m: A tiger is a mammal. It comes from Asia.
beginner.e: I'm going to take the kids to the zoo to see a tiger.

beginner.m: A wheelchair is a chair with large wheels that is used by a sick or disabled person.
beginner.e: He broke both of his legs while skiing so he'll be in a wheelchair for the next few months.

beginner.m: Something that is remote is a long way off, distant, not near anything.
beginner.e: She walked to a remote corner of the farm, so she could be alone.

beginner.m: A spoon is a little, long, thin, metal thing with a round end for putting food in one's mouth.
beginner.e: Put a knife, a fork and a spoon near the plate on the table.

beginner.m: Several people can get a share of something if they divide it between them.
beginner.e: I will give you a share of this big bag of candy.

beginner.m: A schedule is a plan of things that are happening and the times when they happen.
beginner.e: The train is right on schedule.

beginner.m: Hair is long, very thin, soft material that grows on people and animals.
beginner.e: She had never seen him with his hair cut short.

beginner.m: A spell is an amount of time.
beginner.e: He stayed in his house for quite a spell.

beginner.m: A snack is a small amount of food or a small meal.
beginner.e: The snacks I ate were potato chips and candy.

beginner.m: A camp is a place, usually outside of cities, where people stay for a short time.
beginner.e: I don't think I can walk anymore today. Let's set up camp for the night.

beginner.m: Laws are the official rules of a government or organisation.
beginner.e: The Kyoto treaty became law in 2005.

beginner.m: Making firm rules.

beginner.e: It was unfair for the boss to give larger bonuses to his friends.

beginner.m: If you satisfy something, you fulfill it or meet its needs.
beginner.e: Will the results of the investigation satisfy you?

beginner.m: If you save something, you keep it; you do not give it or toss it away.
beginner.e: Please save that book for me.

beginner.m: Mail is the messages and packages that you send to other people.
beginner.e: The new book arrived in the mail.

beginner.m: A channel of water.
beginner.e: The river bends there.

beginner.m: A measure of time, approximately equal to the time taken for the moon to circle the earth.
beginner.e: There are 12 months in one year.

beginner.m: A lead is a wire or strap attached to something.
beginner.e: Attach this lead to one end of the battery.

beginner.m: Peace is the way a country is when there is no war.
beginner.e: The people lived in peace for thirty years.

beginner.m: A flat thing with a few words or pictures on it to tell people something.
beginner.e: I saw a stop sign, so I stopped the car.

beginner.m: Something that is official is approved by some authority.
beginner.e: The letter was an official document from the president.

beginner.m: We measure an angle using degrees. All the way around a circle is 360 degrees. Often, ° is written instead of "degrees".
beginner.e: A right-angled triangle has an angle of 90 degrees.

beginner.m: If something is familiar, you already know it or about it.
beginner.e: New a month ago, he's become quite familiar to all of us.

beginner.m: The direction that the sun sets; from north, 90º to the left.
beginner.e: He is from the west.

beginner.m: A reunion is the act of coming back together.
beginner.e: It was a happy reunion when the trapped miners finally saw their family again.

beginner.m: Chocolate is a candy made from cacao beans and often used to flavour other foods such as cakes and cookies.
beginner.e: In my opinion, the best cookies are those that contain chocolate.

beginner.m: Something that is usual happens often
beginner.e: It is usual for me to read the newspaper in the morning.

beginner.m: A towel is a large, soft piece of cloth that people use for drying themselves after they have a bath, or for drying dishes after they are washed.
beginner.e: I want to have a shower, but there are no clean towels!

beginner.m: An award is something that you give to someone who has done something very well.
beginner.e: He won the National League's Most Valuable Player award in 2007.

beginner.m: A scientist is a person who studies science.
beginner.e: The scientist looked at the Petri dish under a microscope.

beginner.m: A company is an organization for doing work for money.
beginner.e: He works for a big company.

beginner.m: One of the two directions, the opposite of right. This arrow is pointing left: ←
beginner.e: Turn left at the next corner.

beginner.m: Someone's character is the combination of things that they do, feel, and believe that makes them a certain type of person.
beginner.e: He's got a really funny character.

beginner.m: A sport where you try to hit a ball so that you can run to four bases, causing a run. The team with the most runs after nine or more innings wins.
beginner.e: The New York Yankees are a baseball team.

beginner.m: The parents of a person or animal are its father and mother.
beginner.e: Children may only enter the pool with a parent or guardian.

beginner.m: A medal is flat and usually round metal thing that you take as an award (if you did something brave).
beginner.e: He got a medal from serving in the army.

beginner.m: A shake is a type of beverage.
beginner.e: They were known for their shakes.

beginner.m: The act of traveling.
beginner.e: Astronauts do space travel.

beginner.m: A pile is a lot of things with some on the bottom and more on top.
beginner.e: He found his phone under a pile of clothes.

beginner.m: If something is thin, there's a short distance from one side to the other.
beginner.e: The man was very tall and thin as a stick.

beginner.m: Weak is used to describe something that does not have a lot of strength.
beginner.e: The child was too weak to move the boulder.

beginner.m: If something is appropriate, it matches the situation.
beginner.e: It is the job of management to look at the problems and take appropriate action.

beginner.m: A ray is a line of light or energy, coming out from where it starts.
beginner.e: Some rays of light from the sun shone between the leaves of the tree and lighted the top of his head.

beginner.m: A tradition is something that has been done in the same way for a long time.
beginner.e: Tradition says that we need a drink before the speech.

beginner.m: Someone looks at something when they move their head or move their eyes so that they can see the thing.
beginner.e: Look at this picture! Isn't it beautiful?

beginner.m: If something is still, it is not moving and resting in one place.
beginner.e: Sit still when you are in school.

beginner.m: A person that is clever is able to think quickly and sharply.
beginner.e: He is a very clever salesman. He almost got me into buying his product.

beginner.m: A roll is something round that was made by rolling.
beginner.e: The cloth in the store is in big rolls.

beginner.m: A pizza is a baked Italian food made of rolled bread dough crust, generally topped with tomato sauce, cheese and other ingredients.
beginner.e: I bought some pizza from a nearby Italian restaurant for the party.

beginner.m: A comparative is a form of a comparable adjective. You use it to show that something is "more big", "more good", etc.
beginner.e: My students always forget the -er in comparatives.

beginner.m: A state is a condition or a situation.
beginner.e: I am worried about her. She is in a constant state of depression.

beginner.m: If you sleep, you rest quietly with eyes shut, usually in bed for many hours at night.
beginner.e: I need to sleep now because I'm tired.

beginner.m: Something that is green in color.
beginner.e: The grass is green.

beginner.m: A girl is a female child or teenager; someone who is not a woman yet.
beginner.e: Many girls like to play with dolls.

beginner.m: Not much, very little.
beginner.e: I hardly noticed the pain.

beginner.m: The set is the scenery for a theatrical work such as a play, ballet, musical, etc.
beginner.e: The Metropolitan Opera's set for Aida is spectacular.

beginner.m: A group of people that come together to do something or decide something.
beginner.e: He is on the administrative committee. They decide how to administer the school.

beginner.m: If you describe something, you say what it looks like, sounds like, acts like, etc.
beginner.e: The hospital described her condition as serious.

beginner.m: An interview is when questions are asked formally.
beginner.e: I need an interview was a celebrity.

beginner.m: If you fill something, you put something in it until there is no space left.
beginner.e: She filled the car up with gas.

beginner.m: Something that is correct has no mistakes.
beginner.e: For question #5, only 5 people got the correct answer.

beginner.m: A fever is when you are hot because you are sick and your temperature will be higher than normal.
beginner.e: I took some medicine to lower my fever.

beginner.m: If x becomes y, it changes into y or changes to be more y.
beginner.e: The boy has become a man.

beginner.m: A pal is a friend of yours.
beginner.e: He has a pen pal that he often writes to.

beginner.m: A circle (●) is a round shape.
beginner.e: The dog was running in circles.

beginner.m: If you reveal something, it was hidden and you show it or make it known.
beginner.e: It was revealed yesterday that the president has decided to step down.

beginner.m: When you consider something you think carefully about it.
beginner.e: I will take time to consider what you said.

beginner.m: A sweetheart is someone you love in a romantic way.
beginner.e: My sweetheart gave me a box of candy on Valentine's Day.

beginner.m: A walk is what we do when we go on foot.
beginner.e: Are you taking the dog for a walk?

beginner.m: A secretary is a person who works in an office, helping with typing letters, filing, and other simple tasks.
beginner.e: I will ask my secretary to write to them.

beginner.m: If you sing you use your voice to make music.
beginner.e: I'm going to sing a song to you.

beginner.m: When you shoot, you use a weapon to throw something at a very fast speed at someone or something.
beginner.e: The man, in a desperate bid for freedom, grabbed his gun and started shooting anyone he could.

beginner.m: A way to apply something; an application.
beginner.e: They put it to good use.

beginner.m: You use truly before an adjective to emphasize that something it has all the characteristics of that adjective.
beginner.e: This has become a truly global business.

beginner.m: An officer is a person in an army who has much authority. A general and a captain are two types of officers.
beginner.e: A soldier must obey his commanding officer.

beginner.m: Interesting means to cause a person to want to know more about someone or something or to like someone or something or to like doing something.
beginner.e: That was a really interesting movie.

beginner.m: A scarf is a long item of clothing to wrap around the neck.
beginner.e: Wear a scarf, it is cold outside.

beginner.m: If you wait for someone or something, you do something (or nothing) until something else happens.
beginner.e: The fans waited patiently for their idol to arrive.

beginner.m: If you repeat something, you do it again.
beginner.e: I don't want to have to repeat typing this.

beginner.m: A detail is a small part of something that is not as important as the whole thing.
beginner.e: This is a very clear picture. You can see every detail.

beginner.m: The soft part of the body below the chest.
beginner.e: He got punched in the belly.

beginner.m: If you borrow something from someone, you use it and then you give it back to them.
beginner.e: Can I borrow your car and show my dad I can drive?

beginner.m: A fool is a person who does or thinks stupid things.
beginner.e: I made a fool of myself by forgetting her birthday.

beginner.m: Written characters (letters).
beginner.e: Russian language uses Greek script fonts.

beginner.m: If something does not happen anymore, it happened in the past, but has stopped happening.
beginner.e: I'm not sick anymore. I got better last night.

beginner.m: A circle.
beginner.e: The students sat in a ring.

beginner.m: Beef is the meat of a cow.
beginner.e: We're having ground beef for dinner.

beginner.m: If a person is excited, he or she is very enthusiastic.
beginner.e: He was very excited about his promotion.

beginner.m: A timetable is a kind of schedule with times of when the events are going to happen, usually used by schools to schedule lesson times.
beginner.e: Check the timetable to know what the next lesson is.

beginner.m: If something is helpful it can or does help in some way.
beginner.e: The way you explained that word was very helpful to me.

beginner.m: When you just do something, you only did that thing.
beginner.e: He was hungry, and he just wanted a good meal.

beginner.m: A thing that surprises someone, mostly something good.
beginner.e: The number of apples on the tree this year is a surprise.

beginner.m: Your hands are the parts of your body at the end of your arms. A hand has four fingers and a thumb.
beginner.e: Mother, I'm afraid, please hold my hand.

beginner.m: A clear idea is an idea that is easy to understand.
beginner.e: OK, so you need the key. I see. That's clear now.

beginner.m: If something is special, it is not usual; it is different or important in some way.
beginner.e: She is the most special person in my life.

beginner.m: An expression is a way your face can look that shows how you feel. Smiles and frowns are expressions.
beginner.e: I could tell he was lying by the expression on his face.

beginner.m: Something is local if it comes from a specific place. It often it means a place near the person who is speaking.
beginner.e: We do not like fruit grown in other countries. We like to eat local fruit.

beginner.m: Fog is a cloud that is close to or on the ground and sometimes prevents a person from being able to see.
beginner.e: It was hard to see in the morning because there was a lot of fog.

beginner.m: A letter is a symbol which makes up part of a word.
beginner.e: The word fly has 3 letters: f, l and y.

beginner.m: A thing that is true is real.
beginner.e: Strange as the story sounded, the story was real.

beginner.m: When someone feels sad, they have a bad feeling because of a loss or other problem. They are not happy.
beginner.e: The sad girl cried.

beginner.m: If something is false, it is not true or not real.
beginner.e: It is false that 2 + 2 = 5.

beginner.m: A leader is someone who leads others and has them following him.
beginner.e: Kings, presidents, governors, and mayors are all different types of leaders.

beginner.m: A check is a piece of paper that gives someone else the right to receive some money from your bank account. (Other spelling: cheque)
beginner.e: She wrote him a personal check for $250.

beginner.m: An atom is the smallest bit that matter can be broken down into.
beginner.e: Atoms of hydrogen make up a water molecule.

beginner.m: When you say something, you share it in words.
beginner.e: He says he is hungry.

beginner.m: The act of visiting.
beginner.e: I paid a visit to my grandmother last weekend to see how she was doing.

beginner.m: If something is loose, it moves easily or may come away from what it is attached to.
beginner.e: His tooth is loose and will probably come out in a day or two.

beginner.m: A drink is a liquid that you take in through your mouth.
beginner.e: He served her a hot drink and some cake.

beginner.m: If something is pleasant, it is enjoyable or agreeable.
beginner.e: When it rains in the summer, it is a pleasant event.

beginner.m: An apartment is a place with several rooms in a building where other people also live.
beginner.e: The woman moved her furniture into her new apartment.

beginner.m: A double door, window, etc. includes two of the same kind.
beginner.e: Call me at five nine double three.

beginner.m: When something is right, it is correct.
beginner.e: You did the right thing.

beginner.m: If you earn something you get it by working or doing something.
beginner.e: He worked hard to earn our respect.

beginner.m: A tear is hole made by pulling or ripping something.
beginner.e: I cannot wear a shirt with a tear in it!

beginner.m: A type is one thing or a group of things that are all members of a larger group because of some similarity.
beginner.e: I use the same type of camera at work.

beginner.m: Grass is a green, leafy plant that often covers the ground.
beginner.e: We haven't got much rain, and the grass on the lawn is turning brown.

beginner.m: When you provide something, you make it available.
beginner.e: The restaurant provided food for the party.

beginner.m: If you admire something, you like it very much.
beginner.e: He admired the painting on the wall.

beginner.m: When two people agree about something, they have the same ideas. They both think the same things are true.
beginner.e: We agree that it will probably rain this afternoon.

beginner.m: Contrasts are the differences you find when you compare something or someone.
beginner.e: Married life is a sharp contrast to the life of a single person.

beginner.m: If you have independence, you are alone or relying on yourself.
beginner.e: The American soldiers bravely fought against the British to earn their independence.

beginner.m: Punctuation is a set of symbols used to give meaning in text by putting them between words, clauses, phrases and sentences.
beginner.e: Use the proper punctuation in your essay.

beginner.m: Gender is a way of grouping nouns in some languages, for example: masculine, feminine & neuter.
beginner.e: In French, the gender affects everything from the choice of le or la to the adjective endings.

beginner.m: The image caused by light in your eyes, due to light of various wavelengths hitting your retina.
beginner.e: My favorite color is blue.

beginner.m: If you imagine something, you make a picture of it in your head.
beginner.e: I imagined myself fighting a monster.

beginner.m: A skirt is a loose cloth that a woman uses to cover her legs; the lower part of a dress.
beginner.e: She has a blue skirt and a red shirt on.

beginner.m: A concert is a musical performance, usually of several selections.
beginner.e: I attended three concerts last month.

beginner.m: A princess is the daughter of the king and queen of a country, and sister of the prince. The princess can also be the wife of a prince.
beginner.e: The soldier is going to marry the princess.

beginner.m: A theater is a building with a big room with a stage and places for many people to sit, so that people can watch a play with actors in it.
beginner.e: We went to the theater to watch a play by Shakespeare.

beginner.m: A land that is controlled by a government.
beginner.e: Russia is the largest country in the world.

beginner.m: A gun is a weapon that sends bullets through its metal tube.
beginner.e: John F. Kennedy was shot by a gun.

beginner.m: The seaside is the area by the sea, especially where people go for fun or vacation.
beginner.e: They spent their vacation at the seaside.

beginner.m: Food is what people and animals eat for nutrition or pleasure when they are hungry.
beginner.e: We grow our own food.

beginner.m: A concern about something means something that a person is worried about.
beginner.e: Poor sales are causing concern among the owners.

beginner.m: An egg is a common food that is ball-shaped and can have a baby animal inside, such as a chicken, a fish, a snake, etc.
beginner.e: I had a boiled egg for breakfast.

beginner.m: To have a fear of someone or something means to be scared of someone or something; to be afraid of someone or something.
beginner.e: She has a fear of spiders.

beginner.m: An emergency is a serious situation that needs to be dealt with very quickly.
beginner.e: She called 911 to report the emergency to police.

beginner.m: If a rule, a principle, a law, etc. applies, it has some effect on the situation.
beginner.e: I understand the idea, but I don't think it applies here.

beginner.m: A guard is a person or a group of people who watch something and try to stop anything bad from happening to it.
beginner.e: The inmate was beaten by a prison guard while other guards watched.

beginner.m: Harvest is the time that you bring the crops in from the fields.
beginner.e: We had an early harvest this year because of all the sun.

beginner.m: Another name for refrigerator.
beginner.e: I'll get some cheese from the fridge.

beginner.m: Feathers are the things which cover birds.
beginner.e: The bird was covered in feathers.

beginner.m: The beginning of something in place or time.
beginner.e: We went back to the start.

beginner.m: A face is the front part of the head.
beginner.e: His face was red with embarrassment.

beginner.m: A small person or thing is not big. It doesn't have much size.
beginner.e: A mouse is a small animal. A baby mouse is very small.

beginner.m: A mosque is the place of worship for Muslims.
beginner.e: There's a mosque near where I live.

beginner.m: Dishes are the flat round holder for food that we usually put on the table and eat off of.
beginner.e: There was a crash when the waiter dropped his tray of dishes on the floor.

beginner.m: Using very little time; moving far in little time.
beginner.e: I will wash quickly.

beginner.m: An inner item is located close to the center.
beginner.e: The inner city was crowded and dirty.

beginner.m: A guest is a person who you welcome into your house, your office, etc.
beginner.e: There were over 200 guests at our wedding party.

beginner.m: The fruit is the part of a plant or tree that holds the seeds. It's usually sweet and good to eat.
beginner.e: Most people don't eat enough fruit and vegetables.

beginner.m: A root is a part of a tree or plant that is under the ground.
beginner.e: The tree was supported by strong roots.

beginner.m: You use however to show that there is a contrast between two ideas.
beginner.e: It was very long. However, it was not long enough.

beginner.m: Writing that looks at an issue or subject.
beginner.e: Each student had to write an essay on his favorite author.

beginner.m: A poster is a large piece of paper with a picture or writing on it.
beginner.e: I saw a poster advertising lemonade.

beginner.m: A barber is a person whose job is cutting hair and shaving beards.
beginner.e: I went to the local barber to get a shave and a haircut.

beginner.m: If you are glad about something, you are happy about it.
beginner.e: I'm glad to hear you're feeling better.

beginner.m: An editor is someone who edits or changes the text in a document.
beginner.e: Simple English Wiktionary welcomes all editors to edit its pages.

beginner.m: When you wander around, you walk or move slowly around without a purpose.
beginner.e: He would wander through the city streets late at night when he could not sleep.

beginner.m: If something is fresh it is not old, it is new or like new. Often this means not spoiled or rotten.
beginner.e: I only eat fresh food.

beginner.m: When someone is rich, they have a lot of money and things.
beginner.e: Bill Gates is rich because he has 60 billion dollars.

beginner.m: A menu is a small book for displaying the type of food sold in a restaurant.
beginner.e: We collected the menu from the waiter after we sat down in the fast food restaurant.

beginner.m: Mutual; shared by more than one.
beginner.e: The two teams have the common goal of winning the game.

beginner.m: If something is probably true, or will probably happen, it means there is a high chance of it.
beginner.e: I'm not sure what I'm doing tonight, but I'll probably stay home and study.

beginner.m: A part of the face used for eating and talking
beginner.e: He opened his mouth to speak.

beginner.m: A building where you can keep and borrow money.
beginner.e: I have to stop at the bank to deposit my check and get money for tonight.

beginner.m: The part of arithmetic where numbers are added together.
beginner.e: He learned addition quickly.

beginner.m: Rice is a white or brown grain that people boil and eat.
beginner.e: In many Asian countries, including Japan, China, and Thailand, they eat rice with almost every meal.

beginner.m: If you hurry, you move or work quickly.
beginner.e: I woke up late and had to hurry through breakfast.

beginner.m: Candy is a sweet-tasting food.
beginner.e: There is a bowl of candy on the table.
