beginner.m: Someone or something that annoys is annoying.
beginner.e: He is so annoying!

beginner.m: A mushroom is a fungus that grows on soil or on dying wood.
beginner.e: While in the forest, make sure to look on dead trees for mushrooms!

beginner.m: If x reflects y, x shows or matches y, or x is affected by y.
beginner.e: His letters began to reflect his growing anger.

beginner.m: You use especially to say that something is special, or somehow different from others.
beginner.e: Nobody was old, but Paulo was especially young.

beginner.m: A cloud is a collection of condensed water vapor floating in the sky that sometimes makes rain.
beginner.e: Those dark storm clouds are quickly getting closer.

beginner.m: When you choose a thing, you decide you want it and not something else.
beginner.e: The manager and coaches will choose the starting line-up.

beginner.m: Liberty is the state of being free from someone else's control, not a slave or a prisoner.
beginner.e: John isn't in prison anymore; he has regained his liberty.

beginner.m: A bay is water with land around most of it.
beginner.e: She visited San Francisco Bay.

beginner.m: If you predict something, you say that it will happen before anyone observes it.
beginner.e: It is still difficult to accurately predict the weather more than two days in advance.

beginner.m: A page is one side of a sheet of paper in a book, newspaper, etc.
beginner.e: The picture of the accident was on page one of the morning's paper.

beginner.m: When you prevent something, you stop it from happening.
beginner.e: No one can prevent us from going.

beginner.m: A government is a group of people who make the laws and control a country or other place.
beginner.e: The local government announced a 5% cut in taxes.

beginner.m: Dreams are the images and things you see when you are sleeping.
beginner.e: In my dream I had forgotten the baby in a drawer.

beginner.m: The act of smiling; the form of one's mouth when one is smiling.
beginner.e: A visit to the fair always brings a smile to my face.

beginner.m: An umbrella is a tool to keep you dry when it rains. You hold it over your head.
beginner.e: I use my umbrella when it rains.

beginner.m: The principal thing is the main or most important one.
beginner.e: Canada's principal trading partner is the USA.

beginner.m: A century is a period of 100 years.
beginner.e: Centuries passed before the slaves were freed.

beginner.m: A measure of time, equal to 60 minutes.
beginner.e: There are 24 hours in one day.

beginner.m: A fee is the money you pay for some kinds of services, such as legal advice, education, or club membership.
beginner.e: School fees have increased again this year.

beginner.m: If someone or something is old, they are not young; they have been in existence for a long time.
beginner.e: An old man has gray hair.

beginner.m: A dog is a domestic mammal, related to wolves and foxes, that is often kept as a pet.
beginner.e: My pet dog is called "Rover".

beginner.m: Your attitude is your feelings and opinions, especially when your actions show how you feel.
beginner.e: He has a really bad attitude towards work.

beginner.m: A senior person has a higher social position.
beginner.e: She's a senior vice-president with the company.

beginner.m: A bus is a vehicle that carries a large number of people on roads.
beginner.e: Tourists didn't usually ride the local bus.

beginner.m: A musician is a person who makes music. Most often, this is someone whose job is to make music for other people.
beginner.e: There were five musicians in the band.

beginner.m: If something is military, it is a characteristic of people in the armed forces.
beginner.e: Sick soldiers go to the military hospital.

beginner.m: If something improves, it changes from bad to good.
beginner.e: The government is planning to improve the quality of rail service by adding new trains.

beginner.m: If something is possible, it is able to be done; doable; not impossible.
beginner.e: Life on other planets is possible.

beginner.m: A curse is a wish or hope that something bad will happen to someone or something.
beginner.e: The evil queen put a curse on the young girl.

beginner.m: If something is convenient, you can get it or use it quickly and easily.
beginner.e: This is the most convenient route to take.

beginner.m: An influence is a force that causes something to happen or for someone to do something.
beginner.e: Aerosmith has been quite an influence on rock music.

beginner.m: A storm is bad weather with high winds that disturbs the atmosphere.
beginner.e: Small boats should stay off the water tonight because we are expecting a storm.

beginner.m: Childhood is the state or condition of being an child, that is, being under 18 years of age.
beginner.e: Childhood is the first stage of every man's life.

beginner.m: Sense is any basic ability or understanding.
beginner.e: She has a great sense of fashion.

beginner.m: A problem is something that is difficult to do, understand, or believe.
beginner.e: Problems like these arise from a lack of care.

beginner.m: A host is a person or animal who makes a place for others and usually provides food and drink.
beginner.e: The host of the party was so busy, she didn't have time to eat.

beginner.m: When a food is delicious, it is tasty or tastes very nice.
beginner.e: The lasagna the school cooks is delicious and the children loved it a lot.

beginner.m: When you receive something, you get something that was sent or given to you.
beginner.e: It is better to give than to receive.

beginner.m: If you make a bargain with someone, that means you agreed with them to make an exchange or trade.
beginner.e: He gave me his sandwich and I gave him my apple; it was a bargain.

beginner.m: Something that is more than what you expected; exceeding; additional.
beginner.e: I always put extra ketchup on my hamburger.

beginner.m: To bake or boil, to prepare food.
beginner.e: Darren will cook dinner today.

beginner.m: A mug is a large cup for hot drinks, with a handle but not used with a saucer.
beginner.e: He drank his hot coffee from an old mug.

beginner.m: A member is someone belonging to a group or organization.
beginner.e: I am a member of Simple English Wikipedia.

beginner.m: A party is when people get together for fun or to celebrate something like a birthday.
beginner.e: I'm throwing a huge party for my 21st birthday. There'll be cake, games, and lots of fun!

beginner.m: If you are busy, you are doing something and not available to do something else.
beginner.e: I'm too busy to go to the movies.

beginner.m: A lawyer is an expert in law. A lawyer has the job of standing for other people in court giving them advice about the law.
beginner.e: The lawyer represented the man in court.

beginner.m: A catch is something that is caught, like the fish a fishermen catches.
beginner.e: My dad brought home a good catch of trout today.

beginner.m: A monkey is a primate with a long tail that climbs trees.
beginner.e: We saw Vervet monkeys in the Zoo.

beginner.m: The position of something is the place where the thing is.
beginner.e: The position of the table is two metres from the wall.

beginner.m: An opinion is a personal idea, a person’s thoughts on a topic.
beginner.e: You gave your opinion of the case.

beginner.m: The last one of a group. Or, the last part of a thing, the place where it stops.
beginner.e: I tied a knot in the end of the rope.

beginner.m: A trip is a journey to a place
beginner.e: Let us go on a trip to John Doe Mountain. I have not been there in a while.

beginner.m: If something is wrong, it is not right. If something is wrong it may be incorrect, not true, or bad.
beginner.e: That answer is wrong.

beginner.m: Juice is the liquid that you get when you squeeze a fruit or vegetable.
beginner.e: I usually have orange juice and toast for breakfast.

beginner.m: If you pray, you make a wish or give thanks to a god believing they will pay attention or make the wish come true.
beginner.e: We prayed prayers of thanks.

beginner.m: A crowd is a lot of people in one place together.
beginner.e: The crowd were asked to go home.

beginner.m: Something wonderful is exciting, excellent, and creates feelings of wonder.
beginner.e: The newly discovered continent was full of strange and wonderful creatures.

beginner.m: If something is nice, it's good and people probably like it.
beginner.e: Thank you, sir; have a nice day yourself, sir.

beginner.m: A moment is a very short time. It is not an exact measurement.
beginner.e: Don't worry. I'll be back in a moment.

beginner.m: If something is precise it is correct and exact.
beginner.e: The precise nature of the tax changes has not been decided.

beginner.m: A plate is a hard flat thing, especially round ones that we put food on.
beginner.e: He ate everything on his plate.

beginner.m: A lifestyle is a way of living.
beginner.e: His lifestyle was not a good example for young people.

beginner.m: If something is likely, it is probably true or will probably happen.
beginner.e: It seems likely that he will miss the meeting.

beginner.m: A bee is a black and yellow striped insect with wings that makes honey. It has a stinger.
beginner.e: That bee is flying to the flower.

beginner.m: If you compare two things, you look at, talk about, or think about how they are the same and how they are different.
beginner.e: Compared to the sun, the moon is quite small.

beginner.m: A club is an organisation of people who share a similar sport, interest, or hobby.
beginner.e: He was a member of his high school drama club.

beginner.m: When you are shy, you are easily frightened, afraid, or careful.
beginner.e: He is usually shy around people.

beginner.m: The place that is between two things; the place that is halfway between two ends of something.
beginner.e: The middle of the three books is the one you want.

beginner.m: Used to describe something done every day.
beginner.e: He kept a daily diary.

beginner.m: Someone's grandson is the son of their son or daughter.
beginner.e: My daughter, Mary, just had a baby boy. He is my grandson.

beginner.m: A fight is when people are fighting.
beginner.e: There was a fight in the bar last night and three people had to go to the hospital.

beginner.m: A call is a time when you use the telephone to contact someone.
beginner.e: After she made the phone call, she left the office.

beginner.m: A habit is something that you do regularly.
beginner.e: John, don't bite your fingernails. It's a bad habit.

beginner.m: A perfume is something that gives out a scent, odor, aroma.
beginner.e: Her perfume smelled like lily of the valley.

beginner.m: When someone is slim, they are thin and not fat.
beginner.e: She is so slim that she looks like a wooden stick.

beginner.m: History is what happened in the past.
beginner.e: China has many old books about its history.

beginner.m: A stone is a hard, solid piece of earth.
beginner.e: I do not have a hammer but I will use a stone to hammer the nail.

beginner.m: If you realize something, you become aware of it.
beginner.e: Do you realize what you've done?

beginner.m: A topic is a general idea that someone is speaking (reading, thinking, etc.) about at a specific time.
beginner.e: Our library has books on a wide range of topics.

beginner.m: A creature is a large animal, especially a created (mythical) nonhuman.
beginner.e: Those creatures only come out at night.

beginner.m: If you admit someone, you allow them to enter an area or a building.
beginner.e: The man was admitted to the theater, and sat in the front row.

beginner.m: A winner is someone that has won a competition, or often wins.
beginner.e: Terry is considered the winner since he came in first in the 100 meters race event.

beginner.m: Seafood is any fish, shellfish, or underwater life that can be eaten.
beginner.e: The restaurant typically has fresh seafood coming in each day.

beginner.m: The original person or thing, happened or existed before others of its kind.
beginner.e: The book has been translated from the original Russian version.

beginner.m: When you tell something to someone, you speak to the person about some fact or idea.
beginner.e: I will not tell anyone.

beginner.m: A handbag is a small bag used by women (and sometimes men) to carry a few small personal items.
beginner.e: For my sister's birthday, I bought her a brown handbag and she really liked it.

beginner.m: If something is plastic, it is made of plastic.
beginner.e: Cameron is going to recycle some plastic bottles.

beginner.m: Dust is a thin powder that can be seen in the air or on a surface.
beginner.e: The old building was filled with dust.

beginner.m: A library is a place where books and other media are kept, usually on shelves. Most of the time, people are allowed to borrow these things.
beginner.e: I borrowed books at the public library today.

beginner.m: Design is how something looks and works.
beginner.e: Honda has a new engine in design.

beginner.m: If something is excellent, it is very, very good.
beginner.e: The tea we had with lunch was excellent. Where did you get it?

beginner.m: A superstar is an extremely successful, high-profile performer or sportsperson.
beginner.e: Madonna is a pop music superstar.

beginner.m: Rats are medium-sized rodents. They often live near people and eat garbage. Rats can carry diseases. They are also kept as pets and can be very tame.
beginner.e: I caught the rat that was eating our food.

beginner.m: If you say that perhaps something will happen or that perhaps it is true, you mean it may happen or be true.
beginner.e: Perhaps someday I'll learn how to drive.

beginner.m: News is information about things that happened a short time ago, especially on the radio, TV or in newspapers.
beginner.e: Do you have any news about Paul's sickness?

beginner.m: If you have ambition, then you have a want to accomplish (complete) a task.
beginner.e: Sometimes our ambition drives us to do things that we shouldn't.

beginner.m: Kilogram is a measurement of mass, one kilogram is 1000 grams.
beginner.e: One litre of water weighs about one kilogram.

beginner.m: A word that is used to agree or accept; to mean the same thing that the other person said.
beginner.e: Yes, I do eat fish.

beginner.m: If something is safe, it is not in danger.
beginner.e: I feel safe when I am at home.

beginner.m: A dig is a short negative comment about someone.
beginner.e: In a dig at the teacher, he said she's lucky to be right even once in a while.

beginner.m: A haircut is what happens when someone's hair is cut.
beginner.e: I usually get about three haircuts a year.

beginner.m: A small coin of little value, also called a penny; 100 cents make a dollar.
beginner.e: This gum only costs five cents.

beginner.m: If something is empty, it has nothing inside it.
beginner.e: Hey! You finished my beer. It's empty.

beginner.m: A week is a period of time that lasts seven days.
beginner.e: There are seven days in one week.

beginner.m: Panic is a very strong and overwhelming fear which dominates thinking.
beginner.e: When he yelled "fire!" a panic went through the crowd and suddenly people were yelling and pushing to get out.

beginner.m: If someone is rude or does something rude, they act in a way that will likely upset people.
beginner.e: Don't interrupt me when I'm speaking. It's rude.

beginner.m: A web is a series of lines, ideas, or thoughts connected.
beginner.e: Her web of thoughts is complex.

beginner.m: A wedding is a special time when two people marry each other.
beginner.e: The wedding was very beautiful.

beginner.m: Crisps are thin, deep-fried potatoes.
beginner.e: I ate a packet of potato crisps yesterday.

beginner.m: A trip made by a runner; compare to walk.
beginner.e: I’m going for a run.

beginner.m: If a person says an option, he or she is suggesting.
beginner.e: I suggest that we go to the mall.

beginner.m: A tourist is a person who travels for pleasure, not for business.
beginner.e: There are many tourists looking at the church.

beginner.m: Something that is expensive costs a lot of money to buy or takes a lot of effort to get.
beginner.e: A pencil that cost $100 is very expensive.

beginner.m: Something that has been invented
beginner.e: Nowadays, we can buy new inventions as soon as they are made.

beginner.m: A plan is a clear idea of what you will do, often for a particular goal.
beginner.e: Have you made any plans for tomorrow?

beginner.m: An apron is a piece of clothing that is worn to protect from spills.
beginner.e: Chefs at this restaurant are required to wear aprons.

beginner.m: A grandchild is the grandson or granddaughter of someone. It is the child of someone's child.
beginner.e: Jemima is my grandmother. She is my father's mother. I am her grandchild.

beginner.m: A teacher is a person who teaches other people.
beginner.e: She was a very good teacher, I learned a lot from her.

beginner.m: One of a measure of something; the amount of something that is counted as "one".
beginner.e: Measure five units to the left.

beginner.m: A website is a place on the World Wide Web; if there are many pages to a website, they have the same URL and are usually part of the same server.
beginner.e: My favorite websites are ebay.com, espn.com, and facebook.com.

beginner.m: The bottom of something is its lowest part.
beginner.e: He was wet from top to bottom.

beginner.m: If something is negative, it is harmful, sad, or otherwise not good.
beginner.e: You can believe or not believe, that there's a positive and negative side to everything.

beginner.m: If X replaces Y or if you replace Y with X, X now does what Y used to do.
beginner.e: Smith will replace the injured Jones for England who are leading 2 to 0.

beginner.m: A cassette is a small flat case that holds the tape that records sounds and pictures.
beginner.e: The cassette was broken. None of the movie we filmed was recorded.

beginner.m: A piece of furniture to sleep on.
beginner.e: At night, I go to bed.

beginner.m: In a successful way; with success; without failing.
beginner.e: He successfully climbed the mountain.

beginner.m: A calendar is a system of measuring time.
beginner.e: The Chinese new year is different from the western new year because the Chinese use a lunar calendar.

beginner.m: Toast bread that is put into a toaster oven and toasted.
beginner.e: I had toast for breakfast.

beginner.m: If someone or something is famous, then many people know about them.
beginner.e: The ballet was made famous when it was produced in Paris.

beginner.m: Glass is a transparent solid and is usually clear. Windows and eyeglasses are made from it, as well as drinking glasses.
beginner.e: Through the window glass I could see the trees bend in the wind, but I was warm indoors.

beginner.m: A fish is an animal that lives in the water and has scales and gills.
beginner.e: When I went fishing, I only caught two fish.

beginner.m: A headache is a pain in your head.
beginner.e: I can't think properly because I have a bad headache.

beginner.m: If you fully understand or do something, you understand or do all of it.
beginner.e: I have not yet been able to understand this idea fully.

beginner.m: In software, a version of something that is put up for sale or that the public can use.
beginner.e: The video store advertised that it had all the latest "releases".

beginner.m: When something is alright, that means that it is in good condition.
beginner.e: My car is alright.

beginner.m: A spot is a small area that's different from that area around it.
beginner.e: I have a bald spot on my head.

beginner.m: A long, high basin that you put water in and go in to wash your body.
beginner.e: Jane put in water up to the top of the bath.

beginner.m: If something is fancy, it nicer than usual, often with decorations and bright colours.
beginner.e: That's a very fancy dress you're wearing.

beginner.m: The female leader of a country whose son will probably lead the country.
beginner.e: The queen wore her royal robes at the ceremony.

beginner.m: A length; 100 centimeters.
beginner.e: This table is 2 meters wide.

beginner.m: A cake is a sweet baked food.
beginner.e: Would you like some cake for dessert?

beginner.m: A song is some music with words in verse.
beginner.e: That song sounds beautiful.

beginner.m: A runner is someone who runs.
beginner.e: The cheetah is a very fast runner.

beginner.m: A festival is an organized event that contains a number of performances and usually happens every year.
beginner.e: Many actors are in town for the Toronto international film festival.

beginner.m: A dancer is someone who dances.
beginner.e: I'm a really bad dancer.

beginner.m: Technology is the tools, equipment, and activities that come from scientific knowledge.
beginner.e: The 1800s saw a gradual development (growth in small steps) of new technologies in farming and transportation.

beginner.m: A radio is piece of electronic equipment that sends or receives signals though the air and plays voice, music, or other sounds.
beginner.e: CBC 99.1 FM is my favorite radio station.

beginner.m: Figures are numbers showing the value or amount of something.
beginner.e: The sales figures from the spring were down from last year.

beginner.m: A photo is a picture created by a camera digitally or on film.
beginner.e: I took a photo of that beautiful old building.

beginner.m: A room in a house that is used for sleeping. This is where the bed is kept.
beginner.e: I hate camping. I wish I was back in my bedroom, sleeping in my own bed.

beginner.m: A desk is a table for studying and writing, usually with drawers.
beginner.e: The phone on her desk buzzed; Gillian picked it up.

beginner.m: A sauce is a thick liquid that you put on food to give it a special taste.
beginner.e: I put the chicken in a special sauce for two hours before I cook it.

beginner.m: The study of finding how things work. Some kinds of science are mathematics, biology, physics and chemistry.
beginner.e: Biology is a kind of science.

beginner.m: If you invite someone to something, you ask them to be there.
beginner.e: Rasheed invited me to his house on Friday, but I don't think I can go.

beginner.m: A globe is a solid shaped like a ball, often with a map on it.
beginner.e: He spun the globe on his desk, looking for Japan.

beginner.m: Petrol is a liquid fuel made from oil.
beginner.e: Let's hope the car doesn't run out of petrol.

beginner.m: A balloon is a light round ball filled with air that floats; often a child's toy.
beginner.e: My balloon floated away into the sky.

beginner.m: If you have an adventure you have a trip with a lot of excitement, hazards, or dangers.
beginner.e: Bilbo went on an adventure.

beginner.m: A mention of something, is when somebody mentions it.
beginner.e: Kavanagh's book makes no mention of Katherine's name.

beginner.m: If someone is sleepy, that person feels like they need to sleep; they are tired.
beginner.e: My son woke me up at four in the morning, and I had to work until eight at night! Now I'm very sleepy.

beginner.m: A hill is a piece of high ground that rises up out of lower ground. A hill is like a mountain but smaller.
beginner.e: My house was on the top of a hill.

beginner.m: If something is dry, it has no water or liquid on it.
beginner.e: The Sahara desert is dry.

beginner.m: Touch is the act of feeling or coming into physical contact with something.
beginner.e: A gentle touch of the fabric told her it was silk.

beginner.m: Whole is used to describe every part of an object.
beginner.e: I ate the whole meal, leaving nothing left.

beginner.m: The act of placing your lips on something, usually to show love or affection.
beginner.e: She gave him a long kiss on the lips.

beginner.m: A tree is a tall plant of wood.
beginner.e: I'm going to climb a tree.

beginner.m: Two people are friends of each other if they like being together and they like helping each other, but are not related.
beginner.e: I only have three close friends.

beginner.m: Trade is the buying and selling of goods.
beginner.e: Trade between Canada and the US is at its highest level in years.

beginner.m: Huge; very big; very large.
beginner.e: Elephants are enormous animals.

beginner.m: A plane is a vehicle with wings that flies.
beginner.e: Can we hurry? I have to catch a plane to Miami.

beginner.m: A quarter is one fourth (1/4) of something.
beginner.e: The lake was about a quarter mile from town.

beginner.m: A rush is a fast movement.
beginner.e: A rush of air blew the papers off the desk.

beginner.m: If you remind somebody of something, you tell them something they already know to make them think about it again.
beginner.e: We doctors have to constantly remind ourselves to keep it simple.

beginner.m: When you learn something, you start to know how to do things that you didn't know before.
beginner.e: I'm going to learn English!

beginner.m: A birth is when a new baby comes out of its mother.
beginner.e: My mother gave birth to my brother at 12:00 on Dec. 31st.

beginner.m: A citizen is a person who lives in a particular place.
beginner.e: With the recent economic problems, ordinary citizens are worried.

beginner.m: Pants are a type of cloths worn on the legs. A pair of pants has a covering for each leg.
beginner.e: Pants were traditionally worn by men, but now women wear them too.

beginner.m: A surname is a family name, sometimes called a last name.
beginner.e: John Smith's surname is "Smith".

beginner.m: A band is a group of people working together.
beginner.e: Those in the army who fought closely together in the war were called a band of brothers.

beginner.m: A palace is the home of a king or queen.
beginner.e: Elizabeth II of England lives in a palace in London, called Buckingham Palace.

beginner.m: A response is some words or actions that happen as a reaction to something else.
beginner.e: The police response to these problems has been slow and weak.

beginner.m: A mall is a shopping center where there are many stores that are all in one building.
beginner.e: My friends and I like to go to the mall.

beginner.m: Post is the letters and parcels that you send to other people.
beginner.e: The new book arrived in the post.

beginner.m: A can is a metal container, usually for holding food or drink.
beginner.e: I drink cola from a can.

beginner.m: A photograph is a picture that is created by a camera digitally or on film.
beginner.e: The photograph of the event won a Pulitzer Prize.

beginner.m: Sunglasses are objects that people put on their eyes to protect their eyes from the sunlight
beginner.e: You should wear sunglasses if it is a sunny day.

beginner.m: A married woman.
beginner.e: Bill just married his second wife.

beginner.m: A hamburger is a sandwich made from meat in small pieces that are fried together.
beginner.e: I'd like to have a hamburger and some fries.

beginner.m: A court is where people are tried for crimes.
beginner.e: The bad guy goes to court to stand before the judge.

beginner.m: If something is tidy, it is clean and everything is in its place.
beginner.e: The book had a neat and tidy ending.

beginner.m: A pear is an edible fruit that is made by the pear tree, looking like an apple, but with an elongated area around the stem.
beginner.e: Sally bit into a ripe green pear, with juice coming out from either side of her mouth.

beginner.m: Not alive.
beginner.e: My brother is dead. His funeral was last week.

beginner.m: A shade is a shadow of a tree or another big thing that blocks some of the light and heat of the Sun.
beginner.e: She rested in the shade of the tree because she felt hot.

beginner.m: If something is high, it is a long way up.
beginner.e: The airplane flew very high.

beginner.m: Water is a clear liquid of the chemical compound H₂O that all living things need in order to live.
beginner.e: Your plant needs more water as it is about to die.

beginner.m: Something you do to fool (trick) someone.
beginner.e: I did a trick that the children thought was magic.

beginner.m: Colored black
beginner.e: The black bunny was the color of night.

beginner.m: An offer is when you say you will do something or give something.
beginner.e: He wanted to buy my car, so he made me an offer of $5000.

beginner.m: A symbol is a letter or simple picture with a particular meaning.
beginner.e: These symbols represent the phone's various functions.

beginner.m: A hat is a piece of clothing that you wear on your head.
beginner.e: Men remove their hats when entering a church.

beginner.m: Fried food is food that has been cooked in a pan with hot oil.
beginner.e: I don't like fried chicken. It's too oily.

beginner.m: A note is a single sound in music.
beginner.e: In this song, every word is on a different note.

beginner.m: The sounds made by throat.
beginner.e: His voice was deep and clear.

beginner.m: A prediction is an idea or guess of what will happen in the future.
beginner.e: The president gave a prediction as to whether or not the bill would be passed.

beginner.m: A survey is a broad look at a topic or place.
beginner.e: Before looking for a job, he did a survey of the companies in the area.

beginner.m: A story is a piece of text that tells someone who reads it about a real or fictional (made up) event.
beginner.e: The film is based on a true story.

beginner.m: An instrument for eating, with 3 or 4 sharp points called tines, all in the same direction.
beginner.e: I ate with my fork.

beginner.m: A hobby is an activity that a person likes to do with their extra time.
beginner.e: When I'm not at work, my hobby is to work on my car.

beginner.m: An onion is a vegetable. They can make you cry when you cut them.
beginner.e: She liked eating onions, but they made her cry.

beginner.m: A castle is a large, strong building used to protect the people inside.
beginner.e: In the Middle Ages, castles were used to protect the king and queen.

beginner.m: If something is rather large, different, difficult, etc., it is quite that way.
beginner.e: I saw something rather unusual this morning.

beginner.m: A box is a square container, usually with four sides, a top and a bottom.
beginner.e: UPS had delivered a stack of boxes.

beginner.m: If you talk about the health of a person or animal, you are talking about whether they are sick or not.
beginner.e: Before you start exercising, you should be in good health.

beginner.m: A force is the act of a thing pushing on another thing, or how strongly it pushes.
beginner.e: In science, energy is force times distance.

beginner.m: A move is something which is done to achieve a goal.
beginner.e: The move had not been expected.

beginner.m: The east is a place that is closer to where the sun rises than another place.
beginner.e: My parents live in the east.

beginner.m: A singer is someone who sings.
beginner.e: She is a very good singer.

beginner.m: Dinosaurs are reptiles that were extinct (all died) millions of years ago.
beginner.e: Most dinosaurs were large.

beginner.m: Someone who is smart shows intelligence.
beginner.e: You know algebra? Wow, you're smart!

beginner.m: An idea for something to do, that someone says to another person. The other person is free to do the thing or not do the thing.
beginner.e: I have a suggestion for you: have more fruit and you will be healthier.

beginner.m: A repair is something a person does to something to fix it.
beginner.e: Last night the car wouldn't start, so this morning I took it in for repairs.

beginner.m: Foreign means something that comes from a different place or country. Foreign people are known as foreigners.
beginner.e: Sven has a foreign accent.

beginner.m: A metal with a near white colour and high value and the symbol Ag.
beginner.e: He paid with a silver dollar.

beginner.m: A system is a group of things that work together; a way of doing something.
beginner.e: This coloured paper is part of my system for keeping lists of people.

beginner.m: A lane is one part of the road that cars traveling in one direction stay in, usually divided by white or yellow paint from other lanes.
beginner.e: It's very annoying when slow drivers stay in the fast lane.

beginner.m: A climb is an upwards movement, often a slow or difficult one.
beginner.e: The Yen has made a strong climb this year.

beginner.m: If something remains it stays. It does not go away.
beginner.e: He remained at home.

beginner.m: A device that liquids come out of.
beginner.e: We don't have bottled water, you'll have to get it from the tap.

beginner.m: A notebook is a book with blank sheets that you can write or draw in.
beginner.e: Remember to take your notebook to class.

beginner.m: When you believe, you have faith in something.
beginner.e: He believes in one God.

beginner.m: Someone's grandmother is the mother of one of their parents.
beginner.e: The mother of my mother is Jane Smith. Jane Smith is my grandmother.

beginner.m: Your legs are the two long parts of your body that you move to walk, or a similar body part on an animal.
beginner.e: I lost a leg in the war.

beginner.m: If you feel that something is the case, you have a strong idea in your mind that it is the case.
beginner.e: I feel that not enough is being done to protect the local animal life.

beginner.m: A vacation is some time, usually between a week and a month, when people do not have to go to work, but get paid.
beginner.e: Our last vacation was very nice.

beginner.m: A star, especially a star that is at the center of a solar system.
beginner.e: Scientists have found other suns with planets around them.

beginner.m: A roof is the top part of a building.
beginner.e: My five brothers, two sisters and seven cousins all live together under one roof.

beginner.m: If something is clean, it is free from dirt
beginner.e: To keep the air clean, smoking is not allowed.

beginner.m: To face a different direction
beginner.e: The dancers turned round and around.

beginner.m: Laziness is the act of being lazy or idle and to do no work.
beginner.e: Laziness is one of the seven deadly sins.

beginner.m: If you create something, you make or invent it. Usually, it's something that nobody has made before.
beginner.e: Wiktionary editors create Wiktionary entries.

beginner.m: If you work, you do a job, usually for money.
beginner.e: My father works at Microsoft.

beginner.m: Jam is a sweet spread for bread made by boiling fruit.
beginner.e: I want blueberry jam on my toast.

beginner.m: Once more.
beginner.e: They didn't understand the answer, so they asked again.

beginner.m: An exchange is the act of exchanging.
beginner.e: I did well in that exchange. Now I have three good new books, and I only paid a little money.

beginner.m: A soft, plush seat for one or more people, often made of leather or cloth.
beginner.e: Our pet cat and dog are both sitting down the couch.

beginner.m: If you feel dizzy, you have a feeling of spinning around and losing your balance.
beginner.e: I stood up too fast and felt dizzy.

beginner.m: If you are asleep, you are sleeping.
beginner.e: Please be quiet. The baby's asleep.

beginner.m: Upset in an aggressive way.
beginner.e: He embarrassed her, so she was angry.

beginner.m: When you stay somewhere, you do not move from there.
beginner.e: Whenever I am tired I stay in bed.

beginner.m: A flower is part of a plant. Flowers are often very pretty. Plants make them so that they can make new seeds.
beginner.e: The flower of the plant is starting to wilt.

beginner.m: A waiter is the person at a restaurant who takes your order and brings the food to you.
beginner.e: I'm trying to get the waiter to bring our bill but he isn't looking this way.

beginner.m: Upset means to be very angry or sad; to be unhappy.
beginner.e: He was upset after someone said bad things to him very loudly.

beginner.m: To find a new idea that was not known before, or to find a thing that was not known about before.
beginner.e: Doctors want to discover a cure for cancer.

beginner.m: A challenge is something difficult that you want or have to do.
beginner.e: Many churches overseas are struggling to meet the AIDS challenge.

beginner.m: Homework is practice or study that you are supposed to do outside class.
beginner.e: Dad, could you help me with my homework?

beginner.m: Something is political if it is related to politics.
beginner.e: He supports the Democratic political party.

beginner.m: If you operate a machine, you control it.
beginner.e: Everyone on board is able to operate the ship.

beginner.m: If you introduce someone or something, you make them known to someone else.
beginner.e: Let me introduce you to my friend.

beginner.m: When you are thirsty, you feel like you need to have a drink.
beginner.e: After eating dinner, I was very thirsty.

beginner.m: A product is an item that can be bought.
beginner.e: That store sells many different products.

beginner.m: A star is a bright thing in the sky at night. The sun is also one of stars.
beginner.e: Stars seem little, but they are big and far away.

beginner.m: If a piece of furniture, clothing, a room, etc. is uncomfortable, you feel uncomfortable in it (see 2.)
beginner.e: The chairs looked so uncomfortable that he didn't sit down.

beginner.m: If something is unnecessary, it is not needed.
beginner.e: Do not add unnecessary words to your comprehension answers.

beginner.m: Someone's mind is the part of them that thinks.
beginner.e: In my mind I know I must go, but in my heart I want to stay here.

beginner.m: A shout is when somebody shouts one time.
beginner.e: His angry shouts and yelling woke me up.

beginner.m: A quality that make a person (or thing) distinct from another.
beginner.e: My teacher complained to me about my personality.

beginner.m: A bird is a warm-blooded animal that has feathers and wings and lays eggs. Most birds can fly.
beginner.e: A sparrow is a bird and so is a penguin, even though it cannot fly.

beginner.m: A cry is a loud shout or scream.
beginner.e: She gave a little cry of fear.

beginner.m: Butter is a firm yellow substance that is made from milk spread on bread or used in cooking.
beginner.e: Please pass the butter.

beginner.m: A symphony is music that is written for an orchestra.
beginner.e: Beethoven's most famous symphony was Symphony No. 5.

beginner.m: Classmate is a person (a student) who studies in the same class as you (in a school).
beginner.e: My classmate finished his assignment.

beginner.m: A person's vocabulary is the words that person knows.
beginner.e: Reading will help you increase your vocabulary.

beginner.m: A baby is a very young child, less than two years old, who has not yet learned how to speak.
beginner.e: I used to be a baby but now I am an adult.

beginner.m: You use apparently to indicate that the information you are giving is something that you have heard or seen, but you are not certain that it is true.
beginner.e: Rudolph said no more. Apparently he was a man of few words.

beginner.m: A load is something carried, often something heavy.
beginner.e: The truck arrived with a load of dog food.

beginner.m: If you add x to y, you put x and y together.
beginner.e: Cook for five minutes, then add the remaining spices to the soup.

beginner.m: Not loud; making no sound or making very little sound.
beginner.e: You should be quiet in a library or a movie theater.

beginner.m: A type of box with a lid that you can lock.
beginner.e: He put his things in the chest.

beginner.m: A natural rise of the Earth's surface having considerable mass
beginner.e: We visited that mountain last year. The scenery was beautiful.

beginner.m: A drum is a musical instrument with a skin that you hit to make music.
beginner.e: My cousin plays drums.

beginner.m: If you publish a book, an article, a song, etc. you make it available for other people to buy, read, listen to, etc.
beginner.e: She publishes a monthly magazine.

beginner.m: If someone is frightened, they feel scared.
beginner.e: I was frightened by a loud noise.

beginner.m: With everything included; entire, total.
beginner.e: It was a complete shock when he turned up on my doorstep.

beginner.m: If something is hard, it is not soft.
beginner.e: I kicked the wall and hurt my foot. The wall is hard.

beginner.m: Someone gets an education if that person learns something or if somebody teaches that person something, usually at school.
beginner.e: He studied German by himself, but he has no formal education.

beginner.m: A lot of something is a large amount of it.
beginner.e: He caused lots of trouble.

beginner.m: When a group of people stop working to improve or defend their working conditions or pay, they go on strike.
beginner.e: Every secretary at the company went on strike for better pay.

beginner.m: The finish is the last part or end of something.
beginner.e: It was a good day from start to finish.

beginner.m: A sofa is a type of chair with soft seats and arm rests, typically designed to seat more than one person.
beginner.e: Your sofa is comfortable.

beginner.m: A cross (🞣) is a figure made of two straight lines or bars that intersect each other such that at least one of them bisects the other.
beginner.e: In Christianity, the death of Jesus is represented by a cross.

beginner.m: Someone's granddaughter is the daughter of their son or daughter.
beginner.e: My daughter, Mary, just had a baby girl. She is my granddaughter.

beginner.m: If a person is overweight, they are above a weight that is considered normal or desirable.
beginner.e: He used to be very overweight.

beginner.m: A way to get away from something.
beginner.e: I'm afraid we have no escape.

beginner.m: If something is bright it gives out or fills with much light.
beginner.e: The sun is very bright during summer.

beginner.m: Someone or something produces something when they make it or create it or make it come out.
beginner.e: He produced the paper out of his bag.

beginner.m: The owner of a thing is the person who owns the thing: who has the thing or who should have the thing. A thing belongs to its owner.
beginner.e: You have to give it back to me. I'm the owner.

beginner.m: Wind is the moving air.
beginner.e: The wind blows so strongly now that a person's hair goes in the person's face.

beginner.m: Something that is recent has happened a short while ago.
beginner.e: These changes are quite recent.

beginner.m: If you have control over someone or something, you can make it do what you want.
beginner.e: The country fell under the direct control of the army.

beginner.m: Someone taking part in a sport or game.
beginner.e: Tom watched as the players walked on to the field.

beginner.m: Stuff is what makes up something; the things that it is made from.
beginner.e: What is all that stuff on your bedroom floor?

beginner.m: Inspiration is being inspired.
beginner.e: I've been filled with inspiration lately.

beginner.m: A daughter is a female child of someone.
beginner.e: I am her father and she is my daughter.

beginner.m: A student is person who studies a subject, especially in a school.
beginner.e: I am a student at the school.

beginner.m: An office is a room or building where people sit at desks and work.
beginner.e: We're meeting at the office after work.

beginner.m: Silence is when no noise is heard.
beginner.e: The silence was strange, not even a bird could be heard.

beginner.m: Entertainment is things that you do, watch, read, or listen to for fun (e.g., movies, TV, music, games, etc.)
beginner.e: Most people in town go to the bar for entertainment.

beginner.m: An apple is a sweet, red, yellow or green fruit.
beginner.e: I gave my teacher an apple.

beginner.m: If something is pretty, people like to look at it.
beginner.e: Those flowers are so pretty.

beginner.m: A shower is a place with water spraying down to clean something.
beginner.e: I usually have a shower before going to work.

beginner.m: Trousers are clothes worn over the lower body, with two legs.
beginner.e: He put on his trousers.

beginner.m: An issue is a particular topic or subject, often one that people are discussing and/or is a problem.
beginner.e: We'd like to hire you, but there are some legal issues that we have to consider first.

beginner.m: Something that happens soon happens shortly after another time, often shortly after the time of speaking.
beginner.e: John is coming home soon.

beginner.m: An attempt is a try at something, usually something difficult
beginner.e: It's broken and no attempt has been made to fix it.

beginner.m: If you are brave, fear will not stop you.
beginner.e: She has been brave about her disease.

beginner.m: A small group of questions asked together. Often a quiz is like a small test at school.
beginner.e: I thought we were going to have a test, but it was only a short quiz.

beginner.m: When you keep something for someone, you make something safe.
beginner.e: I will keep your money for you.

beginner.m: An album is a record, tape, or CD, with many songs on it.
beginner.e: He loved the Beatles, and had bought all their albums.

beginner.m: If it is foggy, it is covered by fog.
beginner.e: It was hard to see because the road was foggy.

beginner.m: If something shines, light comes from it, or it reflects light.
beginner.e: I love the way the stars shine.

beginner.m: The role of a person or thing is the job that they do in a certain situation.
beginner.e: Music plays an important role in the movie.

beginner.m: Heat is a kind of energy. It is the quality things have when they are warm or hot.
beginner.e: This is a good coat. It keeps the heat in.

beginner.m: Soap is a solid or liquid that you use to wash things.
beginner.e: The soap bubbles filled the sink.

beginner.m: A manager is someone who manages or organizes people or things together.
beginner.e: Ask the manager of this project. He knows what to do next.

beginner.m: A fare is money that you pay for public transportation; that is, to ride on a bus, taxi, train or airplane.
beginner.e: The city is planning to increase its bus fares again.

beginner.m: A tool is an object that you use to do a specific job, such as a hammer.
beginner.e: I used to fix my own car, but I sold all my tools.

beginner.m: If something is clearly true, then it is easy to see that it is true.
beginner.e: The building is clearly visible from the air.

beginner.m: A car is a small passenger vehicle with four wheels, moved by an engine.
beginner.e: I just drive around in my car all day.

beginner.m: An earring is a piece of jewelry worn on the ear.
beginner.e: She wore golden earrings.

beginner.m: The end of the working week, usually Saturday and Sunday.
beginner.e: I do not have work on the weekend.

beginner.m: A piece is a part of something that can be or has been separated from it.
beginner.e: I own a piece of land in the country.

beginner.m: A jacket is a piece of clothing with long sleeves that you wear over a shirt. A jacket is not as long as a coat.
beginner.e: He took his phone from the pocket of his jacket.

beginner.m: If you do something quickly or something happens quickly, it happens in a very short time.
beginner.e: I hope the train gets here quickly. I'm late already.

beginner.m: A living thing is a person, animal or plant that is not dead—it is still able to function and grow.
beginner.e: Living things grow and make more living things like themselves.

beginner.m: If you adjust something, you change it a little so that it fits or works better.
beginner.e: I had to adjust the cupboard door so that is would close easily.

beginner.m: A drawing is a picture.
beginner.e: He sketched a drawing of that vase.

beginner.m: A watch is a little clock on a person's arm near the person's hand, to measure time.
beginner.e: The person looks at his watch and has a thought that he is late.

beginner.m: A thing is something.
beginner.e: She sent her things to New York.

beginner.m: A coach is a teacher of a sport.
beginner.e: Even though his team won, first-year coach Andrew Johnson was not happy.

beginner.m: A major change, problem, event, etc. is a big and important one.
beginner.e: Tom Cruise had a major part in the movie. He directed it and acted in it as the main character.

beginner.m: A mother is the woman who is one of a person or animal's parents.
beginner.e: My mother read me a story and put me to bed every night when I was a child.

beginner.m: The act of seeing.
beginner.e: He had a view of the fight.

beginner.m: If I ask you if you have ever been to France, I am asking if you have been to France at any time in your life.
beginner.e: Have you ever met a king or queen?

beginner.m: A match is a game of football, tennis, etc.
beginner.e: We lost the first match, but hope to win our next two.

beginner.m: A common farm animal, the female cattle.
beginner.e: Milk comes from cows.

beginner.m: When you put a thing someplace, you move a thing to a place.
beginner.e: I always put my books on the table when I get home from school.

beginner.m: A swimsuit is a piece of clothing that fits close to your body that you wear when you swim.
beginner.e: Put on your swimsuit and let's go for a swim.

beginner.m: A row of things is a line of them, usually going from side to side.
beginner.e: OK, students, can you please put your desks in five rows?

beginner.m: If you tell a joke, you say something to make people laugh.
beginner.e: Trevor's joke about the boring lexicographer was too funny.

beginner.m: Friendship is being friends with someone.
beginner.e: Our friendship began in childhood.

beginner.m: If you give an example of something, you name one of that type of thing.
beginner.e: A baseball, a softball, a football, and a soccer ball are examples of balls.

beginner.m: When you depend on something, you need it; you rely on it; you trust it.
beginner.e: I knew I could depend on you to meet your aunt at the station.

beginner.m: An athlete is person involved in a sporting activity.
beginner.e: The athlete gets ready for her race.

beginner.m: A long and narrow piece of land between two places. Usually, cars drive on it, and it is often paved.
beginner.e: The taxi is parked on the side of the road.

beginner.m: We say "please" when we want to ask someone politely to do something.
beginner.e: Pass the salt, please.

beginner.m: Uncertain is the opposite of certain. You don't know whether it is going to happen or not. You have doubts about it.
beginner.e: I'm uncertain whether I should go out tonight.

beginner.m: A dentist is a doctor who specializes in dentistry.
beginner.e: I have to go to the dentist to get a tooth pulled.

beginner.m: If something is fine, it is OK, not a problem, or acceptable.
beginner.e: She said it works -- it's fine.

beginner.m: A policeman is someone who works for the police.
beginner.e: The policeman carried a gun.

beginner.m: A drive is a trip by car.
beginner.e: Let's go for a drive down to the lake.

beginner.m: A dress is a loose cloth covering a woman's body. The lower part is like a skirt. The top part is like a shirt.
beginner.e: She looked beautiful because she had a very nice dress.

beginner.m: When you stand, your body is at rest and supported only by your feet.
beginner.e: I stand in the bus when there are no seats.

beginner.m: A suit is a set of clothes that includes a coat or and pants or dress.
beginner.e: Everyone wears a suit where I work.

beginner.m: If you roast vegetables or meat, you cook it over a fire or in an oven for a long time.
beginner.e: I will roast the chicken in the oven.

beginner.m: Tea is a light brown or green drink that is very popular around the world.
beginner.e: Would you like coffee or tea?

beginner.m: The Earth.
beginner.e: Our world needs to be cared for.

beginner.m: Spaghetti is a type of pasta made using long thin noodles.
beginner.e: Spaghetti and meatballs was her favourite meal.

beginner.m: If you bake something, you cook it with dry heat all around it, usually in an oven.
beginner.e: Bake the cake at 325 °F for 25 minutes.

beginner.m: If you complain about someone or something, you say or write that you are not happy about it.
beginner.e: We complained to the manager about the service after waiting one hour for our food.

beginner.m: To not achieve a goal, or to go wrong.
beginner.e: The event is going to fail.

beginner.m: When you forget something, you have no memory of it.
beginner.e: I forget every thing that you tell me.

beginner.m: If something annoys people, it makes them angry or bothered. This often happens after someone does an action many times.
beginner.e: Stop annoying your sister.

beginner.m: If something is terrible, it's very bad.
beginner.e: He said she was ugly. Wasn't that a terrible thing to say to anyone?

beginner.m: When you perform something, you do it.
beginner.e: Please come help me perform this task.

beginner.m: A very reflective surface which light can bounce off of.
beginner.e: She kept staring at the mirror all day.

beginner.m: You use simply to emphasize that something is true and thinking about it in different ways won't change that.
beginner.e: Aliens simply do no exist.

beginner.m: When one thing happens and a second thing happens in a same or similar time or way, then the second thing also happens.
beginner.e: We bought bread at the store. We also bought milk.

beginner.m: When you serve food or drink, you give it to somebody to eat or drink, especially as a host.
beginner.e: Shall I serve your drinks first?

beginner.m: If you hear a sound, you notice it with your ear.
beginner.e: Speak louder, I cannot hear you!

beginner.m: Part of the leg between the thigh and the shin.
beginner.e: I hurt my knee in football.

beginner.m: A gentle person is kind and careful not to cause damage, pain, or surprise.
beginner.e: That bear is a monster, not at all a gentle giant.

beginner.m: If something happens automatically, it happens without the need for a person to start it or do anything more.
beginner.e: The door closed and locked automatically behind him.

beginner.m: The act of washing.
beginner.e: He gave the dog a wash.

beginner.m: Architecture is the art of planning, designing, and constructing buildings.
beginner.e: He studied classical architecture and design in Rome.

beginner.m: If you feel tired, you have no energy and you need a rest.
beginner.e: After walking for 15 km, I was so tired, that I couldn't take another step.

beginner.m: A hotel is a place where people pay to stay in a room overnight, usually for only a few days.
beginner.e: We fly to Taipei and stay at the Hilton hotel for three days and two nights.

beginner.m: A zoo is a park that people go to where live animals can be seen.
beginner.e: There are lions at our local zoo.

beginner.m: A wallet is a small case for holding money. It is made to fit in a pocket.
beginner.e: I put my wallet back in my pocket after paying for our meal.

beginner.m: About a job such as doctor, lawyer, accountant, etc.
beginner.e: The group offers free professional advice on legal matters and housing.

beginner.m: If you relax, you stop working, worrying, etc., and you take a rest or have fun.
beginner.e: If you don't relax your shoulders, you'll have a sore neck.

beginner.m: If someone splashes something (usually water) on somebody, they pour water on another person.
beginner.e: He playfully splashed water on the old man downstairs.

beginner.m: A museum is a building where pictures, sculptures and other arts are shown.
beginner.e: There are several museums in Paris.

beginner.m: A sink is a container for water to wash things in, usually with a drain.
beginner.e: The kitchen sink was always full of dirty dishes.

beginner.m: A container is full of things if there are many of the things in the container and no more can go in.
beginner.e: My life is full of problems.

beginner.m: A playground is a place where people go to play.
beginner.e: The playground had swings and slides for children.

beginner.m: A throw is the act of throwing.
beginner.e: You made a fast throw!

beginner.m: Smooth feels pleasant and flat when you touch it; not rough.
beginner.e: He felt the smooth skin on her cheek.

beginner.m: A custom is an activity that happens traditionally or regularly.
beginner.e: My mother's custom is to have breakfast in the garden with her newspaper.

beginner.m: Funny things keep people interested and can make people laugh.
beginner.e: That was a funny joke.

beginner.m: A bicycle is a vehicle with two wheels. You use your legs to make it move.
beginner.e: I learned to ride a bicycle when I was six years old.

beginner.m: If something is automatic, it works by itself.
beginner.e: A washing machine is automatic.

beginner.m: A kilometer is a measurement of distance. It is 1,000 meters (3,280.8 feet or 0.621 miles).
beginner.e: Four times around the track is one kilometer.

beginner.m: The proper way, place, use, etc. is the right one.
beginner.e: What is the proper way to write a letter?

beginner.m: To hear and then fully know what was said, know enough to do it. To know the meaning of something.
beginner.e: She didn't understand. She thought I meant the meeting was today.

beginner.m: To move towards a place or into a place; to move to the place where the person who is talking is.
beginner.e: Come to my house and I will give you something to eat.

beginner.m: Something's value is how good or important it is; how much money someone will exchange a thing for; an amount of money.
beginner.e: Human life has very much value.

beginner.m: A holiday is a day when people don't go to work or school, often because there is a religious celebration.
beginner.e: In North America, Christmas is the biggest holiday of the year.

beginner.m: An envelope is a paper cover that you put a letter in to send it.
beginner.e: She put the letter into the envelope, addressed it to Charles, and put a stamp on it.

beginner.m: Lunch is the meal that we eat in the middle of the day.
beginner.e: Shall we have sandwiches for lunch?

beginner.m: Email is a system where people can send a message from one computer to another.
beginner.e: I have a new email in my inbox.

beginner.m: A drop is a very small amount of a liquid.
beginner.e: A drop of water weighs 0.1 grams.

beginner.m: Oil is a liquid that is burned to create heat or used in machines to make them run well.
beginner.e: Gas and oil are essential to running a car.

beginner.m: Different
beginner.e: They were dressed in an unlike manner.

beginner.m: If something is female, it is of, for, or about women or girls.
beginner.e: This movie is good for a female audience.

beginner.m: A minute is a short time equal to sixty seconds. There are sixty minutes in one hour.
beginner.e: He ran the race in 1 minute and ten seconds.

beginner.m: Imagination is the ability to see something in your mind, or pretend that something false is true.
beginner.e: Children use imagination to see sticks as swords and fight monsters.

beginner.m: Existing in or constructed from fantasy; of or relating to fantasy; fanciful.
beginner.e: His fantastic post-school had all failed.

beginner.m: Someone pulls something when they use their hands to move the thing closer to themselves.
beginner.e: Pull the handle if you want to open the door.

beginner.m: A painting is a picture that is painted.
beginner.e: A painting of the president hung on the wall.

beginner.m: An item is a particular thing that is separate from other things.
beginner.e: There are a number of items here that belonged to your father.

beginner.m: A customer is a person who pays money for goods or services.
beginner.e: The restaurant had to close because there weren't enough customers.

beginner.m: A refrigerator is a machine which keeps food cold.
beginner.e: Put the milk in the refrigerator so it will stay fresh.

beginner.m: If something is due, it should happen at a particular time.
beginner.e: Your homework is due on Tuesday.

beginner.m: When someone is confident, the person is certain of something.
beginner.e: I am confident that I will win.

beginner.m: A half is 1/2 of a whole; 50%.
beginner.e: The glass was half full.

beginner.m: A test is writing that many learners do in a room at the same time so that people are able to see how much knowledge the learners have.
beginner.e: I'm happy because I got a high mark on the test.

beginner.m: To be afraid of someone or something means to be scared of someone or something; to have a fear of someone or something.
beginner.e: I'm afraid of snakes. I can't even go near them.

beginner.m: If you find something, you discover or locate it.
beginner.e: I can't find my keys. Have you seen them?

beginner.m: If you prefer something, you like it more than another thing.
beginner.e: Sometimes I eat in restaurants, but I prefer to cook.

beginner.m: All of the people in a big place like a country.
beginner.e: Getting Western publics to understand the nature of the war is hard enough.

beginner.m: If you cheer, you shout to show that you are happy about something or to encourage someone.
beginner.e: People cheered the home team wildly.

beginner.m: If something exists, it is real and has some kind of being.
beginner.e: Dinosaurs used to exist.

beginner.m: In some religions and myths, a spirit that delivers messages from God. Often angels are seen as working for God in general.
beginner.e: Gabriel is an important angel in Christianity and Islam.

beginner.m: You use possibly to say that something might be true.
beginner.e: This is possibly the biggest tree in the city.

beginner.m: Something that is broken is not as it should be because it has been damaged or injured
beginner.e: After the crash his arm seemed broken.

beginner.m: The heating is the system that keeps a house or building warm.
beginner.e: We put new gas heating into the house to make it warmer.

beginner.m: A high floor where some people perform while other people watch
beginner.e: The actors performed on the stage while the audience watched.

beginner.m: When something is really a certain way, its very or very much that way.
beginner.e: I'm really hungry now.

beginner.m: A regular event repeats after a similar amount of time or space.
beginner.e: I call home on a regular basis.

beginner.m: A break is a time when something stops before starting again.
beginner.e: I'll phone you during my lunch break.

beginner.m: A rule is a statement that tells whether you might get spanked for master baiting in class. If something is right or wrong.
beginner.e: Peter picked up the football, which was against the rules, so the other team got a throw-in.

beginner.m: Something that is done in a physical way.
beginner.e: He physically bullied the weak, causing them to be injured.

beginner.m: The weekdays are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, & Friday.
beginner.e: I can't sleep late on a weekday.

beginner.m: A person is someone.
beginner.e: She is a very nice person.

beginner.m: If a noun is singular in English grammar, it usually refers to only one thing.
beginner.e: If I say, "one cat", that's singular, but if I say, "a lot of cats", that's plural.

beginner.m: A teenager is a person whose age is a number that ends in "-teen." That is, someone between the ages of 13 and 19.
beginner.e: Many teenagers want to rebel.

beginner.m: A unit of length that is equal to 2.54 centimetres; there are 12 inches in a foot.
beginner.e: My pencil is six inches long.

beginner.m: A mystery is a secret or hidden matter which can't be explained.
beginner.e: She never told me where the money was, and it remains a mystery to me even now.

beginner.m: If you take an action, you do it.
beginner.e: I'm going to take a rest. = I'm going to rest.

beginner.m: A child is a young person, usually older than a baby but younger than a teenager.
beginner.e: Even as a child of six, I knew what hard work was.

beginner.m: Words are the smallest meaningful pieces of a language that can be used on their own.
beginner.e: Do you even understand the words I am saying?!

beginner.m: A boy is a male child or teenager; someone who is not a man yet.
beginner.e: Two teenage boys died in the crash.

beginner.m: One of the colors people can see
beginner.e: The wall was a mix of watery blues and greens.

beginner.m: Something's age is how long it has existed or been alive; how old something is.
beginner.e: Scott is showing his age.

beginner.m: Time is what we measure with a clock.
beginner.e: I don't have time to talk to you right now. Can we do it later?

beginner.m: If something is long, it takes a lot of time.
beginner.e: How long is it until we have our trip?

beginner.m: A lover of someone or something is someone who loves (like very much) that person or thing.
beginner.e: I'm a real pizza lover, and could eat pizza all day.

beginner.m: An airplane is a vehicle with wings that can fly.
beginner.e: Can we hurry? I have to catch an airplane to Miami.

beginner.m: A show is a display of art, movie, or drama. It can be a play, a movie, a concert, an opera or a television program.
beginner.e: I saw the art show at the museum.

beginner.m: Wealth is when one has a lot of money. Wealth is a lot of money or a lot of things of high value like land, houses, factories, jewelry, etc.
beginner.e: His wealth is so great that he wears new shoes every day.

beginner.m: The weight of something is how heavy it is.
beginner.e: I'm exercising to try to lose some weight.

beginner.m: If something is native, it belongs to you by birth.
beginner.e: This is my native land.

beginner.m: Your boss is the person who tells you what to do at work.
beginner.e: My former boss was very happy for the chance to fire me.

beginner.m: Pleasure is a nice feeling we have when we do something that's fun or that feels good.
beginner.e: Being at this party and seeing my friends again is a real pleasure.

beginner.m: A breeze is a gentle wind.
beginner.e: The cool evening breeze is very refreshing.

beginner.m: If your are kindly you often show kindness, usually for older people.
beginner.e: She was a kindly old lady.

beginner.m: An island is a piece of ground that is completely surrounded by water.
beginner.e: The fisherman lived alone on a small island in James Bay.

beginner.m: A clue is a piece of information that helps you answer a question or solve a problem.
beginner.e: She disappeared without a clue.

beginner.m: The back is the rear part of something; it is the part in the other direction from the front.
beginner.e: I went to the back of the house.

beginner.m: When you let someone do something, you allow them to do it.
beginner.e: I let him come with me.

beginner.m: Two things are the same if the two things have one size, and one shape, and one color, etc.
beginner.e: Sometimes we wear the same shirt.

beginner.m: A piece of glass in a wall to let people see through it.
beginner.e: He looked out the window.

beginner.m: A bookshelf is a shelf that hold books.
beginner.e: The book should be on the bookshelf.

beginner.m: A board is a group of people who govern something.
beginner.e: I have a meeting coming up with the Community Advisory Board.

beginner.m: If a piece of furniture, clothing, a room, etc. is comfortable, you feel comfortable in it (see 2.)
beginner.e: There were a few old but comfortable chairs in the meeting area.

beginner.m: A building for sick people, with doctors and nurses.
beginner.e: Mary had an accident. She will be in hospital for a week.

beginner.m: If something is uniform, there is no variation in it.
beginner.e: It was designed to be uniform from one end to the other.

beginner.m: A biscuit is a cookie.
beginner.e: He brought along homemade biscuits for the picnic.

beginner.m: A potato is a food that grows under the ground, which is round and white inside.
beginner.e: We usually eat meat and potatoes.

beginner.m: A book is a lot of paper joined together with writing and pictures printed on them for you to read or write in.
beginner.e: I borrow books from the library, and keep them in a bookcase.

beginner.m: Any noise; something that can be heard by the ears.
beginner.e: There was a loud sound.

beginner.m: An ancestor is a person from whom one is descended. A very similar word is forebear.
beginner.e: We get our customs from our ancestors.

beginner.m: If you arrive somewhere, you come to that place, usually the place that you planned to go to.
beginner.e: We arrive in New York at 10:52.

beginner.m: Help is the act of helping.
beginner.e: Will you please give me some help? This is hard for just one person to do.

beginner.m: A lake is a place with a lot of deep water. A lake not always have salt in it.
beginner.e: We went swimming in the lake.

beginner.m: A point is a position with no size, or a small dot.
beginner.e: These two lines meet at this point.

beginner.m: If someone is alone, they are not with other people.
beginner.e: She looked around to make sure that she was alone before opening the desk.

beginner.m: To ask is to look for an answer to a question by saying it.
beginner.e: She sure does ask a lot of questions!

beginner.m: The way a thing smells; the substance in the air that people can smell.
beginner.e: The smell of the flowers is very good.

beginner.m: Competition is a situation or event in which people or groups try to succeed over each other.
beginner.e: Brazil will play in this year's World Cup competition in Italy.

beginner.m: How big or small a thing is.
beginner.e: These shirts come in four sizes: small, medium, large, and extra large.

beginner.m: If you remember something that you did or knew before, you can think of it again.
beginner.e: He can't even remember where he left his books.

beginner.m: When you include something, you make it part of something else.
beginner.e: The store always includes the tax in their price.

beginner.m: Your pay is money you receive after doing something.
beginner.e: Go to the office to receive your pay.

beginner.m: If you communicate an idea, you make someone else understand your idea, usually by using words.
beginner.e: Parents have to work hard to communicate better with their children.

beginner.m: If someone is lazy, they do not want to work or do anything difficult.
beginner.e: I had a lazy dog who just slept on the sofa all day.

beginner.m: Business is the buying and selling of things or services.
beginner.e: The tax changes will be hard for small business.

beginner.m: A code is a set of rules or laws.
beginner.e: Section 244(1) (a) of the Canadian Criminal Code defines assault.

beginner.m: If something is short then there is a small distance from the bottom to the top. The opposite is tall.
beginner.e: I can't reach the table because I'm too short.

beginner.m: A rhythm is the part of music that drums do. It's the way music goes in time, without thinking about higher or lower notes.
beginner.e: A healthy heart beats with a steady rhythm.

beginner.m: A ticket is a piece of paper that allows you to enter a train, airplane, show, etc.
beginner.e: I bought my ticket to Mexico last week, but now I can't find it.

beginner.m: A gift is something given to another person voluntarily.
beginner.e: I didn't receive many gifts this Christmas.

beginner.m: If you decide something, there were different things you could do, but you choose one.
beginner.e: I haven't decided what to do yet.

beginner.m: Bags are containers made of soft material like paper, plastic or leather.
beginner.e: I put the garbage in a black plastic bag.

beginner.m: Behavior refers to the way that you behave. That is, the kind of things you do.
beginner.e: His behavior is bad.

beginner.m: When you terrify someone, you frighten the person greatly; to fill with terror.
beginner.e: The dogs terrify the cats.

beginner.m: A paragraph is one or more sentences that are written together with no line breaks separating them. Usually they are connected by a single idea.
beginner.e: She knew what it would say after reading the first paragraph.

beginner.m: A mouse is a very small animal that is similar to a small rat.
beginner.e: The mouse ran across the room.

beginner.m: The state of being free; the state of not being imprisoned or enslaved.
beginner.e: He enjoyed his freedom after he was released from prison.

beginner.m: If a piece of paper or something else is blank, it has nothing written on it.
beginner.e: I thought he would sign the check, but he left it blank.

beginner.m: If someone or something is alive, it is living or it continues to exist. If you are alive you have life.
beginner.e: The doctors tried to keep her alive, but she died an hour after arriving at the hospital.

beginner.m: If something is early, it is sooner than expected.
beginner.e: It was an early end to the meeting.

beginner.m: If something is elementary, it is basic and easy to understand.
beginner.e: The math problems are elementary for students in the first grade.

beginner.m: If people or things gather, they come together.
beginner.e: We gathered thousands of signatures to end the war.

beginner.m: To get to a temperature that a liquid lets out bubbles and gas at.
beginner.e: Water boils at 100°C.

beginner.m: Unusual or odd.
beginner.e: My brother is so strange that he can turn his eyelids inside out.

beginner.m: A road in a city with buildings on the sides and places where people can walk.
beginner.e: I saw a woman with a dog walking down the street.

beginner.m: A turkey is a bird that is often raised for food.
beginner.e: There was a spotting of a flock of wild turkeys in the forest.

beginner.m: A portrait is a painting or picture of a person's head and shoulders.
beginner.e: The portrait of the former queen sold for several million dollars.

beginner.m: Text is written language (often academic).
beginner.e: The text is OK, but we need to change the graphics before we publish.

beginner.m: To clone is to make an identical copy of something, especially a living being.
beginner.e: Cells usually reproduce by cloning themselves.

beginner.m: A blackboard is a large, flat piece of slate, typically hung in a classroom and written on with erasable chalk.
beginner.e: The teacher wrote the day's lesson on the blackboard.

beginner.m: A debate is an exchange of ideas looking at different sides of an issue.
beginner.e: The government's spending programme is the subject of much heated debate.

beginner.m: If someone is relaxed, they feel calm, they are not worried, and their muscles are not tight.
beginner.e: I feel most relaxed when I'm fishing.

beginner.m: If you are grateful for or about something, you want to say, "thank you" because of it.
beginner.e: I'm very grateful for your kindness during this difficult time.

beginner.m: A pro is somebody who is very good at what they do; short for professional.
beginner.e: She's real pro who cares about her job.

beginner.m: A solution is an answer to a problem.
beginner.e: The only solution is new regulations.

beginner.m: Treasure is a collection of valuable things, such as gold, diamonds, money, etc.
beginner.e: I felt like I was in a children's novel, or a story of hidden treasure.

beginner.m: Happening or coming before all other similar things or people.
beginner.e: I don't like the job much at first.

beginner.m: A mark is a single line left by a pen or pencil, or any small bit of color that got onto something.
beginner.e: You have a mark on your shirt from that tomato sauce you were eating.

beginner.m: Fairly is when something is between slightly and very.
beginner.e: The sun was shining brightly today, however the light breeze still made it feel fairly chilly.

beginner.m: If something finally happens, it means there was a long wait before it happened.
beginner.e: I finally finished university. Now, I can start my real life.

beginner.m: A reading is a spoken performance of something written.
beginner.e: The author was giving a reading of his new book.

beginner.m: If people or things are attractive, you like them because you think they are good, beautiful, etc.
beginner.e: I think that howard is a very attractive-looking man.

beginner.m: A championship is a contest to decide which person or team is best at the sport.
beginner.e: Gene Tunney won the world heavyweight boxing championship from Jack Dempsey.

beginner.m: To cause something is to make it happen.
beginner.e: His careless driving caused the car accident.

beginner.m: A ball is a round thing. People often use them to play games.
beginner.e: A ball is hit with a racquet in tennis.

beginner.m: If something is new, it is not old.
beginner.e: They had a new car.

beginner.m: A bottle is a container, usually made of glass that holds liquid and has a cap or stopper.
beginner.e: The bottle had a long, thin neck.

beginner.m: When you spend money, you give the money to buy something.
beginner.e: I spend too much at the book store each month.

beginner.m: Strength, energy, force, control. A quality that can make things happen.
beginner.e: His muscles have a lot of power.

beginner.m: A maker is someone who makes stuff.
beginner.e: Harley Davidson is a maker of motorcycles.

beginner.m: When a game is tied and no one has won, then the game is a draw.
beginner.e: The game ended 3 to 3. We were disappointed that it was a draw.

beginner.m: A scream is a loud noise made by a person.
beginner.e: A scream echoed out in the night.

beginner.m: Sunlight is light from the sun.
beginner.e: The sunlight is bright today.

beginner.m: Your cousin is the son or daughter of your aunt or uncle.
beginner.e: Every year at Christmas, I got to play with all my cousins at my grandma's house.

beginner.m: A yard is the area around a house.
beginner.e: The children went out to play in the yard.

beginner.m: Food that is eaten by animals.
beginner.e: Bird feed consists mainly of seeds.

beginner.m: A step is a movement of the foot
beginner.e: Take one step forward to win the game.

beginner.m: If something is exciting, it makes you feel happy and very awake.
beginner.e: Star Wars is the most exciting movie ever.

beginner.m: Heavily is a quality of heavy, a great weight, load, effort, or to a large amount.
beginner.e: In his plays, he borrowed heavily from Shakespeare.

beginner.m: A corner is the place where two lines or edges meet.
beginner.e: They live on the corner of Main Street and Dundas.

beginner.m: A summary is a short explanation of a longer idea, article, story, etc.
beginner.e: In this short time, I can provide only a summary of the work we have done.

beginner.m: Diamond is a very hard mineral made from carbon that is shiny like glass.
beginner.e: The blades of cutting tools like saws and knives are sometimes coated in diamond.

beginner.m: Today is the current day, the day that is happening now, the day between yesterday and tomorrow.
beginner.e: I have classes today.

beginner.m: A person moves a comb through their hair many times to make their hair look nice.
beginner.e: Joe always had a comb in his pocket.

beginner.m: If a person, animal, or plant is sick, it has a disease and is not healthy.
beginner.e: I'm sorry, I'm too sick to go to work today.

beginner.m: Practice is an activity you do again and again to improve your ability.
beginner.e: My driving is getting better, but I still need practice.

beginner.m: A measure of the time taken for the earth to circle the sun - any 12 month period
beginner.e: There are 365 days in a year and 366 days in leap years.

beginner.m: Not open.
beginner.e: The store is closed on the weekends.

beginner.m: Pepper is a kind of spice, usually black, that you put on food.
beginner.e: The pepper was so hot the boy could not eat it.

beginner.m: If something succeeds, it has happened the way somebody wants it to happen.
beginner.e: He succeeded in getting everyone to like him.

beginner.m: Something that is light in color is close to white.
beginner.e: The morning sky was very light.

beginner.m: A level is a place that is higher or lower than some other places.
