beginner.e: The room you want is on the third level of this building.

beginner.m: To talk
beginner.e: He speaks with him daily.

beginner.m: You use unfortunately to show that you feel something is not the way you wish it was.
beginner.e: Unfortunately, we didn't win.

beginner.m: A piece of land where people work growing plants and animals. Usually, a farm makes food for its owners to eat or sell.
beginner.e: We grow cows and apples on our farm.

beginner.m: A swim is when someone swims.
beginner.e: We all went for a swim in the lake.

beginner.m: When you sit, your body is not standing, but is in a position so that your bottom is on something.
beginner.e: I sit on a chair at the table.

beginner.m: If something is educational, it is related to education.
beginner.e: A school is an educational establishment.

beginner.m: A burn is an injury caused when you burn yourself.
beginner.e: The burn on my arm hurts.

beginner.m: Bones are the hard, white things inside your body. They give your body its shape.
beginner.e: How many bones did a dinosaur have?

beginner.m: A body is the main part of a person, animal, physical object, or organisation.
beginner.e: The governing body of the UN meets in Geneva.

beginner.m: A magazine is a publication that is printed regularly (usually weekly or monthly), and is often about a topic like a hobby, sports or news.
beginner.e: I get the magazine Cosmopolitan every month. I really like the articles it has on fashion and love.

beginner.m: If you greet someone or something, you meet them and say, "hello" or welcome them somehow.
beginner.e: The tour guide greeted us when we arrived at the airport.

beginner.m: If something is impossible it cannot happen or cannot be done.
beginner.e: It is impossible for people to breathe water.

beginner.m: A steak is thick slice of meat cut for roasting, usually beef.
beginner.e: This strip of steak is perfectly cooked!

beginner.m: Advertising is the business or study of using newspapers, TV, etc. to sell products or inform people.
beginner.e: There's too much advertising on radio.

beginner.m: When you are fit, you are healthy and able to do a task.
beginner.e: After he slept he looked very fit.

beginner.m: Paint is a liquid used to colour something
beginner.e: Sarah used pink paint to decorate the wall.

beginner.m: An elevator is a machine that moves people and goods up and down between floors of a building.
beginner.e: Take the elevator to floor 13.

beginner.m: When x makes or has contact with y, they touch each other physically.
beginner.e: The trains in Tokyo are so crowded that everyone has to stand in close contact to everyone else.

beginner.m: When you avoid something, you stay away from it or you don't do it.
beginner.e: Are you avoiding me?

beginner.m: If you carry something, you lift it up and move it to another place.
beginner.e: Let me carry those bags in for you.

beginner.m: If something is silly, it shows that somebody didn't think about it carefully.
beginner.e: People get excited about the silliest things.

beginner.m: A task is a specific piece of work, often unpleasant.
beginner.e: Come here, young man. I have a task for you to do.

beginner.m: A speaker is a person that speaks.
beginner.e: Bob is a native English speaker.

beginner.m: A matter is something that you can talk about or do something about a topic or a situation.
beginner.e: Try not to do anything to make matters worse.

beginner.m: Dinner is the largest meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening.
beginner.e: I'm sorry, I'll be late tonight, so I won't be home for dinner.

beginner.m: Used in negative statements to mean too or also.
beginner.e: I can't sing and I can't dance either.

beginner.m: If something always happens, it happens at all times or every time.
beginner.e: For all of my life, the sun has always risen every day.

beginner.m: Happiness is the emotion of being happy; joy.
beginner.e: I hope that your new job brings you happiness.

beginner.m: A snake is a long, thin reptile with no legs.
beginner.e: Some snakes will attack people, but most will try to hide or run away.

beginner.m: A university is a school of advanced study that offers both undergraduate and graduate classes.
beginner.e: A doctor studies for many years at a university before going to work in a hospital.

beginner.m: An ability is something that you can do.
beginner.e: I have a very good reading ability.

beginner.m: An elephant is a very large animal with two long teeth called tusks and a long nose called trunk.
beginner.e: Elephants live in both Asia and Africa.

beginner.m: If you are nervous, you are tense and worried about something.
beginner.e: I am nervous about my examinations.

beginner.m: If you say that maybe something will happen or that maybe it is true, you mean there is a chance of those things.
beginner.e: Maybe someday I'll learn how to drive.

beginner.m: A chili is a type of hot pepper, which may be eaten or used to make food spicy.
beginner.e: I used to grow chilies in a flowerpot in my window.

beginner.m: Someone who has good luck is someone who regularly has good things happen to them, almost as if by magic.
beginner.e: Many people believe the number 13 will bring you bad luck.

beginner.m: A team is a group of people who play or work together on the same side.
beginner.e: The operation was performed by a medical team led by Dr. Wood.

beginner.m: Something is necessary if people need it. It must happen or there will be a big problem.
beginner.e: It's necessary to stop when you see a red light.

beginner.m: An outer piece of clothing that covers the upper part of the body and the arms.
beginner.e: The woman wore a fur coat.

beginner.m: If you disagree, you do not agree. When two people disagree with each other, they have different ideas. They do not believe the same things are true.
beginner.e: I disagree with you.

beginner.m: Speed. A rate is how fast something happens. Something can go at a fast rate or a slow rate.
beginner.e: Her heart rate is 70 beats every minute.

beginner.m: Partners are people, usually two, who are together for a particular purpose, such as for business, sports, or a romantic relationship.
beginner.e: My partner, Tom, looks after the administrative parts of the business.

beginner.m: If something is direct, it is straight and as short as possible with nothing extra in between.
beginner.e: These improvement are a direct result of the recent changes.

beginner.m: You see something when you look at it with your eyes.
beginner.e: I can't see the words in this book because the writing is too small and I don't have my glasses.

beginner.m: A delay is a wait or the waiting time.
beginner.e: Computer problems caused a long delay in the meeting.

beginner.m: In science, pressure is force applied over an area.
beginner.e: It hurt when the doctor put pressure on her cut foot.

beginner.m: A pill is a small piece of medicine that is usually taken to cure illnesses.
beginner.e: Take pills only if you are ill.

beginner.m: A beginner is someone who has just started something and has little or no experience.
beginner.e: John is a beginner at football.

beginner.m: Affairs are things that happen or are done, usually that are important enough to be in the news.
beginner.e: The whole affair with Bill Clinton was a terrible mess.

beginner.m: A case is a container to hold something.
beginner.e: He opened the case and pulled out his violin.

beginner.m: Some help.
beginner.e: Can you please do me a favor by washing the dishes?

beginner.m: A college is a school for adults who have finished high school.
beginner.e: I graduated from college in 1992 when I was 22 years old.

beginner.m: If you have a choice, you can decide between two or more things or actions.
beginner.e: You have a choice of three cheeses.

beginner.m: If something is mostly true, empty, sunny, etc., it is close to 100% so.
beginner.e: The cup was mostly empty.

beginner.m: An alarm is a signal that something needs attention or a machine that makes the signal.
beginner.e: A fire in the fry pan set off the smoke alarm.

beginner.m: An indoor event happens in a building, not outside.
beginner.e: The gym has an indoor swimming pool.

beginner.m: Having a lot of weight.
beginner.e: This suitcase is very heavy.

beginner.m: When you say "you bring" something to someone, you carry it with you to that someone.
beginner.e: You bring lunch to me every day.

beginner.m: If you are intelligent, you can understand difficult ideas easily and think clearly.
beginner.e: Any intelligent person should be able to understand this.

beginner.m: If you freeze something, you cool it until it becomes solid.
beginner.e: Water freezes at 0°C.

beginner.m: If something is true, it is correct or real, not imagined or made up.
beginner.e: My wife is my one true love.

beginner.m: A drill is an object used to dig a hole.
beginner.e: He used the drill to make a hole on the wall.

beginner.m: The superlative form of bad; most bad.
beginner.e: Well, you've seen me at my worst.

beginner.m: A shadow is the dark area that is made when something blocks light, and that is shaped like the thing blocking the light.
beginner.e: I saw your shadow against the wall.

beginner.m: A boat is a vehicle used to travel on water.
beginner.e: We got wet on the boat ride.

beginner.m: If you need something, you want it and must have it.
beginner.e: Everyone needs food and water.

beginner.m: About physical health and medicine.
beginner.e: Dr. Barry was very creative in his teaching, research, and medical practice.

beginner.m: If something is little, its size is not big.
beginner.e: I just ate a tiny little piece of the cake.

beginner.m: If you play a musical instrument, you make music using it.
beginner.e: He plays guitar in a rock and roll band.

beginner.m: A ball game with two teams of five players. A goal is scored when a player throws the ball into a net (attached to a hoop) at each end of the court.
beginner.e: I play on my school's basketball team.

beginner.m: The amount of work that is done on something.
beginner.e: You should put more effort into your work.

beginner.m: You use x or else y to say that if x doesn't happen or isn't true, y would happen or would be true.
beginner.e: They don't want to be here or else they would have come.

beginner.m: If you accept something, you take it when somebody gives it to you.
beginner.e: She accepted the award.

beginner.m: Something unimportant is not important, it is minor or petty.
beginner.e: He had to know the starting time, but the other details were unimportant.

beginner.m: If you allow something, you let it happen; you say it's OK.
beginner.e: I allow food in my car.

beginner.m: The day you were born.
beginner.e: My birthday is September 14, 1972.

beginner.m: Magic has to do with making things happen in ways that are not physical, and might be called supernatural.
beginner.e: The fairy god mother used magic to turn mice into horses.

beginner.m: A grandfather is the father of a person or animal's parent.
beginner.e: My grandfather was very old when I was still a boy.

beginner.m: A chair is a piece of furniture for one person to sit on.
beginner.e: Please, pull up a chair and sit down.

beginner.m: If you are merry you feel happy.
beginner.e: We were all feeling very merry that night.

beginner.m: A chairman is the person who controls a meeting or an organization.
beginner.e: Alan Eastwood is the former chairman of the Police Federation.

beginner.m: Being separate means that a piece of an object is not connected to or attached to the rest of the object.
beginner.e: This chair was broken into five separate pieces.

beginner.m: A block is a hard piece of material, usually with six smooth sides.
beginner.e: When I was young, I liked building things with wooden blocks.

beginner.m: An appointment is a formal agreement to meet or visit someone (for example, a doctor) at a certain time and place.
beginner.e: I have a doctor's appointment at 3:00 tomorrow.

beginner.m: If something happens gradually, it happens in a gradual manner.
beginner.e: The everyday lifes of the citizens gradually went back to normal after the earthquake.

beginner.m: Prepared.
beginner.e: Let's get ready to rumble!

beginner.m: An exhibition is a public display of objects or products.
beginner.e: There was an art exhibition on in the town hall.

beginner.m: If you hit someone or something, then you touch them hard and fast.
beginner.e: The red car was turning when the blue car hit it.

beginner.m: A film is a recording of a moving picture that tells stories including actors, directors, and producers.
beginner.e: Let's go to the theatre and watch a film.

beginner.m: Bread is food made from mixing flour, water, and yeast.
beginner.e: Small children love eating bread and butter.

beginner.m: A scene is a place where something happened.
beginner.e: Police found a gun near the crime scene.

beginner.m: If something is modern, it happened in current times.
beginner.e: The new house has all modern conveniences.

beginner.m: A game is something that people do to have fun.
beginner.e: Shall we play a game?

beginner.m: When you have a thought, you have an idea or concept in your mind.
beginner.e: I have a thought about the answer to that problem.

beginner.m: If you have permission to do something, then the person who has authority over you or over that thing allows you to do it.
beginner.e: My father gave me permission to go to the city.

beginner.m: A bride is a wife, the female partner in a marriage. Most used for the period of time around the marriage ceremony.
beginner.e: Jill was the bride, and Jack was the bridegroom.

beginner.m: A toilet is something you may put human waste (feces and urine) into.
beginner.e: Excuse me, I need to use the toilet.

beginner.m: You use actually to say that something is real; in fact; really.
beginner.e: Actually, I had nothing to do with that incident.

beginner.m: If you pursue a job or hobby, you do it for a long time.
beginner.e: The band motivated her to pursue a career in music.

beginner.m: A great object or event is very big and large in scale.
beginner.e: A great storm is approaching our shores.

beginner.m: If something is tall, there is a long distance from the bottom to the top.
beginner.e: There are too many tall buildings in Toronto.

beginner.m: If you explore a possibility, plan, idea, etc. you think about it carefully.
beginner.e: This is just an introduction. We will explore the ideas further in the next chapter.

beginner.m: Regularly is when something is done often.
beginner.e: I go there quite regularly.

beginner.m: A doubt is a question or uncertainty about something.
beginner.e: His mind was full of doubts about the phishing website.

beginner.m: Smoke is the gray or black substance that goes up into the air when something burns.
beginner.e: The smoke from that factory is making me sick.

beginner.m: When you pack something, you put it in a container to carry with you.
beginner.e: Did you pack your swimming suit?

beginner.m: An image is something you can see or imagine that looks like the real thing.
beginner.e: Many people have an image of God as an old man.

beginner.m: A pig is a mammal.
beginner.e: On this farm, we have over 200 pigs, but no cows or horses.

beginner.m: If you appreciate something, you understand its value or its qualities
beginner.e: It's hard to appreciate how difficult the job is until you try it yourself.

beginner.m: The direction opposite to north. For a person looking at the setting sun, the south is on their left hand.
beginner.e: The wind usually comes from the south.

beginner.m: Very much, or to a great degree.
beginner.e: He's not just a little bit better; he's far better.

beginner.m: A disadvantage is something that is a handicap or a weakness.
beginner.e: The hockey team had a disadvantage against its opponents because its goalie was not good.

beginner.m: An association is a way that two things are similar, belong together, or are connected or related.
beginner.e: I don't see any association between what happened to you and what happened to me.

beginner.m: When you begin something, you start to do the first part of a longer action.
beginner.e: A journey always begins with a first step.

beginner.m: The superlative form of good; most good.
beginner.e: It's best if you go now.

beginner.m: The solution of a mathematical equation.
beginner.e: The result of 1 + 1 is 2.

beginner.m: An airport is a place where airplanes land and take off.
beginner.e: I took a taxi to the airport for my flight to London.

beginner.m: If you are successful, you are effective at something.
beginner.e: The successful business man knows how to get money for his work.

beginner.m: In school, a course is a class in a specific subject.
beginner.e: The science course was very difficult.

beginner.m: A textbook is a book that is used in school, university, or college to study an academic topic.
beginner.e: I had to bring my math textbook home so I could do my homework.

beginner.m: A strategy is a planned way to do something.
beginner.e: The new government is likely to change the economic strategy because the old strategy clearly isn't working.

beginner.m: The third thing is the one that is number three (3) in order.
beginner.e: I have two older brothers. I'm the third child.

beginner.m: The plural form of person; more than one (kind of) person.
beginner.e: Who are these people at the party?

beginner.m: Meat is the muscle of animals that we eat. Beef, chicken, and pork are kinds of meat.
beginner.e: You should cook the meat at 135 to 140°C.

beginner.m: Software is a computer program.
beginner.e: This wiki runs the MediaWiki software available from MediaWiki.org.

beginner.m: To be average is to be not one extreme or another.
beginner.e: In football, he is an average player.

beginner.m: If you survive something, you experience it and you did not die.
beginner.e: They survived the war but died two years later.

beginner.m: If someone is violent, they act physically to hurt people or break things.
beginner.e: Police said he had a history of violent behavior.

beginner.m: A room is a place which is part of a building. Someone is able to see other people who are in the same room.
beginner.e: We need a long, wide room because many people will be at the meeting.

beginner.m: If you bury something, you put it into the ground and cover it.
beginner.e: John was buried near Washington, D.C.

beginner.m: A computer is a machine that helps you store, organize, and use information.
beginner.e: If you're looking at a web page, you must be using a computer.

beginner.m: By a good chance.
beginner.e: Happily, the situation today is very different.

beginner.m: A park is an outdoor area where people can relax and play.
beginner.e: We sat under the trees and had lunch in Central Park.

beginner.m: If you buy something, you give money and the thing becomes yours.
beginner.e: I can't afford to buy a new house.

beginner.m: The difficulty of something is how hard it is to do.
beginner.e: The student finished the homework with great difficulty.

beginner.m: If something is straight, it does not bend, or turn. It continues in one direction.
beginner.e: He had had too much to drink and couldn't walk in a straight line.

beginner.m: If a day is sunny, you can see the sun clearly in the sky and there is a lot of sunshine.
beginner.e: I'll go for a walk later if it is sunny; if not, I'll stay in my flat.

beginner.m: If you are polite, you treat people nicely and follow the social rules of your group.
beginner.e: Susie is more polite than her sister Cindy.

beginner.m: A reader is somebody or something that reads.
beginner.e: We got a new card reader for the door.

beginner.m: The quality of being different.
beginner.e: You need to learn to accept differences in people.

beginner.m: If something is dirty, it has dirt on it, or it is not clean.
beginner.e: After playing outside all day, her hands were all dirty.

beginner.m: A slide is a structure, usually on a playground, that you slide down.
beginner.e: He made a splash by entering the pool on a water slide.

beginner.m: A range of X is a number of different kinds of Xs
beginner.e: We offer you a whole range of clothes, from socks to hats.

beginner.m: A pen is a writing tool that uses ink.
beginner.e: He picked up his ballpoint pen, crossed out some words.

beginner.m: A pilot is a person who flies and controls an airplane.
beginner.e: I hope the pilot does not crash the plane.

beginner.m: A seed is a small round thing that can grow to be a plant, a flower or a tree.
beginner.e: She put the seeds into the ground in the garden so that food and flowers would grow.

beginner.m: The plural form of penny; more than one (kind of) penny.
beginner.e: These apples are twenty pence each.

intermediate.m: If you protect something or someone, you keep it safe; you stop it from being harmed.
intermediate.e: The knight protected the castle.

intermediate.m: A relation is the way two things are towards each other or in comparison with each other.
intermediate.e: There is a relation between eating good food and being healthy.

intermediate.m: If something or someone is fierce, then they are violent or aggressive.
intermediate.e: The dinosaur was fierce.

intermediate.m: If something lingers, it stays or remains in a place or situation.
intermediate.e: The taste of spices lingered in my mouth.

intermediate.m: A regulation is a rule or a control.
intermediate.e: The company has recently imposed new safety rules and regulations to reduce accidents.

intermediate.m: A seller is a person or thing that sells stuff.
intermediate.e: That man is a seller of unusual items.

intermediate.m: A leap is a jump.
intermediate.e: The clown took a leap through the hoop.

intermediate.m: When something is crucial, it is very important. It will make a big difference. You cannot succeed without it.
intermediate.e: Iron plays a crucial role in moving oxygen around the body.

intermediate.m: When something is vacant, it is unused, unoccupied or empty.
intermediate.e: That room has been vacant since my uncle moved out of the house.

intermediate.m: A carpet is a floor covering, usually made of nylon or wool.
intermediate.e: He walked in with his boots leaving snow on the carpet.

intermediate.m: If someone resigns from a job, they quit it.
intermediate.e: He resigned his job when his fellow workers were attacked.

intermediate.m: An interaction is when two or more things affect each other or work together.
intermediate.e: She should have a lot of interaction with other students, or with the teacher.

intermediate.m: If something is done in an orderly fashion or manner, it works very well as expected.
intermediate.e: He packed up his things in a very orderly fashion and left the next day.

intermediate.m: A dimension is a part of a problem, issue, or situation.
intermediate.e: The baby has added a new dimension to our lives.

intermediate.m: If someone has patience, they can wait without feeling upset.
intermediate.e: Andrew has so much patience with the children; I just get so angry with them.

intermediate.m: Administrative staff or positions are those related to organizing and managing a company or institution.
intermediate.e: The teacher was removed from teaching duties and placed in an administrative position.

intermediate.m: Luggage is a bag that contains a traveller's belongings.
intermediate.e: Alan just lost his green luggage and is asking the staff at the airport for help.

intermediate.m: Someone lifts something when they use their hands to make the thing go up.
intermediate.e: He is lifting some suitcases.

intermediate.m: A crease is a line or mark made by folding something that is soft.
intermediate.e: He forgot to iron his shirt on that day and went to work with many creases on his shirt.

intermediate.m: A little; to a very small degree.
intermediate.e: The two pictures look very similar, but they are slightly different.

intermediate.m: If you recommend something, you tell somebody that it is good or that they should try it.
intermediate.e: The committee strongly recommended that the head teacher take the lead in defining the aims of the school.

intermediate.m: The main thing is the most important or biggest one.
intermediate.e: There are many problems, but the main one is money.

intermediate.m: If you impose something on someone, you force it on them, even if they don't want it.
intermediate.e: The law imposes a duty on all employers to provide safety training.

intermediate.m: Lettuce is a round green vegetable.
intermediate.e: There is lettuce, cabbage, and beans in this salad.

intermediate.m: An emperor is the male leader or monarch of an empire.
intermediate.e: The coronation of the Japanese emperor happened this year.

intermediate.m: A sort is a kind or type.
intermediate.e: Red and green are two sorts of apple.

intermediate.m: If something is suppressed, it is eliminated, stopped, or held back.
intermediate.e: I struggled to suppress my smile.

intermediate.m: A person who is optimistic expects the best in all possible ways.
intermediate.e: He is very optimistic about his plans that they will succeed.

intermediate.m: Relating to agriculture
intermediate.e: Few safety regulations are available to protect agricultural workers.

intermediate.m: If a group of people is divided, it cannot agree.
intermediate.e: Teachers were very divided over the new textbooks.

intermediate.m: If you enhance something, you make it bigger or better.
intermediate.e: He can greatly enhance his reputation by winning tonight.

intermediate.m: The act or process of expanding.
intermediate.e: The expansion of metals and plastics in response to heat is well understood.

intermediate.m: Something that is conventional is what is generally done, believed, or ordinary.
intermediate.e: I prefer more conventional clothing.

intermediate.m: When something happens precisely, it happens in an exact and precise manner.
intermediate.e: The egg flew out the window and landed precisely on Mr. Norton's bald head.

intermediate.m: An edit is a change in text or a document.
intermediate.e: Thank you for your edit to the page hello on the Simple English Wiktionary!

intermediate.m: A provision is an item that is kept by a person that he needs to support himself for the future.
intermediate.e: He kept a provision of food with him for the trip.

intermediate.m: Lava is the molten rock that is spit out of a volcano when it erupts.
intermediate.e: When the volcano erupted, it spit out lots of lava.

intermediate.m: An adult male cattle.
intermediate.e: The bull was kept away from the cows.

intermediate.m: A grain is a seed that people eat, such as wheat, rice, corn, etc.
intermediate.e: Most North Americans get their grains from bread and pasta.

intermediate.m: A sweet fruit.
intermediate.e: You need to take the pit out of that peach.

intermediate.m: Incorrect things are wrong, or not correct.
intermediate.e: He got points off for an incorrect answer on the quiz.

intermediate.m: A count is the number of something.
intermediate.e: Our new-student count is now up to 124, five more students than last time.

intermediate.m: A temporary group that is formed for a particular reason.
intermediate.e: The two governments formed a coalition to help their workers.

intermediate.m: A hop is a small jump.
intermediate.e: Make a hop over the fence and a skip over the brook.

intermediate.m: If you lower something, you move it down.
intermediate.e: The man was lowered into the hole on a rope, so he could save the child.

intermediate.m: If something is rare, you seldom see it or there are only a few.
intermediate.e: It's rare to have snow in June.

intermediate.m: Compared to something else.
intermediate.e: I feel good relative to yesterday.

intermediate.m: An inscription is the words cut into or printed on a stone or other surface.
intermediate.e: The inscription says he died 100 years ago.

intermediate.m: A librarian is a person who manages a library.
intermediate.e: You can ask the librarian to help you find the book.

intermediate.m: An interpretation is an attempt to understand something.
intermediate.e: Weather forecasters use a lot of data, but the interpretation of the data is very difficult.

intermediate.m: A perspective is a way of looking at or thinking about something.
intermediate.e: He has to look at everything from an international perspective.

intermediate.m: Heavenly things are related to heaven in some religions.
intermediate.e: Heavenly choirs sing the praises of Jesus.

intermediate.m: A remark is your spoken opinion or observation about something.
intermediate.e: He made some very interesting remarks about what he expects in Iraq.

intermediate.m: If something is valid, it is correct, appropriate, and acceptable.
intermediate.e: To log in, you need a valid password.

intermediate.m: If you interpret something, you understand a particular meaning in it, and may explain that meaning to others.
intermediate.e: Children's behaviour can often be difficult to interpret.

intermediate.m: If someone or something is unfit for a role or purpose, they do not have the correct requirements for it.
intermediate.e: Jack cannot run, making him unfit for the track team.

intermediate.m: A terrorist is a person who uses terror and violence to get political change.
intermediate.e: The car bomb at the busy market was the work of a terrorist.

intermediate.m: To violate means to break something like a law.
intermediate.e: A person violated the copyright of a book.

intermediate.m: If you arrange something, you put it in order or you organise it.
intermediate.e: I will arrange for a car to meet you at the airport.

intermediate.m: A type of meat-eating bird.
intermediate.e: He saw an eagle perched on top of that tree.

intermediate.m: An individual person or thing is looked at separately from others.
intermediate.e: This office assists whole families rather than individual family members.

intermediate.m: If you compete for something, you are working against other people to get it.
intermediate.e: He competed but failed to win a medal in the 1928 Olympics in Amsterdam.

intermediate.m: A pension is money paid regularly by a government or company to someone who has stopped working, usually because of age or illness.
intermediate.e: He regularly puts money into a retirement pension plan.

intermediate.m: When you underestimate something, you think of it to be smaller or less important than it really is
intermediate.e: Do not underestimate our new colleague, he used to be under the President's scholarship to study overseas.

intermediate.m: If you retrieve something, you go and get it back.
intermediate.e: The clerk retrieved the item from the back room.

intermediate.m: The minimum is the lowest number, size, amount, etc. that exists, that is allowed, or that is possible.
intermediate.e: Try to keep drinking to a minimum at school.

intermediate.m: A reflection is an image made by reflected light, such as what you see in a mirror.
intermediate.e: Narcissus fell in love with his own reflection.

intermediate.m: A specialty is something that a person is an expert in.
intermediate.e: They cook well overall, but their true specialty is pasta.

intermediate.m: A feast is a large meal.
intermediate.e: They had a big feast to celebrate the family reunion.

intermediate.m: Not willing to share someone/something; wanting to control someone/something.
intermediate.e: He is very possessive of his car and won't let anyone else drive it.

intermediate.m: Underwear is a piece of clothing that you wear under your clothes next to your skin.
intermediate.e: I got out of the shower, dried myself, and put on some underwear.

intermediate.m: A toll is money you must pay to use a facility.
intermediate.e: A toll house was used to collect toll (payment) to travel on a road.

intermediate.m: When there is a similarity between things, they are the same in one or more ways.
intermediate.e: There is a strong similarity between what happened here and what happened at the other schools.

intermediate.m: A horn is a long, sharp thing that grows on the head of some animals such as goats and sheep.
intermediate.e: The goat used its horn to break the fence.

intermediate.m: A nutrient is a something that is eaten for nourishment or energy.
intermediate.e: Nuts and berries are healthy: they are full of nutrients.

intermediate.m: Having to do with athletes.
intermediate.e: Are you a member of the American Athletic Association?

intermediate.m: An analogy is a likeness or a comparison between two things that have some features that are the same and others which are different.
intermediate.e: Several quite obvious analogies between the two authors can be made.

intermediate.m: If you delete something, you remove or get rid of, or erase it, especially written or printed material, or data on a computer.
intermediate.e: I will delete the first paragraph of my essay from the file.

intermediate.m: A compliment is a few words of praise: saying that someone or something is good in some way.
intermediate.e: William gave me a compliment and that made me feel good. He told me my hair was nice.

intermediate.m: A rental is something that is rented.
intermediate.e: The price includes accommodation and car rental.

intermediate.m: Critique or the expression thereof.
intermediate.e: Their marriage received a lot of criticism from their families.

intermediate.m: A small piece that is broken off of a larger object.
intermediate.e: A chip of paint fell off the wall.

intermediate.m: A debit is a written record of a debt in an account book.
intermediate.e: I wrote the amount he owed into the debit column of the account book.

intermediate.m: If something is nasty it is very bad.
intermediate.e: Her nasty behavior caused much trouble.

intermediate.m: Evacuation is the act of evacuating.
intermediate.e: There was an emergency evacuation when the fire alarm rang.

intermediate.m: If an activity is legal it does not break any laws.
intermediate.e: In Canada, it is perfectly legal for a woman to walk down the street with no shirt on.

intermediate.m: A champion is someone who has been a winner in a contest.
intermediate.e: I was the race and so now I am this year's champion.

intermediate.m: Or (singular) Relief is the good feeling you have when something bad is finished or didn't happen.
intermediate.e: I smiled with relief and thanks.

intermediate.m: A bomber is a person that sets bombs.
intermediate.e: The bomber was caught by the police before he could detonate the explosives.

intermediate.m: A minor change, problem, injury, etc. is not very important.
intermediate.e: We still have to make a few minor changes, but it's mostly done.

intermediate.m: When something is hasty, it is done in haste, very quickly or in a hurried manner.
intermediate.e: Without taking time to think about it, they made a hasty decision to take up the project.

intermediate.m: If you are somewhere firstly, you are the earliest.
intermediate.e: The gardener arrived at the office firstly.

intermediate.m: A spray is a fine and gentle mist of liquid.
intermediate.e: I need to get a spray to freshen up the house.

intermediate.m: If something is done impatiently, it is done without patience.
intermediate.e: Stella was waiting impatiently for the delivery to come.

intermediate.m: If someone is hospitalized, they are admitted into a hospital for treatment.
intermediate.e: My friend was hospitalized as he had a severe car accident.

intermediate.m: Opposition to something, is an action or hope to stop it.
intermediate.e: There was strong opposition to the change from parents.

intermediate.m: If you analyze something, you study it carefully to understand it, often to see what it is made of.
intermediate.e: The dust was analyzed to determine its chemical contents.

intermediate.m: A purchase is something that you have bought.
intermediate.e: Since the purchase of Columbia Pictures by Sony, the US has been very afraid of Japan.

intermediate.m: When you float, it means that your density is lower than the density of the liquid you are in, which makes you be at the surface of the liquid.
intermediate.e: As I have a light body, I always float when I go swimming.

intermediate.m: Something is invisible when we can not see it.
intermediate.e: The magician made the woman invisible.

intermediate.m: A metaphor is a way of talking about one thing by using the language usually used for something else to show some kind of similarity between them.
intermediate.e: We say "spend time" because of the metaphor "time is money".

intermediate.m: A server is a type of computer that people can access through the Internet to visit a website.
intermediate.e: I recently bought a server to host my online shop.

intermediate.m: A recipe is a set of instructions and a list of things (called ingredients) you need to make an item of food.
intermediate.e: I have a great recipe for cookies right here.

intermediate.m: Something that is causing debate, causing talk and discussion.
intermediate.e: The latest book about UFOs has been very controversial.

intermediate.m: Brass is a shiny yellow-orange metal.
intermediate.e: The brass chest only has one key.

intermediate.m: An organization is a group of people with a particular purpose (e.g., teams, clubs, churches, etc.)
intermediate.e: The daycare is operated by a voluntary organization of parents and teachers.

intermediate.m: A thing has a characteristic trait if it is typical for its group.
intermediate.e: Red is a characteristic color of a rose.

intermediate.m: When you bathe, you clean yourself with water.
intermediate.e: I bathe at least two times a day to keep myself clean and refreshed.

intermediate.m: A settler is someone who settles in a new location.
intermediate.e: The new settler was surprised to see the problems of the area.

intermediate.m: You exhibit something when you show it to others.
intermediate.e: He exhibited the new product to the audience.

intermediate.m: Something that is above the everyday, above the ordinary, more than ordinary, spectacular.
intermediate.e: It was extraordinary opportunity to make money.

intermediate.m: If you cultivate a crop, you grow it.
intermediate.e: By 3,600 years ago, farmers were cultivating cereals at a high altitude.

intermediate.m: A wreck is what is left of something that has been seriously damaged.
intermediate.e: The wreck of the Titanic was found on the bottom of the sea.

intermediate.m: If you are confronted with something, you come face to face with it.
intermediate.e: The man confronted the burglar.

intermediate.m: An insane idea is very strange, like something a crazy person might think of.
intermediate.e: That has got to be the most insane thing I have ever heard.

intermediate.m: If a thing is dim, it is not bright.
intermediate.e: It is hard to see in a room where the lights are dim.

intermediate.m: Hearty means to have good health and vigor.
intermediate.e: My grandfather was a hearty man who enjoyed outdoor sports.

intermediate.m: A strong feeling of hurt or discomfort
intermediate.e: He was in pain, because his leg was broken.

intermediate.m: Extensive research, experience, damage, etc. is large in size, amount, or degree.
intermediate.e: After the wild fires, the damage was extensive.

intermediate.m: If something is absorbed, it is sucked or soaked up (usually a liquid).
intermediate.e: The sponge absorbed the spilled water.

intermediate.m: The ribs are a number of bones just below the shoulder that wrap around the top of the torso that protect the lungs and heart.
intermediate.e: A broken rib is generally treated by putting a bandage several times around the chest and the back.

intermediate.m: If someone is depressed, they have the condition called depression - they are very sad and cannot imagine being happy in the future.
intermediate.e: No one knows why it happened, but last year, Jay became depressed.

intermediate.m: A clinic is a place to see the doctor for health checkups or to buy medicine.
intermediate.e: He felt ill yesterday, so he had to visit the clinic to buy some medicine.

intermediate.m: A trophy is a special item given for winning a contest or competition.
intermediate.e: John is very talented. He has won many trophies from different competitions all over the world.

intermediate.m: A reward is something good that is given after an act.
intermediate.e: I got extra money as a reward for working hard.

intermediate.m: A vitamin is something that we need in our food to help us live, that is different from protein, carbohydrates, fat or minerals.
intermediate.e: Eat good food with vitamins in it to stay healthy.

intermediate.m: Denim is a tough cloth made from cotton, and often used to make jeans and jackets.
intermediate.e: My trousers were made out of denim.

intermediate.m: When you speak of clothes in general, you speak of clothing.
intermediate.e: You need to wear warm clothing in the winter.

intermediate.m: A slope is one side of a hill.
intermediate.e: We will have to climb up this slope to get to the top of the hill.

intermediate.m: Multiple items are more than one item.
intermediate.e: We ran into multiple problems, but we solved them all.

intermediate.m: When someone hesitates, they have doubts about something and therefore do not act, or stop the action.
intermediate.e: He hesitated for a while before signing the contract.

intermediate.m: If you exalt a person, you honor and respect them.
intermediate.e: They exalted their queen.

intermediate.m: If something is ambiguous, it has more than one possible meaning, state, or explanation.
intermediate.e: The goal of the challenge remains rather ambiguous.

intermediate.m: A replica is a close copy of something, usually of a famous or expensive item.
intermediate.e: I have a replica of an ancient coin.

intermediate.m: Having a strong feeling of interest.
intermediate.e: John showed a lot of enthusiasm when he started his new job.

intermediate.m: A master is someone who controls something.
intermediate.e: She is the master of this domain.

intermediate.m: If you imply something, you mean it, but you don't say it directly.
intermediate.e: By saying I should exercise more, she implied that I'm fat.

intermediate.m: If something is eternal, it does not end.
intermediate.e: He said his love for her was eternal.

intermediate.m: Two things coincide with each other if they're both in the same place or at the same time.
intermediate.e: The time of your party coincides with my niece's wedding, so I can't come.

intermediate.m: If there is an outbreak, a disease suddenly appears in an area and spreads.
intermediate.e: It was the first measles outbreak in the area in thirty years.

intermediate.m: If you translate something from one language to another, you change the words and sentences into the other language.
intermediate.e: It's not enough to translate word for word.

intermediate.m: About the citizens of a country, especially as opposed to the government, army, police, religion, etc.
intermediate.e: This comes under civil, rather than criminal, law.

intermediate.m: An allegation is a claim or a statement that is not proven and may or may not be true.
intermediate.e: They were arrested on allegations of trying to tamper with the evidence.

intermediate.m: If something is silent, there is no sound. It is unheard.
intermediate.e: The candidates were silent during the exam.

intermediate.m: A destination is the place where a person or thing will go.
intermediate.e: The package's destination was across the country.

intermediate.m: A vehicle is something that moves people or things from one place to another, for example: cars, planes, boats, etc.
intermediate.e: Bicycles and wheelchairs are allowed. All other vehicles must stay off the path.

intermediate.m: Carelessness is a lack of care.
intermediate.e: The accident was caused by a driver's carelessness.

intermediate.m: If something is revolutionary, it causes great change.
intermediate.e: Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin was revolutionary.

intermediate.m: Trust is faith or belief in someone.
intermediate.e: Your parents have trust in you.

intermediate.m: If something shatters, it suddenly breaks into very small pieces.
intermediate.e: The wine glass shattered when I dropped it.

intermediate.m: A rug is a piece of cloth used to cover the floor, just like a carpet.
intermediate.e: My sister bought a new rug for the living room.

intermediate.m: Property is a thing or things that belong to someone; things that someone owns.
intermediate.e: This house is now my property. I've finished paying for it.

intermediate.m: An injury is when someone or an animal is hurt; when something has caused a person or an animal to be harmed.
intermediate.e: She suffered serious injuries to her face and chest in the car crash.

intermediate.m: Corporal acts, like punishment, involve the body rather than the mind or spirit.
intermediate.e: Schools once used corporal punishment to discipline students.

intermediate.m: A sidewalk is a long piece of ground beside a road for walking on.
intermediate.e: It is safer to walk on the sidewalk than on the road.

intermediate.m: To burst something, most commonly a balloon.
intermediate.e: The boy used a needle to pop the balloon.

intermediate.m: If something is worthwhile, it is good and important enough to spend time, effort, or money on it.
intermediate.e: Doing volunteer work to help others is really worthwhile.

intermediate.m: If something is persuasive, it is easy to believe.
intermediate.e: That ad is persuasive.

intermediate.m: A process is a series of steps that you take for a particular purpose.
intermediate.e: Let us look at the factors considered during the formal decision-making process.

intermediate.m: A cherry is a roundish small piece of fruit with a core inside. Its color varies from pale yellow to red or purple and even nearly black.
intermediate.e: We should eat our cherries quickly before birds get them all eaten!

intermediate.m: If you regulate something, you control it by making laws and rules.
intermediate.e: The state maintains the power to regulate all schools.

intermediate.m: A substance like air, made of water that is very hot.
intermediate.e: The food is hot -- I see steam coming from the pot.

intermediate.m: A man who works, especially one employed in manual or industrial labor.
intermediate.e: The workman repaired the brick wall with great care.

intermediate.m: A foreman is a worker, especially a man, who supervises and directs other workers.
intermediate.e: The foreman told his employees to get back to work.

intermediate.m: A department is a part of a business, school, hospital or other institution that has a particular job.
intermediate.e: He was in the Department of Law at the Keele University for nearly 20 years.

intermediate.m: If something is priceless, it is so valuable or special that nobody would try to sell it.
intermediate.e: Having a good friendship is priceless, so treasure it!

intermediate.m: A merchant is someone who sells goods.
intermediate.e: The merchant at the market made a fortune today!

intermediate.m: Hospitality is the friendly and helpful treatment of guests or visitors.
intermediate.e: They showed great hospitality by offering food and a place to stay.

intermediate.m: You use considerably when you want to make a comparative adjective stronger.
intermediate.e: Sharks are considerably faster swimmers than humans.

intermediate.m: A reform is a change to an institution's rules or ways something works to improve it.
intermediate.e: We have implemented additional reforms to make it easier to apply.

intermediate.m: If you agonize over/about a difficult decision or choice, you find making it very difficult, almost painful.
intermediate.e: Don't spend hours or days agonizing about what to do.

intermediate.m: A messenger is somebody that delivers a message
intermediate.e: The messenger told him that there was a meeting tomorrow.

intermediate.m: Land is the part of the Earth that is not covered with water
intermediate.e: The surface of Earth is 70% water, and 30% land.

intermediate.m: When something is compulsory, it is required and has to be followed.
intermediate.e: In most countries, it is compulsory to vote during elections and failing to do so is a crime.

intermediate.m: A spokeswoman is someone that speaks for a group of people.
intermediate.e: Please speak to our spokeswoman if you have any questions.

intermediate.m: When you reconsider something, you think it over again; you think about changing your mind.
intermediate.e: When he realized the temperature outside was below freezing, Pierre reconsidered his plan to go for a run.

intermediate.m: If something is coastal, it is related to the coast or is located near the coast.
intermediate.e: Going to the beach for the coastal breeze is a way of relaxing.

intermediate.m: A dose is a measured amount of medicine that is taken at one time.
intermediate.e: Eat a dose of one spoonful of this cough medicine after every meal.

intermediate.m: A particle is a very small, tiny piece.
intermediate.e: His eye hurt because a particle of dust had got into it.

intermediate.m: A measure of how much material is in something.
intermediate.e: The Earth has much more mass than the moon.

intermediate.m: Entirely refers to the full extent of doing something. It is another word for totally or completely.
intermediate.e: It is entirely up to you on how you intend to get help for your project. I am only here to give advice.

intermediate.m: An avenue is a wide street, often bordered by trees.
intermediate.e: They used to live at 123 Derbyshire Avenue.

intermediate.m: If you do something frequently, you do it often.
intermediate.e: The library is frequently used by students.

intermediate.m: A pulse is a rhythmic, soft beating of the arteries, for example, as felt in the wrists
intermediate.e: He checked her pulse and discovered that her heart was racing.

intermediate.m: Loyalty is the quality or state of a person or group of persons being loyal to someone or something.
intermediate.e: The Germans exhibited great loyalty to Hitler during his rule in Germany.

intermediate.m: A notion is an idea about something.
intermediate.e: The film questions the standard notions of right and wrong.

intermediate.m: The word consequently is used show what happened as a result or consequence of an event.
intermediate.e: He did not wake up early in the morning. Consequently, he was late to work.

intermediate.m: If something is urgent, it needs attention quickly.
intermediate.e: An urgent appeal was sent out for assistance.

intermediate.m: If you adopt something, you choose and begin to use it instead of what you used in the past.
intermediate.e: When she moved out west, she adopted a new name.

intermediate.m: If you respond to something or someone, you do something in reaction to it.
intermediate.e: The police responded forcefully to the problems.

intermediate.m: An apology is words or actions that show you are sorry.
intermediate.e: Japan has never offered an official apology for Pearl Harbor.

intermediate.m: A distance in space or in time.
intermediate.e: There is a ten-minute interval between classes.

intermediate.m: The scope of a book, a law, a duty, etc. is how much is included or how far it can go.
intermediate.e: The small budget has limited the scope of the research.

intermediate.m: Your client is a person or group that uses your services or buys your products.
intermediate.e: As lawyers, we advise our clients not to talk to the media.

intermediate.m: A banker is someone who works at a bank and helps in managing the money and finances of people.
intermediate.e: My Aunt is a banker.

intermediate.m: If something is industrial, it has something to do with industry.
intermediate.e: Factories are industrial buildings.

intermediate.m: Having a cutting edge; not dull.
intermediate.e: He has a sharp knife.

intermediate.m: A piece of cloth to clean dirty stuff, usually dirty.
intermediate.e: Use that dirty rag over there to wipe this mess.

intermediate.m: A clumsy object or idea is one created without much planning.
intermediate.e: This solution is clumsy. I do not think it will work.

intermediate.m: When you execute an action, you carry it out.
intermediate.e: The soldiers executed the orders given by their superior.

intermediate.m: Reserves are extra amounts of something that are for the future.
intermediate.e: She always had some water in reserve.

intermediate.m: If you 'assist someone, you help them.
intermediate.e: She assisted the doctor.

intermediate.m: If something is ordinary, it is normal and not special.
intermediate.e: Today is an ordinary day, just like the last 256.

intermediate.m: A big plate for many people; a wide, long, flat thing that people put food on.
intermediate.e: Take some food from the tray and put it on your plate.

intermediate.m: A crash is something that happens between things. Something that comes together.
intermediate.e: I saw a horrible crash on my way home. Two cars had hit each other.

intermediate.m: If something is forbidden, it is not allowed; it is not permitted.
intermediate.e: Video games are forbidden in this house.

intermediate.m: Unwise. A person who is foolish does not have good sense or judgement. They do things without thinking carefully; they do things that are bad ideas.
intermediate.e: The person who saw and copied my homework today is being foolish.

intermediate.m: If you endorse a person, project, action, or idea, you express your support or approval for them officially.
intermediate.e: His commanding officer endorsed his application for a scholarship.

intermediate.m: To exalt, or give glory or praise to something or someone.
intermediate.e: Fans glorify their favorite divas.

intermediate.m: If you modify something, you change it, often only in small ways, and often because you want to use it in a different situation.
intermediate.e: We found some new problems and modified the program accordingly.

intermediate.m: Mathematics is the study of numbers.
intermediate.e: Use of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division are part of basic mathematics.

intermediate.m: Your salary is the money you are paid every month for doing your job.
intermediate.e: The average monthly Japanese salary increased 4.3 percent last year.

intermediate.m: If something is prime, it is best, most important, most suitable, or in some way number one.
intermediate.e: Canada is a prime example of a multicultural country.

intermediate.m: Describes something that deserves ridicule, is foolish or absurd
intermediate.e: Adam's mohawk is ridiculous.

intermediate.m: If someone is bold, that means they are brave and willing to take risks.
intermediate.e: That is a bold idea.

intermediate.m: Emotional is when your feelings control what you do, rather than reason.
intermediate.e: His reasons for buying the old house were emotional.

intermediate.m: If something is done solo, you do it without a companion.
intermediate.e: Her solo is set to be released next summer.

intermediate.m: A sector is a part or division of an area, especially part of the economy.
intermediate.e: I am going to go patrol the south sector.

intermediate.m: An absentee is someone that is not present in one function. Usually used in absence from school.
intermediate.e: The history class has no absentees today.

intermediate.m: A postcard is a piece of paper with a message on it mailed without an envelope.
intermediate.e: I sent a postcard to my friend when I was on vacation.

intermediate.m: A tent is similar to a house or building that is made of cloth or skins.
intermediate.e: We slept in a tent all week.

intermediate.m: An outrage is a very violent act.
intermediate.e: He kicked a puppy which was an outrage.

intermediate.m: If something is numerous, it is in large amount.
intermediate.e: Why are there numerous ants here?

intermediate.m: A rise is an increase in something, is when something gets higher.
intermediate.e: I got a pay rise so now I can buy a bigger car.

intermediate.m: When you transform something, you change it into a different thing totally.
intermediate.e: The powerful magician transformed the hamster into a rabbit.

intermediate.m: A delivery is the act of moving good or mail from a source to somebody.
intermediate.e: The delivery of the letters was delayed by the weather.

intermediate.m: An attribute is a part, feature, or characteristic.
intermediate.e: A good sense of humour is an essential attribute for a doctor to have.

intermediate.m: To be superb, something must be the very best, grand, excellent and the very best quality.
intermediate.e: The food at the restaurant was superb.

intermediate.m: A reminder is someone or something that is used to remember something.
intermediate.e: He left a note as a reminder to get groceries.

intermediate.m: If someone is narrating, they are telling a story or speech.
intermediate.e: The movie is narrated by John Smith.

intermediate.m: If you bore somebody, you make them feel that they want to do something else because it is not interesting.
intermediate.e: I hate tennis; it bores me.

intermediate.m: The amount which something has grown.
intermediate.e: There was an increase in movie releases last year.

intermediate.m: Thirst is the feeling that you want to drink.
intermediate.e: All that work has given me a thirst.

intermediate.m: An estimate is a judgement of a size, value, amount, cost, etc., which is based on incomplete information.
intermediate.e: British Telecom will give you an estimate of the cost before doing any work.

intermediate.m: Amazing things cause wonder and amazement.
intermediate.e: That was an amazing book. I enjoyed every moment of it.

intermediate.m: A consumer is someone who buys or uses goods or services.
intermediate.e: Selling goods to consumers is known as retail.

intermediate.m: If a person dislikes someone or something, they do not like someone or something.
intermediate.e: He had to eat cabbage although he really disliked its strong smell.

intermediate.m: Very strong or intense fear.
intermediate.e: I never felt such terror as when I was robbed at gunpoint.

intermediate.m: A mayor is the government leader of a village, town, or city.
intermediate.e: Palin took office as mayor in October 1996.

intermediate.m: When you say something, read, or laugh aloud, you speak or laugh so that other people can hear you.
intermediate.e: When we were children, our father read aloud to us.

intermediate.m: A grant is something, usually money, that is given to someone, usually by a government or institution.
intermediate.e: I got a $2,000 government grant to help me go to school.

intermediate.m: The way or the amount of using; use.
intermediate.e: I learnt the usage of some verbs while studying the language.

intermediate.m: A tabloid is a newspaper having pages half the size. They mostly publish popular articles and sensational stories instead of serious news.
intermediate.e: Now Ulrich can be occasionally found in tabloid magazines looking haggard and old.

intermediate.m: Inflation is a general increase in the price of goods and services.
intermediate.e: Wages adjusted for inflation actually fell last month.

intermediate.m: Not characteristic.
intermediate.e: That was uncharacteristic of him.

intermediate.m: Gorgeous is very beautiful.
intermediate.e: The sunsets in Hawaii are gorgeous.

intermediate.m: Aluminum is a metallic (meaning made of metal) element with an atomic number of 13 and the symbol Al.
intermediate.e: These cans are made from aluminum.

intermediate.m: An appeal is a strong or official request.
intermediate.e: The school launched an appeal to raise money for the new library.

intermediate.m: Security is safety.
intermediate.e: Since the attack, many Americans have lost their feeling of security.

intermediate.m: If something is relaxing, it makes you relax.
intermediate.e: After a long day at the office, I like to take a nice relaxing bath.

intermediate.m: A part of something
intermediate.e: How long is that segment of rope?

intermediate.m: If something is coherent, it is logical and well-organized, making sense as a whole.
intermediate.e: His argument was clear and coherent.

intermediate.m: A deed is an action that is done; sometimes it is brave and important
intermediate.e: The man had done a good deed by saving that child.

intermediate.m: If something is commercial, it is related to buying, selling, trading and money.
intermediate.e: There is too much fishing, both commercial fishing and sport fishing.

intermediate.m: An extract is something that has been taken out of something else, usually something that it was part of.
intermediate.e: I'll read a short extract from his speech.

intermediate.m: If you unfold something, you make it flat.
intermediate.e: I took the origami and unfolded it into a flat sheet of paper.

intermediate.m: A qualification is something you add to an idea that limits its effect or meaning.
intermediate.e: I accept your offer, but with some qualifications.

intermediate.m: Ink is a tint, often black, used to write.
intermediate.e: The ink on the paper has dried.

intermediate.m: Something that is democratic is based on or relates to democracy, where the people choose the government.
intermediate.e: The United States is a democratic country, since the citizens choose the leaders in government.

intermediate.m: If something or someone is thunderous, it is very loud, like thunder.
intermediate.e: After winning the duel in the arena, thunderous cheers greeted the hero from the audience.

intermediate.m: If a sound is loud, you can hear it very easily. If it's very loud, it might hurt your ears.
intermediate.e: Can you turn down the music, please? It's too loud.

intermediate.m: A fifth of something is one of five equal parts of that thing.
intermediate.e: Three is one fifth of fifteen.

intermediate.m: A distortion is a change to the original (or normal) shape (or characteristic) of something. It can apply to objects, images, sounds, or information.
intermediate.e: He told her the story, but it was a distortion of the truth.

intermediate.m: Corporate finance, planning, management, etc. is related to business or a company.
intermediate.e: We have accounts for both individual and corporate clients.

intermediate.m: A peer is someone of the same level as you.
intermediate.e: I have peers in school that often help me when I need their help.

intermediate.m: A tragedy is a disaster that usually involves someone getting injured or dying and can affect the lives of many others.
intermediate.e: The 9/11 attacks was a tragedy in the history of United States.

intermediate.m: When something is flexible, it can bend.
intermediate.e: The thin wood stick was so flexible that it would bend but not break.

intermediate.m: A brewery is a building where beer is produced.
intermediate.e: The brewery was only open to visitors on the weekends.

intermediate.m: A reception of something is how well it is doing.
intermediate.e: The reception of this video game is pretty good. I recommend buying it.

intermediate.m: To retard something is to hold it back, or slow it down.
intermediate.e: He cut back the shrub to retard its growth.

intermediate.m: A rainforest is a thick forest with tall trees that grows in hot, wet places.
intermediate.e: The Amazon is the largest rainforest in the world.

intermediate.m: If something is liberal, it allows for change, flexibility, and free thought.
intermediate.e: Any attempt to put a liberal democracy in Iraq will fail.

intermediate.m: A hole or body of water is deep if it goes down a long way.
intermediate.e: Do not dive into this swimming pool because it is not deep enough.

intermediate.m: Income is the money that you get from working.
intermediate.e: The company's income has dropped because of poor sales.

intermediate.m: A treaty is a formal agreement between two or more states.
intermediate.e: Both countries signed the peace treaty.

intermediate.m: Atomic means it is about atoms, which are very small.
intermediate.e: The force of an atomic bomb comes from breaking an atom into pieces.

intermediate.m: To show or speak in public about something, usually done in a formal way.
intermediate.e: The professor gave a presentation to a group of doctors on the benefits of universal healthcare.

intermediate.m: A highlight is a particularly good part.
intermediate.e: The chicken was the highlight of the dinner, just amazing.

intermediate.m: If someone or something is persistent, they continue and do not give up quickly.
intermediate.e: She has had a persistent cough for weeks.

intermediate.m: A register is an official list of names.
intermediate.e: On voting day, I found my name was not on the register and I couldn't vote.

intermediate.m: A waterfall is a part of a river where water falls down.
intermediate.e: Don't swim too close to the waterfall!

intermediate.m: An archaeologist is a person who studies people and societies by looking at the things they have left behind.
intermediate.e: Archaeologists dug around the pyramids looking for clues to show how they were built.

intermediate.m: An ambulance is a kind of van that takes hurt people to the hospital.
intermediate.e: They called an ambulance when they saw he wasn't breathing.

intermediate.m: If something is damp it is somewhat wet.
intermediate.e: The grass was damp with dew this morning.

intermediate.m: Clerical roles or items are those related to the clergy, the official leaders of religious activities.
intermediate.e: The preacher at our church doesn't wear a clerical collar.

intermediate.m: Places that are far from cities or farms; usually places where no people live.
intermediate.e: We were hunting deer in the wilderness.

intermediate.m: An understanding person is able to easily see how someone else feels.
intermediate.e: Thanks for being so understanding about how emotional and erratic I've been acting lately.

intermediate.m: If you amaze somebody, you make them feel very surprised.
intermediate.e: He was amazed when he found that the girl was a robot.

intermediate.m: If something decays it rots.
intermediate.e: My teeth were decaying because I ate too much sugar.

intermediate.m: If something is stressful, it is causing mental or emotional stress.
intermediate.e: Examinations can be stressful for the students.

intermediate.m: An assistant is a person who helps (or assists) another person.
intermediate.e: The doctor's assistant held his tools.

intermediate.m: If something is wildly popular, different, optimistic, etc, it is extremely so.
intermediate.e: They turned a quiet village into a wildly popular location.

intermediate.m: A barn is a building found on a farm where animals live (such as cows and chickens).
intermediate.e: If it wasn't for the barn, all of the animals would have been out in the rain.

intermediate.m: Chemistry is the science that studies matter (material).
intermediate.e: We studied acids in chemistry.

intermediate.m: If something is deceptive, it tries to make people believe something that is not true; it misleads.
intermediate.e: He is a deceptive person. I would not trust him.

intermediate.m: A pillow is the thing you put under your head when you sleep.
intermediate.e: When Jill bought a new pillow she slept a lot better at night.

intermediate.m: A contract is a legal agreement to trade goods, services and/or property. It's usually written down.
intermediate.e: My father's employment contract is for forty years.

intermediate.m: Publication is the act of making a book or other thing publicly known or available where the public can use it.
intermediate.e: This letter is personal and not for publication.

intermediate.m: Disregard is the lack of care or attention to something.
intermediate.e: His actions showed a total disregard for the law.

intermediate.m: If something is functional, it is working properly or normally.
intermediate.e: The flashlight was still functional after I dropped it down the stairs.

intermediate.m: A valuable gem; a precious stone.
intermediate.e: Mary keeps her jewels in a safe.

intermediate.m: Cardboard is a material like paper, but thicker and stiffer.
intermediate.e: Cardboard is used to make boxes.

intermediate.m: A nucleus is the central part of something, such as a cell or an atom.
intermediate.e: The nucleus of an atom is made up of protons and neutrons.

intermediate.m: If you are resident somewhere, you live or work there.
intermediate.e: I am a resident of Thailand.

intermediate.m: If you whip something, you hit it with a whip.
intermediate.e: Jockeys whip horses to make them go faster.

intermediate.m: A leader of a country who has total control over everything.
intermediate.e: Down with the evil tyrant!

intermediate.m: Paralysis is the inability to move.
intermediate.e: The injuries were only millimetres from causing paralysis and death.

intermediate.m: If you are horrified, it means that you experienced horror or shock.
intermediate.e: They were horrified by John's idea to prank the lecturer.

intermediate.m: Something dreadful is something very bad.
intermediate.e: There has been a dreadful accident.

intermediate.m: Absence is when something is not there.
intermediate.e: There was an absence of help for the project.

intermediate.m: The act of collapsing.
intermediate.e: The collapse of the bridge means we can't go over the river any longer.

intermediate.m: A charm is an object that people think has a magical power.
intermediate.e: His old pencil was a charm for him. He always used it on tests.

intermediate.m: Fraud is a trick for the purpose of gaining money or other valuables illegally.
intermediate.e: He faces punishment for the fraud that lost $1 million.

intermediate.m: If you drag something, you pull it, usually with difficulty.
intermediate.e: She heard the noise of a chair being dragged to the window.

intermediate.m: Your stock is the collection of things that you have available, usually to sell.
intermediate.e: Police found a stock of weapons in the house.

intermediate.m: If something is northern, it is in, from, or about the north.
intermediate.e: Rock River runs along the northern edge of town.

intermediate.m: If a person is picky, they are demanding to have things just as they like.
intermediate.e: I am very picky about the way my kitchen is laid out.

intermediate.m: When you tickle someone, you touch them in a way that makes them laugh.
intermediate.e: He tickled Nancy's tummy, and she started to giggle.

intermediate.m: A gravestone is a stone on a grave, usually with the name of the dead person written on it.
intermediate.e: The old gravestone was smooth from many years of rain, but she could still read the name on it.

intermediate.m: A tax, income, or age bracket is a set of values with a bottom limit and a top limit or a group of people who fit between the limits.
intermediate.e: In the 25 to 29 age bracket, 43 percent of men and 29 percent of women had never married.

intermediate.m: A custom or practice of a society or community.
intermediate.e: The institution of marriage is present in many cultures but its details vary widely across them.

intermediate.m: If you bind something put rope or string around it, often many times.
intermediate.e: She tied the rope around their hands, binding them tightly together.

intermediate.m: Something that is wasteful is something that is a waste of good resources, time, or opportunities.
intermediate.e: Throwing away fresh food is wasteful.

intermediate.m: When you slap someone, you use something to hit another person, usually with something flat.
intermediate.e: Josh got mad at Tommy and slapped him really hard.

intermediate.m: When something is isolated, not together with others, apart, alone, or separated.
intermediate.e: Some people in Tibet live in isolation because of the large mountain ranges.

intermediate.m: To dial means to use a telephone to do a call.
intermediate.e: I picked up the phone to dial my boss.

intermediate.m: A species is the most specific level in the scientific tree.
intermediate.e: Humans belong to the species Homo sapiens.

intermediate.m: If you shrug your shoulders, you raise and then lower them in order to say you do not know or are not interested.
intermediate.e: Where's Dad?" "How should I know?" replied my brother, shrugging.

intermediate.m: When you surround something, you confine that object on all sides of it.
intermediate.e: The house was surrounded by flower beds.

intermediate.m: If something is unclear, then it is not clear or isn't easy to understand.
intermediate.e: The instructions for how to build the machine were unclear.

intermediate.m: When you disrupt something, you interrupt it, causing it to be paused or even stopped.
intermediate.e: The heavy snow disrupted the operations of the airport.

intermediate.m: If someone or something is visibly angry, uncomfortable, different, etc, something that isn't always easy to see can be seen.
intermediate.e: She was visibly upset after hearing the news.

intermediate.m: A thrill is an intense excitement.
intermediate.e: My trip to Alaska was the thrill of my life.

intermediate.m: If something is informative, it provides interesting or useful information.
intermediate.e: I read a very informative newspaper article on that subject last week.

intermediate.m: The forehead is the part of a human face between the hair and the eyebrows.
intermediate.e: Kip brushed his hair off his forehead.

intermediate.m: A route is the way someone goes from one place to another place.
intermediate.e: Could you tell me a route to the store from here?

intermediate.m: A dozen is 12 of something.
intermediate.e: He ate half a dozen cookies and felt sick.

intermediate.m: Someone or something that is mortal can age, be injured, die, or disappear.
intermediate.e: When they are young, people usually don't think they are mortal.

intermediate.m: A reaction or opinion of something.
intermediate.e: I'd really like some feedback on my poem.

intermediate.m: If x contains y, y is in x.
intermediate.e: Did the envelope contain a letter?

intermediate.m: If you instruct someone, you tell or teach them what to do or how to do something.
intermediate.e: We were stopped on the road and instructed by the police to turn around and go back.

intermediate.m: A commission is a group of people who work together to research or manage something for a government.
intermediate.e: She was recently appointed to head the European commission on climate change.

intermediate.m: To insist means to get your own way without listening to other people's comments.
intermediate.e: He insisted on eating out. His wife, therefore, had no choice but to also do so.

intermediate.m: Pajamas are clothes worn at night, made up of soft loose-fitting pants and a soft shirt.
intermediate.e: Make sure when you go to sleep that you have your pajamas on.

intermediate.m: A variety of things is a group of things that are not all the same.
intermediate.e: They felt it was important for a variety of reasons.

intermediate.m: To pull; to move one end of something as far as possible from the other end.
intermediate.e: He was big and the shirt was little, but he was able to stretch it and use it.

intermediate.m: A pump is a machine for making water move.
intermediate.e: There was water on the floor of the house, so we had to buy a pump.

intermediate.m: The elite is the best part of a group.
intermediate.e: Only the elite can enter this school.

intermediate.m: If you divert something, you change its path or flow so that it avoids a place it would have gone.
intermediate.e: The Toronto-bound flight diverted to New York.

intermediate.m: A failure is someone or something that fails, or does not achieve a goal.
intermediate.e: I was a failure at my first job.

intermediate.m: A comedy is a humorous drama.
intermediate.e: This comedy is really funny.

intermediate.m: The tide is the regular rising and falling of sea levels caused by the moon.
intermediate.e: After getting the ship stuck on sand, the crew had to wait until high tide so it would refloat.

intermediate.m: To be concerned about something means to be worried about something.
intermediate.e: Her friends became concerned and called the police.

intermediate.m: If something is formal, it is official and/or public.
intermediate.e: He studied German on his own, but he has no formal language education.

intermediate.m: A priority is something that is important; you want to do it first or spend more time or money on it than other things.
intermediate.e: The nineteen national priority areas will receive 70 per cent of the funding.

intermediate.m: If something is bare, it is just enough to get by.
intermediate.e: He survived with just the bare necessities.

intermediate.m: Domestic issues relate to issues inside one country, not affecting other countries.
intermediate.e: He believes the public is ready for change in domestic and foreign policy.

intermediate.m: An organism is any living thing, such as an animal, a plant, or a bacterium.
intermediate.e: The Earth is full of many different kinds of organisms.

intermediate.m: If something is marine, it is of the sea or it relates to the sea.
intermediate.e: Marine biology is the study of animals that live in the sea.

intermediate.m: An outcome is the result of a situation or action.
intermediate.e: The most likely outcome of the war is a broken country with no leader.

intermediate.m: Something that is prominent sticks out and is easily seen.
intermediate.e: He was a tall man with long black hair and a prominent nose.

intermediate.m: When x is true, and nonetheless y is true, then x being true didn't stop y from being true.
intermediate.e: It's raining, but we're going to eat outside nonetheless.

intermediate.m: If you invest your money, you use your money to make more money.
intermediate.e: IBM may invest new money in the company.

intermediate.m: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.
intermediate.e: The government yesterday acknowledged the need for more money.

intermediate.m: An obituary is a death notice with information of someone who has died, usually published in a newspaper or in a booklet, given to people at funerals.
intermediate.e: His obituary was published yesterday, but did not have the cause of his death.

intermediate.m: If somebody conveys something, they take it from one place to another; they move it; they transport it.
intermediate.e: The ship conveyed the goods.

intermediate.m: Fitness is the ability of an organism to survive and reproduce.
intermediate.e: In cold places, fur can increase evolutionary fitness.

intermediate.m: If someone is beloved, he or she is dearly loved by other people.
intermediate.e: His beloved wife has just passed away.

intermediate.m: A saleswoman is a woman that sells things in a shop or on the go.
intermediate.e: The saleswoman knocked on my door and asked if I wanted to buy his soap products.

intermediate.m: A gap is a difference in the level of two groups.
intermediate.e: The company has closed the wage gap by raising women's salaries.

intermediate.m: If a disease is infectious, it is can be spread between organisms through the environment.
intermediate.e: Infectious diseases like cholera are far less deadly today than they used to be.

intermediate.m: A questionnaire is a group of questions that go together, and are asked together.
intermediate.e: I filled out some questionnaires on the internet.
