intermediate.m: The act of hearing or the quality of being able to hear.
intermediate.e: Hearing is necessary to be a sign language interpreter.

intermediate.m: A portion is a part of something.
intermediate.e: We need to put more signs up in this portion of the city.

intermediate.m: Culmination is the highest point of something.
intermediate.e: The signing of this contract marks the culmination of years of negotiation.

intermediate.m: A plumber is someone who installs and fixes pipes and drains to carry water, sewage and gas.
intermediate.e: We had to call a plumber because the bathroom sink was leaking.

intermediate.m: If you undergo something, it happens to you; often it is not nice.
intermediate.e: She had to undergo surgery because of her broken leg.

intermediate.m: Admittedly means is acknowledged to be true; by general admission; confessedly.
intermediate.e: Admittedly, vandalism is a bit of problem.

intermediate.m: A catastrophe is a violent, sudden and unlucky change, which makes very big problems.
intermediate.e: The Great Fire destroyed the city completely. This was a catastrophe.

intermediate.m: To enforce means to make sure that something will be made into effect and followed.
intermediate.e: The police enforce the law.

intermediate.m: Anguish refers to the emotional pain and despair someone can experience.
intermediate.e: My anguish over a break-up with my lover could not be soothed.

intermediate.m: Something offensive is mean, insulting, and unpleasant.
intermediate.e: He said something so offensive to her that she cried.

intermediate.m: Politics is the activity of controlling, affecting or studying an organisation, especially a government.
intermediate.e: Office politics have stopped her from getting the job.

intermediate.m: A backyard is an area that is located behind a house.
intermediate.e: The children are playing in the backyard.

intermediate.m: A revision is a change or edit a to language, a plan, etc.
intermediate.e: The plan has undergone a number of complete revisions.

intermediate.m: If something is being constituted, it is being set up or established.
intermediate.e: Laws appointed and constituted by lawful authority.

intermediate.m: If something is vast, it is very, very big.
intermediate.e: The building was vast and empty.

intermediate.m: If you concede, you admit to something after resisting it.
intermediate.e: I have to concede the argument.

intermediate.m: When you lick something, you touch it with your tongue in order to taste or moisten.
intermediate.e: That boy is licking on the ice-cream that his mother bought for him.

intermediate.m: If a person is stingy, they are mean and unwilling to spend; not generous.
intermediate.e: He's really stingy and never buys anyone a drink when we go out.

intermediate.m: A skateboard is a thin piece of wood with four wheels that you can ride by standing on it and pushing against the ground with your foot.
intermediate.e: My sister won't let me ride on her skateboard, so I have to take my bicycle to school instead.

intermediate.m: A biography is the story of a person's life that is written by someone else.
intermediate.e: He wrote a biography of John F. Kennedy.

intermediate.m: If you act scientifically, you do so a manner consistent with the principles of science.
intermediate.e: The results were analyzed scientifically to ensure accuracy.

intermediate.m: When you educate someone, you instruct them; teach; train.
intermediate.e: He was educated in the public school system.

intermediate.m: If someone or an animal is injured, they are hurt; when something has caused harm to a person or an animal.
intermediate.e: You're too injured to keep playing.

intermediate.m: A venture is an undertaking.
intermediate.e: My venture into television production was successful.

intermediate.m: Acquisition is the act of getting something, often by buying it.
intermediate.e: The judge ruled that the acquisition of XYZ company by Acme Inc. was illegal.

intermediate.m: Disposal is the act of getting rid of or throwing out something.
intermediate.e: There is no long-term plan for nuclear waste disposal.

intermediate.m: When an object is coarse, it is rough and not smooth.
intermediate.e: I prefer to season with fine salt instead of coarse salt because it mixes more easily.

intermediate.m: When you bet, you take a chance with money or something else on the result of a future event.
intermediate.e: Would you bet your life on that answer?

intermediate.m: If you are doubly responsible, careful, proud, etc., you are like that in two ways or for two reasons.
intermediate.e: She felt doubly responsible for the project because she was both the leader and the main designer.

intermediate.m: If something is subtracted, then it is taken away from something else.
intermediate.e: You must subtract your expenses from your income.

intermediate.m: A very strong metal made of iron and other substances mixed together.
intermediate.e: All my pots for cooking are made of steel.

intermediate.m: Something that is vital is something that is needed to live.
intermediate.e: Water is vital to life.

intermediate.m: When you abolish something, you end it by making it invalid or illegal. You usually use the word "abolish" in regard to laws or actions.
intermediate.e: The censorship law was abolished due to huge opposition by many people.

intermediate.m: If you stir something, you move it in a circular movement.
intermediate.e: She stirred the paint to mix the color.

intermediate.m: If you have regard for something, you respect it.
intermediate.e: He has a high regard for his teacher.

intermediate.m: Trims are additional decorations that are usually placed along edges of something.
intermediate.e: Paint the house white with blue trim.

intermediate.m: Passion is a strong feeling or emotion.
intermediate.e: I have a passion for soap operas!

intermediate.m: A region is an area of land or of the body.
intermediate.e: The southern regions of Japan are warm and tropical.

intermediate.m: A pupil is a student, especially a young one.
intermediate.e: These pupils learn to write as well as write to learn in mathematics.

intermediate.m: If you are engaged in something, you are interested in it.
intermediate.e: Americans are very engaged in this year's elections.

intermediate.m: Energy is the ability to do work: move, give off heat, give off light, etc.
intermediate.e: She's all full of energy and she can't sit still.

intermediate.m: If an animal, for example a lion or tiger, roars, then it makes a loud sound.
intermediate.e: I felt scared when I heard the tiger roar in the zoo.

intermediate.m: If you make haste, you try to do something quickly and soon.
intermediate.e: We must make haste if we are to arrive on time.

intermediate.m: If something was done previously, it was done before.
intermediate.e: We discovered a language that was previously unknown.

intermediate.m: Medieval means something belongs to the Middle Ages, the time from about 400 AD to 1400 AD.
intermediate.e: She liked to collect medieval books, with their beautiful pictures and handwriting.

intermediate.m: If a message is anonymous, it is not signed.
intermediate.e: The book without an author was anonymous.

intermediate.m: The existence of a thing is the quality of being real, of being in the world, of just being.
intermediate.e: Do you believe in the existence of God?

intermediate.m: An expedition is a long trip that people go on for a specific reason.
intermediate.e: The expedition across the Alps lasted two weeks.

intermediate.m: An orchestra is a group of people who play musical instruments together.
intermediate.e: The orchestra played a piece by Beethoven.

intermediate.m: If you consume energy, resources, time, etc., you use it and it is no longer available.
intermediate.e: Most of our leisure time is consumed by TV.

intermediate.m: To overwhelm, especially with emotion.
intermediate.e: I was overcome with anger.

intermediate.m: An emotion of wild anger.
intermediate.e: Losing his game sent him into a fit of rage.

intermediate.m: Accidentally means something happens by chance; unintentionally; inadvertently.
intermediate.e: Sorry, I accidentally dropped it.

intermediate.m: Money taken by a government.
intermediate.e: The city is raising taxes again.

intermediate.m: A blossom is a flower of a plant that will become a fruit.
intermediate.e: The cherry blossoms are beautiful.

intermediate.m: To think of something or someone in one particular way, usually in a negative way.
intermediate.e: To say that all Chinese eat rice is a stereotype, because not all of them do.

intermediate.m: If you express yourself, you say something about how you feel.
intermediate.e: Sam expressed his feelings.

intermediate.m: If something is apparent, it is easy to see, realise or understand.
intermediate.e: When she was nine, for no apparent reason, she began to dislike the classes.

intermediate.m: If something is mechanical it is related to a machine, like a machine, or done by a machine.
intermediate.e: Printing presses are mechanical devices for printing on paper.

intermediate.m: A cable is a strong wire or rope that is often made out of metal.
intermediate.e: A strong cable held the two trees together.

intermediate.m: An equation is a mathematical statement in which both sides are of equal value.
intermediate.e: Find x, in the equation x+2y=3y.

intermediate.m: If you promote someone or something, you help it to get bigger, higher, or more popular.
intermediate.e: She's on tour promoting sales of her new book.

intermediate.m: Recognition is the act of recognizing somebody or something.
intermediate.e: Computers are getting much better at facial recognition.

intermediate.m: A lamb is a baby sheep.
intermediate.e: The small lamb was standing in the field.

intermediate.m: Leadership is the capacity of someone to lead.
intermediate.e: I doubt that even his leadership can help us.

intermediate.m: A belief is an idea that is thought to be true.
intermediate.e: It is a widely accepted belief that the Earth revolves around the Sun.

intermediate.m: If something is trivial, it is not important or has no value.
intermediate.e: Proving that is trivial.

intermediate.m: The action of protesting something.
intermediate.e: There will be a protest in the street tomorrow.

intermediate.m: An ideology is the set of beliefs behind a movement, religion, political group, etc.
intermediate.e: Schools reflect clearly the dominant political ideologies of their countries.

intermediate.m: If you are hooking something, you are attaching it to a hook.
intermediate.e: Hook the bag here, and the conveyor will carry it away.

intermediate.m: Vanity is the feeling of being too proud about their actions, looks or possessions.
intermediate.e: Her vanity soon made the other girls very irritated.

intermediate.m: If a place is untidy, it is not organized properly.
intermediate.e: I have never seen such an untidy bedroom!

intermediate.m: If you underline something, you put a line under it.
intermediate.e: You should underline that.

intermediate.m: The literal meaning of a word or phrase is the plain meaning: exactly what it says.
intermediate.e: It is not enough to understand the literal meaning of speech.

intermediate.m: When something fades, it slowly disappears.
intermediate.e: The mysterious figure slowly faded into the darkness.

intermediate.m: If you do something honestly, you do it in an honest manner.
intermediate.e: He answered the questions honestly.

intermediate.m: If something has happened lately, it happened not long ago. This usually for something that might happen more than once.
intermediate.e: There has been a lot of rain lately, too much for me.

intermediate.m: A chat is a casual conversation, sometimes by typing on a computer or cell phone.
intermediate.e: People come to the bar to have a drink and a chat.

intermediate.m: A suburb is the area around a city where people live.
intermediate.e: Carlton is an inner suburb, close to the city of Melbourne.

intermediate.m: If you restore a state, feeling, or ability that has been lost, you make that possible or normal again.
intermediate.e: Police were sent to restore order after an attack on May 4.

intermediate.m: An outer thing is on the outside or toward the outside.
intermediate.e: The outer layer of the coat is water proof, the inner layer keeps you warm.

intermediate.m: If things differ, they are not the same in some way.
intermediate.e: The new cars differ from the old mainly in how they look.

intermediate.m: A mortgage is a loan for the purpose of paying for a house, apartment, building, etc.
intermediate.e: For five-year adjustable-rate mortgages, interest rates rose to 5.58 percent.

intermediate.m: If something is straightforward, it is simple. It is easy to understand and easy to know how to do it.
intermediate.e: Making tea is pretty straightforward.

intermediate.m: If x is worth y, x has the value of y, usually in money.
intermediate.e: The house is worth $20000.

intermediate.m: A certain practice to the preservation of health (i.e. cleanliness)
intermediate.e: The nurse always told me to never give up on hygiene.

intermediate.m: When you squeeze something, you press it very tightly in your hand.
intermediate.e: I squeezed orange juice from the orange with my bare hands!

intermediate.m: A dock is solid a place for boats and other vehicles to connect to.
intermediate.e: She ran down the wooden dock to the waiting boat.

intermediate.m: A disaster is a serious problem.
intermediate.e: The flight had just left the airport when disaster struck.

intermediate.m: A youthful person is an older person who seems young.
intermediate.e: The young man was being very youthful.

intermediate.m: If something is seasonal, it is related to or is reliant on a season or period of the year.
intermediate.e: Hwajeon is a seasonal food that is eaten during certain festivals.

intermediate.m: Administration is the process of running and organising an organisation such as a business or government.
intermediate.e: The mayor is responsible for the administration of the town.

intermediate.m: If you are entitled to something, you have a right to receive or do it.
intermediate.e: Don't try to shut me up. I'm entitled to my opinion.

intermediate.m: When something is unexpected, it is not expected. It was not thought that it would happen.
intermediate.e: Lisa's surprise visit was unexpected and I was not prepared for it.

intermediate.m: If you specify something, you say exactly which one or how to do something.
intermediate.e: We're supposed to meet here on Tuesday, but we forgot to specify a time.

intermediate.m: If you accumulate something, you bring it together.
intermediate.e: He worried that the paperwork would accumulate on his desk if he took a day off work.

intermediate.m: If you implement a plan, you put it into action; you do it.
intermediate.e: To reduce poverty, it is essential for the government to fully implement the new education policy.

intermediate.m: If somebody is disabled, they cannot use part(s) of their body or mind in the same way that most people can.
intermediate.e: This money will help the elderly and the disabled.

intermediate.m: If something is particularly interesting, useful, important, etc., it is more so than usual or more than others.
intermediate.e: Tonight's dinner was particularly good.

intermediate.m: A contribution is something that you give or add.
intermediate.e: Technology to reduce pollution could make a significant contribution to the solution.

intermediate.m: Interruption is the act of interrupting.
intermediate.e: Sorry for the interruption.

intermediate.m: If you disqualify someone from something, you make them ineligible for it.
intermediate.e: My age disqualifies me for the position.

intermediate.m: A reaction is an action that happens because of another action.
intermediate.e: Fast reaction times are common in athletes.

intermediate.m: An improvement makes something better; it improves something.
intermediate.e: The improvement of this entry was well done.

intermediate.m: An act of adopting a child by different parents so that the child becomes one of their own.
intermediate.e: The dog was available for adoption, so I decided to take it.

intermediate.m: To put a seed or plant in soil for it to grow.
intermediate.e: I planted some flowers last week and I hope they will grow and blossom.

intermediate.m: If you lean against something, then you push or press against it.
intermediate.e: He leaned his bicycle against the wall.

intermediate.m: If you motivate someone, then you make them want to do something.
intermediate.e: The guest speaker went to the school to help motivate the students.

intermediate.m: A firm is a group of people who work together as a business.
intermediate.e: John & John is a law firm.

intermediate.m: If you resist something, you work, push, fight, etc. against it.
intermediate.e: She resisted every attempt to make changes.

intermediate.m: Your breath is the air that you move into and out of your lungs.
intermediate.e: After running for just a minute, his breath was coming quickly.

intermediate.m: Finance is activities related to banking and money, especially by government.
intermediate.e: The minister of finance announced that taxes would increase by 1% in May.

intermediate.m: A corporation is a large company or a group of companies that work together.
intermediate.e: The funding will come from government, schools, individuals and corporations.

intermediate.m: Your disposition is your usual way of acting or feeling.
intermediate.e: She has a cheerful disposition.

intermediate.m: An abnormal thing, or situation, is one that is strange, or not typical.
intermediate.e: The weather is abnormal in Europe when it is hot in winter.

intermediate.m: When all of one kind of animal are dead it is extinct.
intermediate.e: Dinosaurs are extinct. No living dinosaurs can be found on Earth.

intermediate.m: A thing or an idea that was found
intermediate.e: The new spacecraft will help us make discoveries about space.

intermediate.m: If you restrict something, you limit it.
intermediate.e: This law restricts the freedom of businesses to set their own prices.

intermediate.m: If x corresponds to y, there is a close relationship between x and y.
intermediate.e: Check that this number corresponds with the one on the document.

intermediate.m: To be jealous is to want something someone else has.
intermediate.e: I'm jealous of all your free time.

intermediate.m: Perception is the action of seeing, hearing, smelling, touching and/or tasting an object that made an impression on the senses.
intermediate.e: The government hopes to change the public's perception of the problem.

intermediate.m: If you legislate, you create or change a law.
intermediate.e: The government legislated changes to the tax law.

intermediate.m: Ginger is a strongly flavored root used in cooking.
intermediate.e: Robert likes ginger-flavored candies the best.

intermediate.m: A pile of something similar.
intermediate.e: There is a stack of books outside. Are those yours?

intermediate.m: If X is involved (in Y), X does Y or is connected to Y
intermediate.e: My teacher's very involved in politics.

intermediate.m: When something is secure, it is firmly held in place and probably will not fall.
intermediate.e: Mike's bicycle is very secure on the bike rack.

intermediate.m: If something is widespread, it happens or exists in many situations or places.
intermediate.e: This particular bird is only found here, but similar species are very widespread.

intermediate.m: To tread is to take a step.
intermediate.e: The wooden bridge did not look safe so I had to tread carefully.

intermediate.m: A cellar is a room to store things.
intermediate.e: The wine is stored in the cellar.

intermediate.m: If something streams, it comes in a flow, usually in order and often not stopping.
intermediate.e: The website offered streaming music and video files.

intermediate.m: When someone is infected by something, they come into contact with something (bacteria, virus, etc.) that causes sickness.
intermediate.e: Don't go near him, or he will infect you with his illness.

intermediate.m: A shelter is a place which can protect someone from the rain and sun.
intermediate.e: There is no shelter nearby. I wonder how we can get out of this heavy rain.

intermediate.m: A homeless person does not have a place to live.
intermediate.e: The earthquake left 1.5 million people homeless.

intermediate.m: A fold is a bend or a crease.
intermediate.e: There was a fold down the middle of the paper.

intermediate.m: The capacity of a container, room, etc. is how much it can hold.
intermediate.e: The capacity of the bottle is 500 ml.

intermediate.m: Jade is a hard, typically green stone used in jewelry and ornaments.
intermediate.e: She wore a necklace made of jade, which matched the color of her eyes perfectly.

intermediate.m: If you have a bunch of something, you have many of them.
intermediate.e: We had to try a bunch of times before we could start the car.

intermediate.m: When something is tasty, it has a good flavor and is delicious.
intermediate.e: You could make this tasty meal for breakfast.

intermediate.m: A stall is a small room or area, usually for one person, animal, etc.
intermediate.e: I stepped into a shower stall and turned on the cold water.

intermediate.m: When you pin something, you are fastening it with a pin.
intermediate.e: We should pin this poster to that wall.

intermediate.m: To be elegant something has beauty and is graceful.
intermediate.e: She looked elegant in her new dress.

intermediate.m: Litter is rubbish that is left alone on the floor.
intermediate.e: When you are in Singapore, you hardly see litter on the floor.

intermediate.m: If you detect something, you use your senses to find or notice it.
intermediate.e: Our instruments are not sensitive enough to detect it.

intermediate.m: If a disease, sickness, or illness is incurable, it cannot be cured; it does not have a remedy.
intermediate.e: The tumor in his brain is incurable.

intermediate.m: The eyelid is a piece of skin that covers the eye. The eyelid can move back, allowing the eye to "open".
intermediate.e: The doctor looked at his eyelids.

intermediate.m: A mosquito is a flying insect that is known for stinging animals and humans to suck their blood.
intermediate.e: Sleeping here is nearly impossible because of all those mosquitoes that bite you all the night long.

intermediate.m: A trigger is the part of a gun that you push with one finger when you want to make the gun shoot.
intermediate.e: I didn't want to make him angry, because he had his finger on the trigger.

intermediate.m: If something is graceful, it has grace.
intermediate.e: The lady walked across the room in a very graceful way.

intermediate.m: Therapy is the treatment of impairment, injury, disease, or disorder.
intermediate.e: My grandfather's therapy will start at the hospital at noon tomorrow.

intermediate.m: A package; a box wrapped in paper; a thing bigger than a letter that is sent in the mail.
intermediate.e: On my birthday, I got a parcel in the mail.

intermediate.m: A rack is a series of shelves stacked on top of each other.
intermediate.e: I have a rack at home that holds the books that I have.

intermediate.m: A location is a place or a site.
intermediate.e: When you're opening a new business, the choice of location is very important.

intermediate.m: When something is completely some quality, it is absolutely that quality, in every way.
intermediate.e: The man was completely honest in his business.

intermediate.m: If you do something gently, you do it in a gentle way.
intermediate.e: Sarah was going downstairs gently.

intermediate.m: A deficiency is a case when there is not enough of something.
intermediate.e: There can be a money deficiency, where there is not enough money to do something.

intermediate.m: If you fulfill something, you meet expectations.
intermediate.e: He fulfilled his promises.

intermediate.m: Mischief is the intention to cause minor trouble or the trouble caused.
intermediate.e: I hope you'll stay out of mischief when we go to church this morning.

intermediate.m: When something is faint, it is not clear, very small.
intermediate.e: The writing was faint.

intermediate.m: To yield is to give way to someone or something else
intermediate.e: Cars yield to the walkers when the walkers are in the crosswalk.

intermediate.m: The capture of something is when you get it and do not let it go free.
intermediate.e: She died just 18 days after her capture.

intermediate.m: If you're determined to do something, you have decided you will do it, and you will not let anything stop you.
intermediate.e: I was determined to make Martin happy.

intermediate.m: Someone is shocked when they are surprised at something
intermediate.e: He was shocked at how much she had changed since he had last met her.

intermediate.m: Consumption is to consuming something.
intermediate.e: The fire's consumption of the forest caused changes in the air.

intermediate.m: The plural form of good; more than one (kind of) good.
intermediate.e: The big company sells both goods and services.

intermediate.m: A condition which is so extreme that you want to stop experiencing it is unbearable.
intermediate.e: The heat was unbearable.

intermediate.m: In a negative manner rather than a positive one.
intermediate.e: His idea for cutting wages was received negatively by the workers.

intermediate.m: A measure is something that you do, usually to solve a problem.
intermediate.e: The police are taking all necessary measures to guarantee the safety of people.

intermediate.m: If someone is idle, they are not active or working.
intermediate.e: The idle workers are going to be replaced by more ambitious employees.

intermediate.m: If something is timeless, it never goes out of style or loses its importance.
intermediate.e: The story's message is timeless and still relevant today.

intermediate.m: If something is monthly, then it happens or comes once in a month.
intermediate.e: This magazine is monthly.

intermediate.m: If something has nothing inside of it, it is hollow.
intermediate.e: The box is hollow.

intermediate.m: A yawn is the action of yawning.
intermediate.e: He did three big yawns, then stood up to go upstairs to bed.

intermediate.m: Something having structure or form.
intermediate.e: The band members created many interesting formations during half-time.

intermediate.m: A name for the head officer or administrator, especially one who can make important decisions.
intermediate.e: The executive of the company was criticized for his poor management.

intermediate.m: If you are aware of something, you know about it.
intermediate.e: I am fully aware of the need for security, and will make the necessary changes.

intermediate.m: A nerve is a cell in the body that sends signals. The brain is made of nerves.
intermediate.e: She can't feel anything with this arm, and can't move her arm, because the nerves were cut in an accident.

intermediate.m: If you reply to someone or something, you answer using words.
intermediate.e: I said hi and she did not reply.

intermediate.m: The standing parts of a broken building or construction.
intermediate.e: Our only look at Mayan culture is the ruins.

intermediate.m: When you discriminate against someone, you make decisions based on prejudice.
intermediate.e: The law makes it illegal for people to discriminate against others based on their skin colour.

intermediate.m: If X is derived from Y, X comes from Y in the way that one idea comes from another.
intermediate.e: He derived a lot of pleasure from teaching.

intermediate.m: If something is religious, it is related to or about religion.
intermediate.e: Religious beliefs can be very important in choosing a marriage partner.

intermediate.m: If something is pretend, it's not real but is used for play.
intermediate.e: Let's have a pretend picnic.

intermediate.m: A headline is something that is on a front cover page. Especially on newspapers.
intermediate.e: His marriage hit the headlines yesterday.

intermediate.m: To furnish is to give a place furniture or other supplies.
intermediate.e: Our new house still needs to be furnished.

intermediate.m: If you ignore someone or something, you don't listen to, look at, or pay attention to them.
intermediate.e: He says he should be paid for fixing it, but he's ignoring the fact that it wasn't broken.

intermediate.m: Short for influenza.
intermediate.e: Sally must have the flu, she has been coughing and sneezing all day.

intermediate.m: Your elbow is the place in the middle of your arm that bends.
intermediate.e: I hurt my elbow playing tennis.

intermediate.m: If you jog you run slowly.
intermediate.e: Many people jog for exercise.

intermediate.m: An attraction is a force that pulls two things together.
intermediate.e: Magnets have an attraction to metal.

intermediate.m: If something is tame, it is not dangerous.
intermediate.e: Tame animals can live with people.

intermediate.m: If something is tasteless, it does not have any flavor; it is bland.
intermediate.e: This chicken broth is tasteless because it is not good.

intermediate.m: A mechanic is a person that can fix machines like cars and airplanes.
intermediate.e: My mechanic can fix anything.

intermediate.m: A mineral is a substance in the earth such as calcium, salt, iron, etc.
intermediate.e: The rocks in this area are rich in minerals.

intermediate.m: If something is stiff, it is not able to be bent.
intermediate.e: The bar is too stiff; I cannot bend it.

intermediate.m: If something inhabits a place, it lives in or occupy it.
intermediate.e: The Inuit inhabit the Arctic.

intermediate.m: To utter is to say something.
intermediate.e: Don't utter that name again!

intermediate.m: If someone is patient, they can wait without getting upset.
intermediate.e: I'm a patient man with a long memory; I can wait.

intermediate.m: When something happens rarely, it almost never happens.
intermediate.e: When the stars come at night, I rarely see the North Star.

intermediate.m: A supply is an amount of something that you can use when you need it.
intermediate.e: We will need a supply of water.

intermediate.m: Construction is the act of building something.
intermediate.e: The workers began construction of the new hospital last week.

intermediate.m: To say something you have memorized
intermediate.e: I will recite my poem tomorrow.

intermediate.m: If something is strengthened, then it is made stronger; strength is added to it.
intermediate.e: They are keen to strengthen ties with the UN.

intermediate.m: If two words rhyme the end of the words sounds the same.
intermediate.e: The words "day" and "way" rhyme.

intermediate.m: If something is constant, it doesn't change over time.
intermediate.e: The rain has been constant all morning.

intermediate.m: A tag is a small label, mostly a price tag.
intermediate.e: Would you mind if I removed the price tag on your shirt?

intermediate.m: A mentor is a wise and trusted guide and adviser.
intermediate.e: Some students use a mentor to help them through their first year of college.

intermediate.m: Participation is the act of joining together with other people to do something.
intermediate.e: After the injury, he was removed from active participation in the war.

intermediate.m: A monitor is part of a computer or other similar machine, and it looks like a TV.
intermediate.e: The engineers stood around the monitor making suggesting about how the drawing could be improved.

intermediate.m: To destroy; to destruct
intermediate.e: They demolished the old house and put up four townhouses.

intermediate.m: Peel is the peeled skin of a fruit.
intermediate.e: Banana peels are slippery.

intermediate.m: A butcher is a person who slices and sells meat.
intermediate.e: I went to the butcher to buy a steak.

intermediate.m: In baseball, a pitch is when the pitcher throws the ball to the batter, who tries to hit it.
intermediate.e: The batter was going to swing at the pitch but it was too high.

intermediate.m: A deck is the floor of a ship.
intermediate.e: The sailors had to clean the top deck.

intermediate.m: The way letters are used to write a word; the way a word is spelled.
intermediate.e: What's the spelling of her last name?

intermediate.m: A church where a bishop is based.
intermediate.e: The new bishop took control of his cathedral.

intermediate.m: If something or someone astonishes you, they surprise you deeply.
intermediate.e: The change astonished me.

intermediate.m: If something is fundamental, it is basic and important.
intermediate.e: Respect is fundamental to a strong education system.

intermediate.m: A mill is a place where things are processed with machines.
intermediate.e: There was an old mill by the farm.

intermediate.m: A distributor is one who divides things into smaller groups and sends them places; someone who distributes.
intermediate.e: Grocery stores buy their goods from food distributors.

intermediate.m: An encounter is a meeting, usually one that you don't expect.
intermediate.e: I had a pleasant encounter yesterday: an old friend of mine visited me.

intermediate.m: A candidate is one person or thing that may be chosen, especially in an election.
intermediate.e: The three presidential candidates will be interviewed on TV tonight.

intermediate.m: If something is shocking, it causes someone to feel shocked or startled.
intermediate.e: Did you hear the shocking news that Dan was fired for stealing?

intermediate.m: Registration is the process of registering something.
intermediate.e: The soccer club has registration at the school this week.

intermediate.m: A loan is money that you borrow and pay back later. Usually, you take a loan from a bank.
intermediate.e: I'd like to take out a loan for $5,000.

intermediate.m: To skate is to travel using roller skates, ice skates, or a skate board.
intermediate.e: I loved to ice skate during the winter.

intermediate.m: If someone or something is tiresome, it makes you bored or annoyed, usually because it is too long.
intermediate.e: All of this talking can get a little tiresome.

intermediate.m: Tourism is the commercial organization and operation of visits to tourist destinations.
intermediate.e: The tourism industry in China is booming.

intermediate.m: When you forgive something, you do not punish the person who did it.
intermediate.e: I know you stole some money from me, but I forgive your stealing.

intermediate.m: An animal that somewhat looks like a horse, but has black and white stripes.
intermediate.e: We saw zebras while we were in Africa.

intermediate.m: Endurance is the ability to continue, to keep going, even if it is painful or difficult.
intermediate.e: Running in a marathon tested the limits of her endurance.

intermediate.m: A confession is when someone admits to doing something.
intermediate.e: He gave a confession about the problem.

intermediate.m: A port is a place for ships to stop to trade or refuel.
intermediate.e: The port was bombed by the Japanese during World War II.

intermediate.m: Having the atmosphere, decoration of a festival or celebration.
intermediate.e: The festive season is around the corner.

intermediate.m: If something or someone is stupid, it shows a lack of clear thought.
intermediate.e: Don't be stupid. Of course it's true.

intermediate.m: A crow is a black bird.
intermediate.e: Can you see the crow in the sky?

intermediate.m: A broadcast is a program that is transmitted electronically over the television or radio.
intermediate.e: The broadcast of the sports game was fun to listen to on my way home from work.

intermediate.m: When you hang things, you put something above the ground and with no support below using rope, wire, or some other means.
intermediate.e: Now, I hang this picture on the wall.

intermediate.m: Someone is definite if they are sure. They have no doubt about what they're saying.
intermediate.e: She was definite that this is the right place.

intermediate.m: If something is awesome, it's very good.
intermediate.e: I love this book, it's awesome.

intermediate.m: If you are careless, then you don't have caution or care.
intermediate.e: Charles was careless and dropped the pencil, which caused it to break in half.

intermediate.m: A ramp is a sloped surface that connects two levels.
intermediate.e: If you are handicapped, you might have to take a ramp to get onto the sidewalk.

intermediate.m: A sensible person thinks clearly and makes good decisions.
intermediate.e: She wasn't talking wildy or anything; she seemed like a nice sensible lady.

intermediate.m: The act of changing.
intermediate.e: If you're gaining weight, you need to make slight adjustments to your food and exercise programme.

intermediate.m: Distribution is sending or giving out things to several people, companies, places, etc.
intermediate.e: The distribution of the mail was slowed by the snow storm.

intermediate.m: If someone or something is formidable, they cause fear, respect, or admiration because they are powerful, strong, or impressive.
intermediate.e: The boxer faced a formidable opponent in the championship match.

intermediate.m: A hesitation is a pause in speaking, usually because you are nor sure of what to say.
intermediate.e: There was a hesitation in his reading as he turned the page.

intermediate.m: When you prove something, you demonstrate that it is for real and true.
intermediate.e: I will prove my method is more effective than yours.

intermediate.m: An aim is something you want to do or have done.
intermediate.e: The ultimate aim is to be able to cure the disease.

intermediate.m: Ashes are what is left of something after it has burned (been destroyed by fire).
intermediate.e: He was covered in ash from the fire.

intermediate.m: If you unload something, you remove the cargo from a vehicle.
intermediate.e: The workers began to unload the ship as soon as the cargo hold opened.

intermediate.m: If you applaud something, you show you like it by hitting your hands together many times, making sounds. (clap) Especially if it is music or a play.
intermediate.e: I applaud your wonderful performance.

intermediate.m: Known by a small group; hidden.
intermediate.e: We found her secret diary.

intermediate.m: If you immigrate to a country, you move to there to live.
intermediate.e: He couldn't find a job in his country, so he immigrated here a few years ago.

intermediate.m: Karaoke is a form of entertainment where people sing along to recorded music using a microphone.
intermediate.e: I first saw karaoke in Japan in the 1990s.

intermediate.m: A connection is a way that two or more things come or belong together.
intermediate.e: My Internet connection is not very fast.

intermediate.m: To dissolve something is to break it into smaller pieces, often by putting it into a liquid.
intermediate.e: The group dissolved when the project was completed.

intermediate.m: A firework is a device that, when set on fire, causes a bang and many colours in the sky.
intermediate.e: The firework show is on the Fourth of July.

intermediate.m: An examination is a formal test, usually important and often at the end of a course.
intermediate.e: Did you pass the English examination last week?

intermediate.m: The flavor of something is how it tastes.
intermediate.e: I do not like the flavor of this snack. I prefer something sweeter.

intermediate.m: A person who is walking or traveling by foot.
intermediate.e: The pedestrian crossed the road when all the cars had stopped.

intermediate.m: A place's facilities are its rooms, equipment, and services.
intermediate.e: Picnic, barbecue and playground facilities are located throughout the park.

intermediate.m: If someone is respected, they have or deserve respect.
intermediate.e: A kind person is generally more respected than a mean person.

intermediate.m: Ballet is a type of dancing from France.
intermediate.e: Jim and Lisa liked to watch ballet.

intermediate.m: An actual thing is one that exists; it is real.
intermediate.e: People call me Peter, but my actual name is Pierre.

intermediate.m: Historical events, record, leaders, etc. all relate to things that happened in the distant past.
intermediate.e: The historical record shows that the country grew dramatically during that period.

intermediate.m: A laborer is a person who works or labors.
intermediate.e: The laborer is very young.

intermediate.m: Evaluation is the process of making a judgement.
intermediate.e: After the problem was found, we began an internal evaluation of the management.

intermediate.m: If Dan is arrogant, he thinks he is better or more important than other people.
intermediate.e: He is arrogant and that is why he is rude.

intermediate.m: A handkerchief is a cloth, usually white, used to clean one's face of sweat, etc.
intermediate.e: The gentleman had a handkerchief in his jacket pocket.

intermediate.m: A project is a complex job or assignment, often involving research or construction.
intermediate.e: She's a project manager with British construction company John Mowlem.

intermediate.m: All the money that you have is your savings.
intermediate.e: She had lost all her savings when the company went out of business.

intermediate.m: If the company sacks you, they end your job; they fire you.
intermediate.e: Phil was sacked last week, and I think they will get rid of more people soon.

intermediate.m: An inspector is someone who wants to inspect something.
intermediate.e: This man is an police inspector.

intermediate.m: A laboratory is a place for scientists to experiment on new things.
intermediate.e: The little child entered the laboratory by mistake.

intermediate.m: If you assure somebody about something, you tell them not to worry because the thing you say is true.
intermediate.e: The doctor assured me that he would be OK.

intermediate.m: The basis of something, is the main ideas or parts that it is built on.
intermediate.e: Her experiences in Cambodia formed the basis for her first book.

intermediate.m: A large organ in the body that makes bile, and controls chemicals in the blood.
intermediate.e: The liver is one of the most important organs in our body.

intermediate.m: A tunnel is a big hole for vehicles to drive in.
intermediate.e: This tunnel collapsed a few years ago due to construction faults.

intermediate.m: Comprehension is the understanding of the meaning or importance of something.
intermediate.e: Reading comprehension questions are often on tests in schools.

intermediate.m: An element with the symbol Fe and the atomic number 26.
intermediate.e: An object that has iron in it is attracted to magnets.

intermediate.m: Humor is ideas that make people laugh: jokes, funny things.
intermediate.e: I like the stories she tells because they're full of humor.

intermediate.m: If something is narrow, it is not wide; it is thin.
intermediate.e: The bridge was narrow.

intermediate.m: When something is momentary, it lasts for a very brief amount of time.
intermediate.e: I took a momentary glimpse at the commotion.

intermediate.m: If you are admirable, people will like you, or what you do.
intermediate.e: She said his quick thinking was admirable.

intermediate.m: A student in his or her second year in a college or university, or the second year in a four-year high school.
intermediate.e: George is currently a sophomore at Yale University.

intermediate.m: An ointment is a smooth oily medicinal substance, or a cosmetic substance that you rub on your skin, usually to ease pain.
intermediate.e: The first aid personnel applied ointment on the injured athlete.

intermediate.m: A tendency is an inclination of something to behave in a particular way or to go in a particular direction.
intermediate.e: He has a tendency to talk too much.

intermediate.m: Mud is dirt (soil) with water in it.
intermediate.e: I slipped and fell in the mud.

intermediate.m: A microscope is a device that makes tiny things easy to see.
intermediate.e: The scientist used a microscope to look at the blood cells.

intermediate.m: If you deliver something, you bring it to the person or place where it belongs.
intermediate.e: The award was delivered to her personally by the president.

intermediate.m: An item or money which belongs to another, and which will be repaid (given back) in the future.
intermediate.e: She must give the bank £100 to clear (remove) her debt.

intermediate.m: A bumper is a bar at the front or back of a vehicle to reduce damage in a crash.
intermediate.e: The car's front bumper was dented in the accident.

intermediate.m: A clip is a small item to hold things on to another.
intermediate.e: We need more clips to hang the laundry.

intermediate.m: If you bat, you swing something or try to hit something.
intermediate.e: She batted her eyelashes shyly.

intermediate.m: Mental health, processes etc. is related to the mind and thinking.
intermediate.e: Manville made a mental note of the cab's licence number.

intermediate.m: A cell is a room in a jail where prisoners are kept.
intermediate.e: He was arrested and kept in a small cell for one day.

intermediate.m: A birdcage is a cage for a pet bird (or birds) usually portable and found in the home.
intermediate.e: I keep a parakeet in a birdcage.

intermediate.m: An entry is a way into a building.
intermediate.e: There is an entry in.

intermediate.m: Frustration is the bad feeling of not being able to do what you want to do.
intermediate.e: He stood on a chair, but to his frustration, he still could not reach the jar.

intermediate.m: A miracle is an amazing thing that happened that seemed very unlikely to happen.
intermediate.e: Thanks to a miracle, Jane recovered from the final stage of cancer.

intermediate.m: You strain when it is difficult to do something and you must work hard to do it.
intermediate.e: He strained to see his friend from so far away.

intermediate.m: Melting is a process of an object changing from the solid state to the liquid state without a change in temperature.
intermediate.e: The ice melted under the hot sun.

intermediate.m: If something is tremendous, it is very good or very big.
intermediate.e: She has tremendous energy for an 85-year-old.

intermediate.m: Useless things that are discarded.
intermediate.e: Please take out the trash.

intermediate.m: An aircraft is a flying vehicle, usually an airplane.
intermediate.e: The army wants money to buy various aircraft, including helicopters and jets.

intermediate.m: If you illustrate something, you draw a picture of it, or you explain it.
intermediate.e: This graph illustrates the change in price.

intermediate.m: A pattern is a design that uses the same set of elements many times in the same order.
intermediate.e: The table cloth had a simple pattern of red and white squares.

intermediate.m: A puzzle is a game to try to put pieces together.
intermediate.e: I just have completed a puzzle with 1,000 pieces.

intermediate.m: To clap is to make a noise by hitting the palms of your hands together.
intermediate.e: The crowd clapped when the baseball team won the game.

intermediate.m: An ornament is something that is put onto something or someone just to look beautiful and for no other reason.
intermediate.e: We put ornaments on the Christmas tree.

intermediate.m: A needle is a small, long, thin sharp metal thing with a hole in it, used for sewing.
intermediate.e: She used a needle and blue thread to fix the hole in the shirt.

intermediate.m: If something is typical, it is normal, and not special. It's what you would expect.
intermediate.e: This rain isn't typical. We almost never get rain at this time of year.

intermediate.m: The volume of sound or music is how loud it is.
intermediate.e: Hey! Turn down the volume. It's too loud.

intermediate.m: A lobby is the entrance of a building.
intermediate.e: Please wait in the lobby for the tour guide.

intermediate.m: When you confess to doing something, you are saying that you did it.
intermediate.e: John confessed to the cops that he robbed the bank.

intermediate.m: If two or more things unite, they come together to form a bigger group.
intermediate.e: We united to form a common cause against our enemy.

intermediate.m: A neighborhood is part of a town or city.
intermediate.e: They live in an Italian neighborhood on the west side of the city.

intermediate.m: If you endure something difficult or painful, you experience it for a long time.
intermediate.e: We had to endure the climb to the top of the steep hill.

intermediate.m: A slogan is like a motto, but longer. It is like a catchphrase used in promoting products, candidate or a cause.
intermediate.e: The presidential candidate came up with a very catchy slogan that people can remember clearly.

intermediate.m: Two countries are allies if they support, help, and defend each other.
intermediate.e: China remains North Korea's most powerful ally.

intermediate.m: A monastery is a building where monks or nuns live.
intermediate.e: After working in the fields, the monks went back to the monastery.

intermediate.m: A kitten is a young cat.
intermediate.e: Our cat has just had kittens.

intermediate.m: An inventor is someone who invents things.
intermediate.e: Alexander Graham Bell is an inventor. He invented the telephone.

intermediate.m: An acid is a liquid with a high number of hydrogen ions in it that can burn things.
intermediate.e: The acid burned the table.

intermediate.m: If you distract someone, you make them pay attention to something different than what they were paying attention to before.
intermediate.e: The crowd was distracted by a helicopter hovering over the stadium when the only goal of the game was scored.

intermediate.m: Repetition is the same thing happening more than one time, usually many times, especially in speaking or writing.
intermediate.e: I used constant repetition to learn it.

intermediate.m: Transportation is the system or vehicles used to move people or things from one place to another.
intermediate.e: In most of Canada, the main form of transportation is the family car.

intermediate.m: If I mislead you, I make you believe something that is not true.
intermediate.e: You mislead him into believing that you are a king. You are only a common man.

intermediate.m: A category is a group of people or things that are the same in some way.
intermediate.e: The music business tries to put music into various categories, such as rock, pop, jazz, etc.

intermediate.m: The impression is the effect something has on a person.
intermediate.e: It is always important to make a good first impression.

intermediate.m: You use furthermore to add more information to what was already said or written.
intermediate.e: We believe that the project is possible. Furthermore, we believe that we can do it within a few months.

intermediate.m: If something is done aggressively, it is done in an aggressive way.
intermediate.e: The mother goose aggressively protected her nest.

intermediate.m: A genius is a person who is very smart.
intermediate.e: Albert Einstein is a genius.

intermediate.m: If something is muddy, it is covered in mud.
intermediate.e: Their shoes were all muddy after walking through the field.

intermediate.m: An awkward person or animal is clumsy, lacks agility, dexterity or grace.
intermediate.e: He doesn't managed well when I try to juggle. He's still awkward.

intermediate.m: A referee is someone who ensures that the rules are followed during a game.
intermediate.e: That referee was hit by the ball during the football game.

intermediate.m: Grains of rock that make beaches and deserts.
intermediate.e: In the summer, Jane goes to the beach, lies on the sand and listens to the waves.

intermediate.m: Decoration is an attractive surface covering, or what makes something more beautiful.
intermediate.e: Fabergé eggs were covered with fine decoration.

intermediate.m: A shoe that covers part of the leg.
intermediate.e: I love my special hiking boots.

intermediate.m: A decrease happens when the number or value of something goes down.
intermediate.e: There has been a 3% decrease in the Australian dollar against the Euro.

intermediate.m: Hidden anger or fear.
intermediate.e: Tensions between the two countries have been rising.

intermediate.m: Demand for something is how much people want of it.
intermediate.e: The power companies should begin to prepare for increased demand for electricity.

intermediate.m: Botany is the science of learning about plants.
intermediate.e: My mother studied botany in college.

intermediate.m: The distance below a surface; how deep something is.
intermediate.e: Measure the depth of the water in this part of the bay.

intermediate.m: If a person, animal, or plant is ill, it has a disease.
intermediate.e: There are many different germs which cause diseases.

intermediate.m: A district is an area of land that shares certain characteristics.
intermediate.e: The lake district is one of England's most beautiful areas.

intermediate.m: Maintenance is the process of regularly fixing things and keeping something in good shape.
intermediate.e: After 8,000 km, you should take the car in for maintenance.

intermediate.m: An axis is the imaginary line that an object spins around. This is the middle of the circle of the turn, and at a right angle to it.
intermediate.e: The Earth rotates once a day on its axis.

intermediate.m: A vessel is a pot or container.
intermediate.e: She poured the milk into another vessel.

intermediate.m: If you sail, you move by catching the wind, usually by ship on water.
intermediate.e: They sail around the world every year in their boat.

intermediate.m: A group of people who live together; the group may or may not be a family. A household may also be an individual living alone.
intermediate.e: How many people are there in your household?

intermediate.m: A symptom is a sign or indication of something, usually an illness.
intermediate.e: He began to show symptoms of chicken pox a few days ago.

intermediate.m: Obey is to do what a person tells you to do.
intermediate.e: Soldiers in the army must obey their officers.

intermediate.m: When you tumble, you fall down over and over again.
intermediate.e: Tie your shoes so that you won't tumble down the stairs.

intermediate.m: Pudding is a dessert made with cake, bread or rice and often fruit, usually hot.
intermediate.e: The shop had desserts-fruit cobblers, pies, bread pudding, and chocolate, pound, and carrot cakes.

intermediate.m: If you are intent on something, you have a strong plan to have or do it, and you won't let other things stop you easily.
intermediate.e: The cat was still, intent on the bird in the garden.

intermediate.m: A patron is a supporter of something.
intermediate.e: John, a well known patron of the arts, donated a large sum of money to the local museum last summer.

intermediate.m: An audition is a performance by an someone hoping to become a performer in order to show suitability or talent.
intermediate.e: The music club had it's auditions on Tuesday.

intermediate.m: The act of obeying orders from others.
intermediate.e: Obedience is very important in any army.

intermediate.m: A finger is a long thin part of your hand that bends. Most people have four fingers and one thumb on each hand.
intermediate.e: He only uses one finger on the keyboard.

intermediate.m: An introduction is the first or opening part
intermediate.e: This is the introduction to the book.

intermediate.m: If you are trying to discredit someone, you are trying to harm the good reputation of that person.
intermediate.e: The candidate tried to discredit his opponent.

intermediate.m: Your reach is the distance that you can move your body to touch something.
intermediate.e: The keys were just out of reach.

intermediate.m: If something is relatively true, it is true in part.
intermediate.e: The apple was relatively small.

intermediate.m: When you distribute something, you divide it and give it out.
intermediate.e: Please distribute this poster to all the people on that list.

intermediate.m: The creator of something is the thing or person that made it.
intermediate.e: Steve Bourne is the creator of the original Unix Bourne shell command interpreter.

intermediate.m: An event that is forthcoming is something that will happen soon. It's coming in a short time.
intermediate.e: The forthcoming publication of her book will help her get status and respect.

intermediate.m: Mount is another word for mountain. This may be shortened to "Mt." to name a mountain.
intermediate.e: Jesus gave us the Sermon on the Mount.

intermediate.m: A crossing is an intersection where roads or tracks cross.
intermediate.e: The rail crossing is notoriously dangerous for drivers.

intermediate.m: A puppy is a young dog.
intermediate.e: My new puppy is so cute and playful.

intermediate.m: A transfer is the act of transferring something from one form to another.
intermediate.e: International trades involve the transfer of currency from one country to another.

intermediate.m: Reality is what actually is. Reality is what is real.
intermediate.e: What you see on television is often very far from reality.

intermediate.m: A mango is a sweet tropical fruit with smooth yellow or red skin, soft yellow or orange flesh and a very large seed inside.
intermediate.e: This mango is very big.

intermediate.m: If you hunt for something, you look for it very carefully.
intermediate.e: We hunted for new clothing at the mall.

intermediate.m: If a situation is unreasonable, it's not something that many people would agree to or like.
intermediate.e: That meeting took an unreasonable amount of time.

intermediate.m: Progress is moving forward or getting better (more good).
intermediate.e: We are making progress on finding a cure.

intermediate.m: An academy is an educational organization, similar to a university or college.
intermediate.e: She passed the exams to enter the local academy.

intermediate.m: Proof is evidence which shows something is correct.
intermediate.e: He has proof that he was not at the crime scene. A witness says that they were somewhere else.

intermediate.m: Management is the act of watching and controlling a business or situation.
intermediate.e: This building uses a computerized energy management systems to save electricity.

intermediate.m: If someone or something is misleading, it is leading you to a lie. It is false and deceptive.
intermediate.e: The wolf's disguise and inviting voice were misleading tricks to trap Little Red Riding Hood.

intermediate.m: If you justify something that people think is bad, you explain why it was good or why it had to happen that way.
intermediate.e: One problem in music education is always having to justify our existence to other teachers.

intermediate.m: The roadside is the area on either side of a road.
intermediate.e: The roadside stand did a good business just selling products to people who merely wanted directions.

intermediate.m: Vinegar is a liquid made by fermenting fruit or grain. It is also an acid.
intermediate.e: When you mix vinegar and baking soda, it explodes in a chemical reaction.

intermediate.m: An instance of something is a time or situation when it happens.
intermediate.e: There have been many instances of cheating that were not caught.

intermediate.m: If something explodes, it breaks apart quickly and strongly, often with strong heat, sound, and light.
intermediate.e: She was so angry, she exploded.

intermediate.m: The significance of something is how important or large its effect or influence is.
intermediate.e: The significance of the discovery was not well understood at the time.

intermediate.m: If you get a promotion you move up in rank or position.
intermediate.e: He received a promotion to sergeant.

intermediate.m: If you investigate a problem, you get information about it and you think carefully about the information, usually to find an answer.
intermediate.e: More work is needed to investigate other possibilities.

intermediate.m: An agreement is where everybody has the same feelings about something; when everyone has the same ideas; saying "yes".
intermediate.e: We have an agreement with our teacher. If we do our homework we can go home early.

intermediate.m: If you clarify something, you make it clearer.
intermediate.e: I think we need to clarify what we have heard on the tape.

intermediate.m: If you abandon something, you go away from it with no plan to return.
intermediate.e: The government abandons after-school programs when money is tight.

intermediate.m: To alternate is change between two positions.
intermediate.e: She would alternate between laughing and crying without warning.

intermediate.m: A suspect is a person or thing who you believe committed a crime or caused something.
intermediate.e: He was the police's prime suspect in the crime.

intermediate.m: If something happens or is done distinctly, it happens in a way that is clear and easy to notice.
intermediate.e: She spoke distinctly so everyone could understand her.

intermediate.m: An employer is a person or company that pays people to do jobs.
intermediate.e: My employer pays less money than other.

intermediate.m: If you engage in an activity, you do it.
intermediate.e: Should United States forces engage in fighting in these situations?

intermediate.m: Defense is the process of protecting.
intermediate.e: Airplanes attacked the Ministry of Defense in Tehran.

intermediate.m: Extreme means to a very high degree far beyond what is usual.
intermediate.e: Few animals can live in the extreme cold of the far north.

intermediate.m: A struggle is a fight, often long and hard, or needing a lot of effort.
intermediate.e: Nature is really an ongoing struggle for survival.

intermediate.m: Hatred is another word for hate. If you have hatred for someone, then you very strongly dislike that person.
intermediate.e: I can't believe he has such hatred for other races! -- what did they do to him?

intermediate.m: If someone is hurt, they are wounded or in pain.
intermediate.e: He got hurt skiing last week when he fell.

intermediate.m: A jug is a large container for liquids, usually with a wide mouth.
intermediate.e: The jug is full of milk.

intermediate.m: If you inquire about something, you ask about it.
intermediate.e: If anyone inquires about it, I just won't answer.

intermediate.m: A rehearsal is a practice session before a performance.
intermediate.e: We held ten rehearsals for the new play.

intermediate.m: If something is personified, it is a representation in the form of a character.
intermediate.e: Mozart could be said to personify musical genius.

intermediate.m: (usually accommodations in American English) Accommodation is a place to stay or live.
intermediate.e: The hotel provides high quality accommodation, mostly for foreign visitors.

intermediate.m: A calf is a young cow or the young of certain other large mammals.
intermediate.e: The cow gave birth to a calf today.

intermediate.m: The federal government is the main country-wide government in a country where there are also state or provincial governments.
intermediate.e: Federal taxes will increase next year.

intermediate.m: If something is worthless it has no value, meaning or importance.
intermediate.e: The china figure was worthless after I accidentally dropped it.

intermediate.m: A container for boiling liquids or cooking food.
intermediate.e: William cooked the beans in a kettle.

intermediate.m: Your viewpoint is your idea of what the world is like.
intermediate.e: Jimmy's viewpoint of the war was that is was wrong.

intermediate.m: Someone's wrist is a part of their body where the arm joins the hand.
intermediate.e: You can move your hand up and down while keeping your arm in one place by bending your wrist.

intermediate.m: A follower is someone who follows.
intermediate.e: The band has a large number of followers.

intermediate.m: A teammate is a person who is on the same team.
intermediate.e: I passed the ball to my teammate so he could score the goal.

intermediate.m: If you recover, you get better after getting sick, or being hurt, surprised, etc.
intermediate.e: Lansky looked surprised, but quickly recovered.

intermediate.m: A restriction is something that restricts or limits something else.
intermediate.e: The restrictions on parking in the city during snowstorms make it almost impossible to find parking anywhere.

intermediate.m: A leopard is a type of large cat that has spots and lives in Africa and parts of Asia.
intermediate.e: People have sometimes hunted leopards for their beautiful skins.

intermediate.m: Height measured from sea level.
intermediate.e: The altitude of Mount Fuji is 3776 meters.

intermediate.m: An urge is a want to do something.
intermediate.e: After watching the basketball game, he had an urge to play too.

intermediate.m: If something is mathematical, it is of or relating to mathematics.
intermediate.e: In the early 1960s, there were not many papers on purely mathematical descriptions of molecules.

intermediate.m: A squad is a group of people.
intermediate.e: The England cricket squad won their last match.

intermediate.m: If you straighten a place up, you put everything in the right place.
intermediate.e: Can you straighten up in here, and make your bed?

intermediate.m: If you flee, you run away or escape.
intermediate.e: The prisoner tried to flee, but was caught by the guards.

intermediate.m: If something is hilarious, it makes you laugh a lot.
intermediate.e: That joke was hilarious.

intermediate.m: If you jeopardize someone or something, you put them in a situation in which there is a danger of loss, harm, or failure.
intermediate.e: After having an affair with a junior, her chances of promotion were seriously jeopardized.

intermediate.m: To unpack something means to remove items from a package or container, usually referring to a bag or a luggage.
intermediate.e: The first thing you should do once you arrive home from camping is to unpack your bags.

intermediate.m: A delicate thing is something that can break easily. It is usually beautiful but people need to be careful if they touch it.
intermediate.e: Flower petals are delicate.

intermediate.m: Someone's estate is everything they own, or everything they leave when they die.
intermediate.e: Because he had no family, he left his estate to the church.

intermediate.m: A network is a group of connections between a number of points.
intermediate.e: I don't have a good social network in my new job.

intermediate.m: To punish someone means to cause someone to suffer, because they have broken a rule.
intermediate.e: The boy was punished for hitting his baby sister.

intermediate.m: Principles are personal rules that tell you what is right and wrong.
intermediate.e: It goes against my principles to ignore her.

intermediate.m: If you inspect something, you look at it carefully to find problems.
intermediate.e: Drivers should inspect their tires regularly.

intermediate.m: A portion or part of something
intermediate.e: The glass broke into hundreds of fragments.

intermediate.m: A push is the act of touching something with a force away from your body.
intermediate.e: My car won't move. Can you give me a push?

intermediate.m: Someone who says things that are not true, that is, someone who lies.
intermediate.e: I don't trust that liar.

intermediate.m: If something is unlikely, then it probably will not happen.
intermediate.e: It's unlikely that it will rain today.

intermediate.m: The format of some writing is the way it is organized: the size and colour of the letters, the way it is divided into parts, the kind of words used.
intermediate.e: What format do you want the report written in?

intermediate.m: Praise is good things said about someone.
intermediate.e: The actor received much praise from the critics.

intermediate.m: A fund is an amount of money kept for a specific purpose.
intermediate.e: Our fund-raising campaign has a target of $100,000.

intermediate.m: A material made from the sap of trees.
intermediate.e: The ball is made of rubber.

intermediate.m: A treatment is an action, usually by a doctor, to make somebody healthy.
intermediate.e: He has had treatments every day since he hurt his neck.

intermediate.m: An operation is a medical process, often opening the human body.
intermediate.e: The doctors performed the operation in three hours.

intermediate.m: An event is frequent if it happens many times in a short time.
intermediate.e: Seeing a lion is not a frequent event around here.

intermediate.m: If it is stormy out, it is rainy and windy.
intermediate.e: The weatherman predicted that it would be stormy outside today.

intermediate.m: Wages is the money a person is paid for doing their job.
intermediate.e: The workers were demanding higher wages.

intermediate.m: A salty water that is produced naturally by the body.
intermediate.e: It is so hot that my whole body is covered with sweat!

intermediate.m: If you cease something, you stop doing it.
intermediate.e: Beyond the window, the rain ceased, giving way to sunshine.

intermediate.m: A prospect is what you think will happen in the future.
intermediate.e: There's a good prospect of this building being converted into a school.

intermediate.m: A pearl is a round, white jewel that you get from inside of oysters.
intermediate.e: She bought a pearl necklace.

intermediate.m: A fleet is a large group of something, especially ships and aircraft.
intermediate.e: The fleet of warships left port at dawn.

intermediate.m: A breed can be a type of animal or plant; a species or race.
intermediate.e: This breed of dog likes to bark more than most.

intermediate.m: A trace of something is a very small amount, almost too small to find.
intermediate.e: He said it without a trace of sadness.

intermediate.m: Realization is the process or result of coming to understand something clearly.
intermediate.e: He slowly came to the realization that she wouldn't be coming back ever again.

intermediate.m: Geography is how a place is on a map. It is about where things like rivers, mountains, cities, and countries are.
intermediate.e: I know the geography of the area because I once lived there.

intermediate.m: If you assume something, you think or believe something without having enough information to know that it's true.
intermediate.e: Oh, hello. I assume you're the new student, are you?

intermediate.m: A coffin is a box used to keep the dead body of a person.
intermediate.e: The family of Mary were very hurt to see her laying in her coffin.

intermediate.m: If something is genuine, it is what is says it is and not something else; it is not fake.
intermediate.e: I have a genuine copy of the famous book.

intermediate.m: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.
intermediate.e: The statues were made out of bronze.

intermediate.m: A thesis is a long paper that university students at the masters or doctoral level write.
intermediate.e: She's writing her thesis on the effects of TV on children.

intermediate.m: If you are reluctant to do something, you do not want to do it.
intermediate.e: She gave him a reluctant smile.

intermediate.m: Collocation is the grouping words or sounds together.
intermediate.e: The phrase "all alone" is an English collocation while "completely alone" is not.

intermediate.m: A spare part, room, key, etc. is an extra one, one that is not being used.
intermediate.e: I've got a spare bedroom. You can stay there.

intermediate.m: A salon is a place where people go to have their hair styled, cut, or treated.
intermediate.e: She went to the salon to get a haircut.

intermediate.m: If something attracts you, it makes you interested in it.
intermediate.e: She jumped up and down to attract attention.

intermediate.m: A phase is stage in a process.
intermediate.e: We will look at very basic ideas during the first phase of training.

intermediate.m: If something is informal, it is friendly and casual; it is not official.
intermediate.e: Can we get together for some informal talks before the meeting?

intermediate.m: If you give someone or something assistance, you give help or support.
intermediate.e: The company may also provide financial assistance to single mothers.

intermediate.m: A tube; a round, hollow piece of metal, plastic, or wood.
intermediate.e: I will fix the pipe.

intermediate.m: Something is nonsense when it makes no sense or has no meaning.
intermediate.e: This is just a bunch of words randomly jumbled together. It is complete nonsense.

intermediate.m: If something is in advance of something else, it is before it.
intermediate.e: Hotel rooms are often booked up months in advance.

intermediate.m: A harbor is some water in a curve of land where it's safe for boats because there are no big waves.
intermediate.e: A ship in the harbor is safe -- but that is not what ships are for.

intermediate.m: To give or sell weapons to a person, group, or country.
intermediate.e: Our taxes pay to arm the military.

intermediate.m: An applicant is a person who makes an application for something, often a job.
intermediate.e: The job applicants had to have an interview with the head of the company.

intermediate.m: If you react to a person or event, you do something because of the person or event.
intermediate.e: When someone shouts at you, you usually react by shouting back.

intermediate.m: A drain is a hole, sometimes in the bottom of a basin, to let water flow out, and a pipe attached to the hole.
intermediate.e: After you wash, you should drain the water from the bath.

intermediate.m: If you have respect for someone, that means you have high regard for them; you are considerate towards them.
intermediate.e: I have great respect for all of my classmates.

intermediate.m: A tribe is a social group of families and individuals who live together and have a long shared history.
intermediate.e: Most of the younger members of the tribe grew up speaking Spanish.

intermediate.m: A coincidence is when two things are in the same place or space, they coincide.
intermediate.e: The scientist studied the beam of electrons and timed examples of coincidence.

intermediate.m: A millionaire is a person who has one million dollars or more.
intermediate.e: The CEO was named as one of the youngest millionaires of the United States.

intermediate.m: A barrier is something that stops passage; it does not allow anything to get through it.
intermediate.e: The barrier across the road stopped traffic from getting past it.

intermediate.m: If something is absent, it means to be not in a place or missing.
intermediate.e: John is absent from school today.

intermediate.m: If something is sufficient, it means there is enough or that it is good enough.
intermediate.e: We now have a sufficient number of people to do the job.

intermediate.m: A participant is a person who takes part in something.
intermediate.e: The athlete was a participant at the Olympics.

intermediate.m: If something is lousy, it is bad or have a poor quality.
intermediate.e: No offense, but his cooking is lousy.

intermediate.m: When you asserts something, you say it with confidence.
intermediate.e: He asserted that he was innocent.

intermediate.m: If you console someone, you try to make them feel better.
intermediate.e: When my friend found his cassette broken, I tried to console him.

intermediate.m: If you persuade somebody to do something, you make them do it, usually by telling them why it's a good thing to do.
intermediate.e: She tried to persuade her mother to leave Greensburg.

intermediate.m: If something is happening currently it is happening at this time.
intermediate.e: We are currently at home.

intermediate.m: If you are motivated to do something, you have a reason to do it and you want to do it.
intermediate.e: It takes a very motivated person to get great scores like that.

intermediate.m: If you can conceive of a certain situation, you can imagine it.
intermediate.e: I just can't conceive of life without you.

intermediate.m: To donate something is to give it away for free to benefit someone or something else.
intermediate.e: I donated my old clothes to charity.

intermediate.m: If information is sent or stored electronically, it is sent or kept in a digital format.
intermediate.e: The company keeps all records electronically for quick access.

intermediate.m: Something that is too unusual, extreme, or incomprehensible to describe
intermediate.e: His artwork was considered indescribable by many.

intermediate.m: Underpants are clothes which you wear under your trousers or skirt.
intermediate.e: Brad took off his underpants.

intermediate.m: You use mere to show how small or unimportant something is or seems to be.
intermediate.e: The mere mention of her name makes him angry.

intermediate.m: About or relating to the economy, business, money, etc.
intermediate.e: Some people are in economic trouble and have difficulty paying their bills.

intermediate.m: Permanently means in a way that lasts forever or for a long time.
intermediate.e: The restaurant closed permanently in January.

intermediate.m: If you multiply x by y, you add x to itself y times.
intermediate.e: Nine multiplied by eleven is ninety nine (9×11=99).

intermediate.m: If something is immediate, it happens right away, without waiting.
intermediate.e: When he joined the team, the impact was immediate.

intermediate.m: If you do something creatively, you do it in a creative way.
intermediate.e: You built that creatively.

intermediate.m: The cast of a play, movie, or show are all the people who act in it.
intermediate.e: The director has brought back many of the cast and crew of the earlier movie.

intermediate.m: An auxiliary worker is one who assists the main workers.
intermediate.e: The auxiliary police receive basic police training but cannot carry a weapon.

intermediate.m: A bounce is a change of direction of motion, often after hitting an object.
intermediate.e: The poor bird made a big bounce off my car when we hit each other.

intermediate.m: If you are carefree, you are not worried about anything.
intermediate.e: He had a carefree way of life. He didn't let anything bother him.

intermediate.m: A salesperson is someone that sells things in a shop or on the go.
intermediate.e: The salesperson knocked on my door and asked if I wanted to buy the soap products.

intermediate.m: A procedure is a particular way of doing something.
intermediate.e: We have decided on new hiring procedures for employees.

intermediate.m: A hairy person or animal has a lot of hair.
intermediate.e: That man's back was so hairy!

intermediate.m: A database is a collection of information arranged neatly.
intermediate.e: I have a huge database of all the employees in my company.

intermediate.m: If you recruit people, you try to get them to come and work or study with you or to join your group.
intermediate.e: A total of 85 participants aged 23-97 were recruited.

intermediate.m: If you adore someone, you love them very much.
intermediate.e: It is clear that he adores his wife.

intermediate.m: The plural form of custom; more than one (kind of) custom.
intermediate.e: The Ancient Egyptian culture had many unique and interesting beliefs and customs.

intermediate.m: When you assign a job to someone, you tell them to do it.
intermediate.e: That teacher always assigns too much homework.

intermediate.m: A genre is a style or category of literature, art or music
intermediate.e: K-pop is a popular genre of music.

intermediate.m: A plant that is grown on a farm.
