intermediate.e: Our farm's crops are corn, apples and potatoes.

intermediate.m: If something is bound to happen to be true, it is very likely to.
intermediate.e: It's no fun to lose, but it was bound to happen sooner or later.

intermediate.m: A cough is the action or sound of quickly blowing air out because of a feeling in the throat.
intermediate.e: My doctor gave me some medicine for my cough.

intermediate.m: Observation is the act of carefully seeing things that happen.
intermediate.e: To learn, you must be good at observation.

intermediate.m: A delegate is a person authorized to act as representative for one or more other people, especially at a conference or in government.
intermediate.e: A majority of the delegates voted against joining with that group.

intermediate.m: If you smash something, you break it into many small parts.
intermediate.e: He used a hammer to smash the glass of the window.

intermediate.m: If you are unaware of something, you do not know (about) it.
intermediate.e: I was totally unaware of that.

intermediate.m: Something is active if it is turned on or started.
intermediate.e: One of the computers was active: its screen was bright.

intermediate.m: When you incur yourself to something, you bring yourself to it, especially if it is harmful.
intermediate.e: The Greek government incurred a heavy debt due to its excessive spending.

intermediate.m: If two people are in correspondence, they are in a friendly discussion.
intermediate.e: My brother and I have been in correspondence over what to do for my elderly father.

intermediate.m: If something is benevolent, it wants to do good.
intermediate.e: Even though fairies were described as tricksters in fairy tales, in Disney movies, they are benevolent.

intermediate.m: If something is reduced, it has been brought down or made smaller.
intermediate.e: Taxes have been reduced by 24 percent.

intermediate.m: When someone relies on something, they need it and they feel certain that it will be there.
intermediate.e: In this place, you can't rely on good weather even in the summer.

intermediate.m: A particular thing is the one that you mean and not any other.
intermediate.e: I don't see any way to solve this particular problem.

intermediate.m: A visa is a document that gives you permission to enter a country.
intermediate.e: His visa expired today.

intermediate.m: A feeling of being embarrassed or worried.
intermediate.e: His bad singing caused us discomfort.

intermediate.m: If something is toxic, it is harmful to your health, and it is lethal to you if you swallow it.
intermediate.e: The antifreeze is toxic if you drink it.

intermediate.m: The top part of a room.
intermediate.e: This room has a very interesting ceiling.

intermediate.m: If something is closely related, linked, or involved it is strongly so.
intermediate.e: The birds on this island are closely related to those on the mainland.

intermediate.m: An option is a choice.
intermediate.e: He has the option to go to university or join the army.

intermediate.m: Blindness is the condition of being unable to see.
intermediate.e: She was born with complete blindness.

intermediate.m: A muscle is a part of the body of a person or animal. It's a part that pulls to make parts of the body move.
intermediate.e: He can lift heavy things because he has strong muscles.

intermediate.m: If something is hourly, then it happens once every hour.
intermediate.e: That train stops here hourly.

intermediate.m: A comet is an object in outer space in an orbit that has dust surrounding its main mass, including a tail formed from gas from it.
intermediate.e: I could see the bright blue comet passing my window at night.

intermediate.m: A writer or speaker's conclusions are the ideas that they have after thinking about all the important information.
intermediate.e: The study's main conclusion is that more money will not solve the problem.

intermediate.m: If you nurse a sick or injured person or animal, you help them with the activities of daily life.
intermediate.e: I admire the time he took to nurse that sick dog back to health.

intermediate.m: A resource is something that is available and useful.
intermediate.e: We don't have enough time and resources to finish the job.

intermediate.m: A bandage is a long piece of material used to cover a wound, or protect an injury.
intermediate.e: The vet wrapped the cat's injured leg with a bandage.

intermediate.m: If you are dependent on something, you need it or rely on it.
intermediate.e: Ocean divers are dependent on their oxygen masks for air.

intermediate.m: If you scramble, you climb quickly and with difficulty, often using your hands to help you.
intermediate.e: They scrambled like spiders up the rocks.

intermediate.m: The part you can see in fire.
intermediate.e: We saw the flames burning the house.

intermediate.m: If something is supernatural, it is something of the other world, spooky, scary or that is not natural or normal.
intermediate.e: Supernatural creatures scare me.

intermediate.m: An incident is an event or occurrence.
intermediate.e: What happened before was sure an unusual incident.

intermediate.m: It is the part of the day when the sun appears on the eastern horizon.
intermediate.e: The sunrise is very bright.

intermediate.m: (countable) When you catch a glimpse of something, you see it only for a moment.
intermediate.e: I caught a glimpse of baby Prince George as his parents left the hospital.

intermediate.m: A career is a job or a series of related jobs that you do for many years.
intermediate.e: He lost his hand in an accident, which ended his painting career.

intermediate.m: A doze is a light, short sleep or nap.
intermediate.e: I felt much better after a short doze.

intermediate.m: Agriculture is farming and the methods that are used to raise and look after crops and animals.
intermediate.e: Ukraine is strong both in industry and agriculture.

intermediate.m: A calculator is a device used for doing mathematical calculation.
intermediate.e: The new calculator has a lot of functions.

intermediate.m: If something is limited, there is only a certain amount of it.
intermediate.e: We have room for only a very limited number of people.

intermediate.m: When someone deserve something, it means he is good enough to have the privilege of getting something special.
intermediate.e: You deserve a gift from me since you often treat me well.

intermediate.m: An organ is a part of an animal or plant with a specific purpose, such as an eye or a heart.
intermediate.e: The stomach is an important organ of the digestive system of humans.

intermediate.m: The surface of an object is the outside of the thing.
intermediate.e: The surface of the earth is very large.

intermediate.m: A sheet is a flat cloth that you cover a bed with.
intermediate.e: Use the sheets next to the bed.

intermediate.m: An unreasonable hatred for a group, usually a race or a religion, etc.
intermediate.e: John had prejudice against Muslims.

intermediate.m: You say you genuinely feel some way when you truly do, especially when others might doubt it.
intermediate.e: I genuinely believe you did your best.

intermediate.m: If X ensures Y, it makes Y certain.
intermediate.e: His work is great and should ensure the survival of his business.

intermediate.m: Folk are people.
intermediate.e: Lots of folks are worried about their jobs.

intermediate.m: A lecturer is a person who gives lectures at a university or college.
intermediate.e: She was promoted from lecturer to professor.

intermediate.m: A nail is a small, long, thin sharp metal thing for holding wood together. People put it into the wood by hitting it with a hammer.
intermediate.e: I need some nails to fix the roof.

intermediate.m: A purse is a small bag that is used to carry money.
intermediate.e: That lady is carrying a yellow purse in her hand.

intermediate.m: A pause is a short time for stopping a work and doing some other work.

intermediate.m: Comfort is a feeling in your body that there are no problems.
intermediate.e: Enjoying the comfort of his own bed, he soon fell asleep.

intermediate.m: If something is profitable, it means it is money-making or it produces other good results.
intermediate.e: Our product was a profitable one for years, and we retired as millionaires.

intermediate.m: If something is detailed, it has many details; it is thorough or complex.
intermediate.e: The plan that he came up with is very detailed.

intermediate.m: Words that use rhythm and good sounds, like the words of a song but with no music.
intermediate.e: It was a book of verse.

intermediate.m: If something is not necessarily true, it may or may not be true.
intermediate.e: I know we don't have a car, but that's not necessarily a problem.

intermediate.m: Objection is used in a court room when the lawyer wants to say that something is wrong.
intermediate.e: This is an objection to the case.

intermediate.m: Based on exact facts which go against common knowledge or intuition but are still true.
intermediate.e: He was technically an American, even though everyone thought he was Canadian.

intermediate.m: A misconception is a wrong idea.
intermediate.e: You're under the misconception that you're better than him.

intermediate.m: If something arouses a feeling or emotion, it causes that feeling or emotion.
intermediate.e: Superiority arouses either anger or jealous of people.

intermediate.m: An accent is the particular way that somebody's speech sounds.
intermediate.e: I can speak French, but I do it with an English accent.

intermediate.m: A recovery is the process of getting better after an illness or a problem.
intermediate.e: The budget is critical to Hungary's hopes for economic recovery.

intermediate.m: A wish, a feeling of want.
intermediate.e: She has a desire to win.

intermediate.m: If something is dusty, it is covered in dust.
intermediate.e: I don't think this book has been touched in a long time because it's very dusty.

intermediate.m: A plus is a good thing.
intermediate.e: On the plus side though, it is small and easy to use.

intermediate.m: Judgment is being able to make good choices.
intermediate.e: It takes good judgment to be a manager.

intermediate.m: A document is a written record, often official.
intermediate.e: They stopped her at the airport and checked all her documents.

intermediate.m: Biology is a type of science that studies living things like plants and animals.
intermediate.e: It is required for students to study biology.

intermediate.m: If something is dated, it is marked with a date.
intermediate.e: That paper is dated.

intermediate.m: When a person writes their own name with a pen, they are writing their signature.
intermediate.e: The cheque has to have my signature on it, or the bank won't give you money for it.

intermediate.m: If you alter something, you change it, usually in a small way.
intermediate.e: The design can be easily altered by selecting new colours, materials, etc.

intermediate.m: Bad, or having a bad smell.
intermediate.e: There's a foul smell in the bathroom.

intermediate.m: The input is the information that is put into something.
intermediate.e: The input to the amplifier should be digital.

intermediate.m: Someone feels shame when they know they did something wrong.
intermediate.e: The boy felt shame and gave back the candy he had taken.

intermediate.m: Certainty is the state of being 100% sure.
intermediate.e: It's a little too early to say that with absolute certainty.

intermediate.m: If you warn someone about something, is to make them aware of a danger approaching.
intermediate.e: I warn you, lions are dangerous.

intermediate.m: If you are childish, you act like a small child.
intermediate.e: There are many people at work who have a childish behaviour.

intermediate.m: If you complicate a task, you make it difficult to do.
intermediate.e: My job is harder. They have complicated it by making me answer the telephone, too.

intermediate.m: A mix is two or more things that have been mixed together; it is a mixture.
intermediate.e: Now add the raisins to the mix.

intermediate.m: Completion is the action from the verb complete.
intermediate.e: The completion of the building took two years.

intermediate.m: If something is irrational is it not rational, or it is nonsensical.
intermediate.e: That decision was completely irrational.

intermediate.m: If you maintain something, you keep it at the same level.
intermediate.e: Who's more likely to maintain the status quo?

intermediate.m: Half-light in the sky before sunrise.
intermediate.e: He woke up before dawn to do a morning jog.

intermediate.m: A hole in a tube. Usually used for gas tubes and water pipes.
intermediate.e: Quick! Get a plumber! I have found a leak in this pipe.

intermediate.m: A conversation between two or more individuals.
intermediate.e: Bill and Melinda maintained a dialog via email over the course of their long-distance relationship.

intermediate.m: A monk is a person who lives in an abbey or monastery and who has devoted his life to religion.
intermediate.e: The monk lives in the abbey.

intermediate.m: When you dive, you go under the water, usually jumping head first.
intermediate.e: She dived under the water and came up blowing air.

intermediate.m: If you accustom someone to something, you make them familiar with, or used to it.
intermediate.e: He accustomed the farm girl to city life.

intermediate.m: Things that happen sometimes only happen at certain times, or on certain occasions, but not every time.
intermediate.e: Sometimes the shop has low prices on a Tuesday.

intermediate.m: A scar is the mark left behind when a wound has healed.
intermediate.e: He still has a scar on his hand where he cut himself with scissors as a boy.

intermediate.m: A mate is someone you do something with.
intermediate.e: Nils, my tent mate, was from the same elementary school in the city.

intermediate.m: To create or generate a new living thing, such as a baby
intermediate.e: To reproduce, two parents need a sperm and an egg cell.

intermediate.m: A collector is somebody who collects things, usually things that are rare and interesting.
intermediate.e: A collector would be willing to pay a lot of money for that painting.

intermediate.m: Twins are two people who were born at the same time from the same mother.
intermediate.e: I didn't know he was your twin: he looks just like you so I thought he was you!

intermediate.m: A leader of a country who has total control over everything.
intermediate.e: Hitler was a terrible dictator.

intermediate.m: A league is a group of sports teams that play against each other.
intermediate.e: They could win and finish as the best team in the best league.

intermediate.m: If something is horrible, it is very bad.
intermediate.e: Yesterday was horrible, just horrible.

intermediate.m: If something is totally true, it is 100% true.
intermediate.e: The class today was totally different from yesterday's class.

intermediate.m: A recommendation is something you tell people that they should do, buy, see because it is good.
intermediate.e: You should follow your doctor's recommendations.

intermediate.m: To have authority means to have the power to make a decision.
intermediate.e: This judge has the authority to throw you in jail.

intermediate.m: A tournament is a series of games until a winner is decided.
intermediate.e: A lot of sports fans are looking forward to the college basketball championship tournament.

intermediate.m: A performer is someone who entertains people with music, dance or acting.
intermediate.e: Freddie Mercury, the lead singer of Queen, was a great performer.

intermediate.m: A fortnight is 14 days; two weeks.
intermediate.e: Her mother will be staying for a fortnight over Christmas.

intermediate.m: Your repertoire is all the music, dances, poems, etc. that you know and can perform.
intermediate.e: The class's repertoire of songs increased as the year went on.

intermediate.m: Something that is messy is very chaotic and not organized.
intermediate.e: His sister's bedroom can be a bit messy at times.

intermediate.m: If x affects y, then x causes a change in y.
intermediate.e: The movement of the soccer ball was affected by the wind.

intermediate.m: When you do something rash, you do it too hurriedly without careful consideration.
intermediate.e: The accident was a result of his 'rash act.

intermediate.m: A keeper is someone who keeps something.
intermediate.e: He is the keeper of the keys.

intermediate.m: If you chop something, you cut it using quick downward movements.
intermediate.e: Use 1 small onion, finely chopped.

intermediate.m: A test that is done to prove something, to see if a guess is valid, or to do something that has not been tried before.
intermediate.e: The experiment will prove that water boils at 100°C.

intermediate.m: The taste of black coffee and many medicines is bitter. This is the taste of a chemical base.
intermediate.e: Yuk! That tastes bitter.

intermediate.m: If you deem something safe, necessary, important, etc., you judge it to be that way.
intermediate.e: Pierre's boss looked at the report he wrote and deemed it useless.

intermediate.m: If you prohibit something, you say that it must not be done.
intermediate.e: The laws were changed to prohibit the use of certain tools.

intermediate.m: A donation is a gift of money or something useful to a person or organization.
intermediate.e: Your donation was greatly appreciated. Be sure to donate canned goods to the shelter again next year.

intermediate.m: An aircrew is the group of people that operates an aircraft.
intermediate.e: The aircrew included the two pilots, a gunner, and a radio operator.

intermediate.m: Squash is a fast game played indoors with a small ball and a racquet.
intermediate.e: He was a great squash player.

intermediate.m: If you can barely do something, you can do it only with great difficulty or effort.
intermediate.e: After the accident, she was barely able to stand.

intermediate.m: A chemist is someone whose job is related to chemistry
intermediate.e: He became a chemist at age 30.

intermediate.m: Any time when a person is exercising.
intermediate.e: Hiking up the mountain was a good workout.

intermediate.m: The ultimate goal, success, decision, etc. is the final one.
intermediate.e: Presidents have the ultimate responsibility to keep us safe.

intermediate.m: A semi-circle shape, like an inverted "U".
intermediate.e: Robert drew an arch on the paper.

intermediate.m: A trait is a typical characteristic or feature, usually of a person or other living thing.
intermediate.e: Antlers are a trait of male deer.

intermediate.m: A parade is an event which involves moving from one place to another. Sometimes marching is a part of the event.
intermediate.e: We saw the band playing in the parade.

intermediate.m: If you anticipate something, you think or do something about it before it happens.
intermediate.e: We do not anticipate any major problems with the new system.

intermediate.m: If x governs y, x controls y through laws or other rules.
intermediate.e: The country is currently governed by the army.

intermediate.m: If you do something artificially, you do it in a way that is not sincere.
intermediate.e: The actor said his lines artificially, with too much expression.

intermediate.m: When there is a controversy about something, people don't agree about it and there is a lot of talking about it.
intermediate.e: Newspapers love to write about controversies.

intermediate.m: To scatter means to go in different directions; separate.
intermediate.e: I must scatter around the park to find my doll!

intermediate.m: An outing is a short trip, such as a picnic, or a shopping trip.
intermediate.e: My latest outing was a trip to the beach.

intermediate.m: A penalty is a legal punishment for committing a crime.
intermediate.e: The penalty for his crime was to pay a fine.

intermediate.m: If you chop something finely, you cut it into very small pieces.
intermediate.e: The recipe calls for 2 tablespoons of finely chopped garlic.

intermediate.m: An implication is a result that may be expected or predicted.
intermediate.e: She said all that, and the implications was that she didn't want to go.

intermediate.m: A ritual is a ceremony that always follows the same steps.
intermediate.e: The annual ritual to honour the gods was tomorrow.

intermediate.m: Feeling shame or guilt.
intermediate.e: John has always been ashamed of his large birthmark.

intermediate.m: A piece of tissue is a sheet of paper that can absorb very well.
intermediate.e: He used the tissue I gave him to blow his nose.

intermediate.m: The act of preventing something or hindering it; when someone or something is stopped from getting close, getting inside, or doing something.
intermediate.e: We built a wall to help the prevention of an attack on the city.

intermediate.m: Somebody who is deaf, cannot hear or cannot hear well.
intermediate.e: She did not hear what I was saying because she's deaf.

intermediate.m: The giraffe is the tallest land animal in the world. It is from Africa and has a very long neck.
intermediate.e: The family went to see the giraffe in the zoo.

intermediate.m: The neck part of a shirt, coat etc.
intermediate.e: He put up his collar because of the cold wind.

intermediate.m: Faculty are the academic staff at schools, colleges or universities.
intermediate.e: Across all Ontario Colleges, faculty have been on strike for two weeks.

intermediate.m: If something is done accurately, it is done correctly or with accuracy; it is not wrong.
intermediate.e: The scientists accurately predicted the results of the experiment.

intermediate.m: To hover is to hang in the air, almost in one place
intermediate.e: The kestrel hovered, with rapidly beating wings.

intermediate.m: Someone compiles some things or ideas when they bring them together into one place.
intermediate.e: I need to compile a list of reasons not to go ahead with the project.

intermediate.m: Smoothly and with ease
intermediate.e: It was a fluid, graceful dance.

intermediate.m: A dot is a small round mark.
intermediate.e: You forgot to put a dot over the i.

intermediate.m: The skies or places in outer space.
intermediate.e: I looked up to the heavens in delight.

intermediate.m: If you rearrange something, you change the order of (or move) it.
intermediate.e: Anagrams are formed when you rearrange the letters of a word.

intermediate.m: Division is the act of dividing a whole thing into parts.
intermediate.e: The division of the pie by the children happened with very little fighting.

intermediate.m: A nap is a short sleep, usually in the daytime.
intermediate.e: The boy is taking a nap.

intermediate.m: If you are allergic to something, you become ill when you eat it or touch it.
intermediate.e: I'm allergic to cats, they make me sneeze.

intermediate.m: A shed is a small building made out of wood that is often used to hold tools.
intermediate.e: Let me go put my tools in the shed.

intermediate.m: An approximate number, length, time, etc. is close to the real one but may not be equal to it.
intermediate.e: If we knew when he left here, it might help us identify the approximate time of death.

intermediate.m: If something is critically ill or injured, they are very unwell and need significant medical care.
intermediate.e: The patient was critically injured in the accident.

intermediate.m: If a hill or slope is steep, it goes up at a high angle.
intermediate.e: Be very careful; the hill is very steep and it's easy to fall and hurt yourself.

intermediate.m: Tools and supplies needed to build and repair things.
intermediate.e: The hardware store sells hammers, nails, and screws.

intermediate.m: A beagle is a small dog with floppy ears.
intermediate.e: The hunter shot the rabbit, and the beagle caught it.

intermediate.m: A pharmacy is a place someone can get prescription medicine.
intermediate.e: On the way home I need to pick up my medicine at the pharmacy.

intermediate.m: A strong wind that moves in a circle with a cloud shaped like a funnel.
intermediate.e: A tornado destroyed our house.

intermediate.m: If you bully someone, you are mean or nasty and you act aggressively towards them.
intermediate.e: I bullied the other boy today by hitting him in the arm.

intermediate.m: If you perceive something, you notice it through one of your senses (you see it, touch it, smell it, hear it, or taste it); to be aware of something.
intermediate.e: He was unable to perceive any difference at all in the room after the changes.

intermediate.m: A logo is a symbol used to identify a group or organization.
intermediate.e: The logo for Wiktionary shows letters in many different languages.

intermediate.m: A clause is a section in a contract or other legal document.
intermediate.e: The author's contract contained a clause giving him creative control over the films.

intermediate.m: To make, build, or form (something) by putting the parts together.
intermediate.e: We constructed the radio from parts.

intermediate.m: With one part going in one direction and another part going in another direction.
intermediate.e: Someone pushed and pulled the metal rod so much that it is now bent -- though it is not broken.

intermediate.m: If a place is gloomy, it is dark or poorly lit.
intermediate.e: The cavern was gloomy.

intermediate.m: If a person or thing originates from something, they come from or are created by that thing.
intermediate.e: Over 60% of the US company's revenues originate elsewhere.

intermediate.m: If you yearn for something, you have a strong desire for it.
intermediate.e: All I yearn for is a simple life.

intermediate.m: If you announce something, you make it public by telling people about it.
intermediate.e: They haven't announced the time of the next train yet.

intermediate.m: If something is visible, it can be seen.
intermediate.e: The car had no visible signs of damage.

intermediate.m: Someone or something that causes trouble is troublesome.
intermediate.e: He said some troublesome things, and I wasn't sure how to reply.

intermediate.m: A stain is an ugly mark on a surface.
intermediate.e: There is an ugly stain on my shirt.

intermediate.m: If something is objective, it is based on facts and things we can see and touch without using people's feelings.
intermediate.e: Newspapers try hard to publish objective stories.

intermediate.m: A cliff is a vertical (straight up and down) rock face.
intermediate.e: Don't go too close to the cliff or you will fall off.

intermediate.m: A vow is a promise. Often, a vow is a special promise that is made formally or in front of other people.
intermediate.e: The monks took a vow of silence.

intermediate.m: Renew means to refresh.
intermediate.e: My energies were renewed after taking a nap.

intermediate.m: If you obtain something, you get it.
intermediate.e: The newspaper was able to obtain the information from police.

intermediate.m: To be courageous is having courage (not being afraid).
intermediate.e: The warrior was very courageous.

intermediate.m: Disguise is a thing (e.g. clothing) used to hide one's identity or pretend to be another.
intermediate.e: That cape and mask completed his disguise.

intermediate.m: If something is moving freely, it is moving in a free manner.
intermediate.e: The water is flowing freely downstream.

intermediate.m: If something is huge it is very big. When you say this, you mean bigger than large, or bigger than what is usually called big.
intermediate.e: Wow! That dog is so huge he could be a horse.

intermediate.m: If you unify something or a group of things, you bring them together as one.
intermediate.e: Music serves to identify and unify members of the group.

intermediate.m: If someone discourages you, they are persuading you not to do something.
intermediate.e: The government's plan is to discourage the people from owning cars.

intermediate.m: If something happens annually, it happens once a year.
intermediate.e: The meeting is held annually in Toronto.

intermediate.m: If you stumble, you trip or fall.
intermediate.e: He stumbled over a rock.

intermediate.m: To direct or manage; to be in charge
intermediate.e: The principal said that our class will need a teacher to supervise us if we go on the field trip.

intermediate.m: A salesman is a man that sells things in a shop or on the go.
intermediate.e: The salesman knocked on my door and asked if I wanted to buy his soap products.

intermediate.m: A flash is a sudden bright light.
intermediate.e: He used the flash on his camera.

intermediate.m: A telescope is a machine that is made up of a tube and lenses that is used to make things that are far away look larger. Often used by astronomers.
intermediate.e: Freddy used the telescope to see the mountain fifty miles away.

intermediate.m: Ground (generally in front of or around a house) that is covered with grass that is mowed short.
intermediate.e: In summer, I have to mow my lawn twice a week.

intermediate.m: If you spread something, you make it cover a larger area.
intermediate.e: I spread butter on my bread.

intermediate.m: A requirement is something that you need, something that is necessary.
intermediate.e: There is a minimum age requirement of 18 years.

intermediate.m: A hazard is something that poses a danger.
intermediate.e: Please look out for the hazard ahead while you are driving along the highway.

intermediate.m: Alternatively is used to introduce another choice or possibility.
intermediate.e: You can take the bus. Alternatively, you could walk if it’s not far.

intermediate.m: If you inform someone of something, you give them knowledge about it.
intermediate.e: Unfortunately, they did not fully inform the public of the problem.

intermediate.m: A hut is a small place for someone to sleep.
intermediate.e: The farmer went back to his hut after working the entire day.

intermediate.m: If you receive an invitation, you are being asked to attend an event.
intermediate.e: The wedding invitations were mailed a week ago.

intermediate.m: A threat is something or someone that might be bad or dangerous, or cause a problem.
intermediate.e: She sensed the threat of rain in the bleary sky.

intermediate.m: A considerable amount, time, degree, etc. is a fairly large or important one.
intermediate.e: The time needed to do it properly is considerable.

intermediate.m: The width of something is the measurement of something from one side to the other side.
intermediate.e: The width of a standard football pitch is 68 metres.

intermediate.m: A spider is an arthropod with eight legs that makes webs to catch its food.
intermediate.e: I hate spiders as they look really scary. Everytime I see them, I get scared, anywhere I am.

intermediate.m: A sequence is a set of things in a specific order.
intermediate.e: I read the books out of sequence, so I got confused.

intermediate.m: The foundation of something is the basic ideas or work behind it.
intermediate.e: Her education gave her a solid foundation in all the major subjects.

intermediate.m: Something that is marked is significant or notable.
intermediate.e: There is a marked difference between the small and large shirts.

intermediate.m: If you fetch something, or someone, you go away to get it and return with it.
intermediate.e: John fetched me a towel from the bathroom.

intermediate.m: If you speak fluently, you are able to express yourself easily.
intermediate.e: He lived in Mexico, so he is able to speak Spanish fluently.

intermediate.m: If something is done officially, it is done in an official way.
intermediate.e: He is now officially the president.

intermediate.m: Something taught by an important person in religion or philosophy.
intermediate.e: Many people follow the teachings of Confucius.

intermediate.m: If something is obvious, it is easy to see it, think of it, or understand it.
intermediate.e: It is obvious that you can't spend a lot of money and save at the same time.

intermediate.m: If you blink, you close your eyes for a very short time.
intermediate.e: She turned her back and blinked away her tears.

intermediate.m: The number 1,000,000,000 (or 1,000,000,000,000 in old British usage).
intermediate.e: Billions of dollars have been spent on the war in Iraq.

intermediate.m: A picture, or a light, or a movement of a hand, or other thing that tells people to do something.
intermediate.e: When I make this signal with my hand, everybody walk to the front of the room.

intermediate.m: A grill is a cooking surface which has parallel metal bars.
intermediate.e: I like steak when it is cooked on a grill.

intermediate.m: Your eyesight is your ability to see.
intermediate.e: The motorist lost his eyesight after an accident with a lorry.

intermediate.m: The upper thing is the one that is in a higher position.
intermediate.e: The upper floors of the building are for offices and the lower floors for housing.

intermediate.m: A nationwide situation or event happens throughout the nation.
intermediate.e: The nationwide change in support for the idea was unexpected.

intermediate.m: A financial problem, issue, activity or other thing is about money or business.
intermediate.e: Our sales are down and we have serious financial problems.

intermediate.m: You use presumably to show that you expect or believe something to be true, but you don't know.
intermediate.e: The disease presumably originated in Canada.

intermediate.m: If you kneel, you lower your body and put one or two of your knees on the floor.
intermediate.e: In many religions, people kneel when they pray.

intermediate.m: A compound is a material made of a number of other materials.
intermediate.e: There is a group of gases that do not easily form chemical compounds.

intermediate.m: An ant is an insect that walks and goes in groups.
intermediate.e: Don't step on those ants.

intermediate.m: A link is a connection between two or more things.
intermediate.e: The link between England and Europe is an old one.

intermediate.m: An employee is someone who works for a company or another person.
intermediate.e: He is an employee of this store.

intermediate.m: A mansion is a large house that is usually really expensive.
intermediate.e: The rich live in mansions.

intermediate.m: Legislation is the official laws and rules of a government.
intermediate.e: Congress approved several pieces of legislation.

intermediate.m: Nuclear weapons, power, waste, etc. is produced by the collision of more than one nucleus, the central part of an atom.
intermediate.e: Most Canadians live in a nuclear family: the husband, wife, and children.

intermediate.m: A country's cabinet is the main group of politicians who work closely with the leader of the government.
intermediate.e: He was senior businessman before he joined President Clinton's Cabinet as Treasury secretary.

intermediate.m: If something is accessible, you can use it, look at it, enter it, etc.
intermediate.e: The building has been changed to make it wheelchair accessible.

intermediate.m: If something is historic, it is important to history.
intermediate.e: This historic event will be remembered for generations.

intermediate.m: A container where someone puts rubbish or trash until it is later collected; a garbage can
intermediate.e: After eating, John threw his trash into the dustbin.

intermediate.m: If you do something passionately, you do it with a very strong feeling.
intermediate.e: The fans passionately cheered for the home team.

intermediate.m: If someone is sincere, then they believe that what they are saying is true.
intermediate.e: I gave my brother a sincere apology after I broke one of his tools.

intermediate.m: Storage is the space for storing goods.
intermediate.e: There is a lot of storage space in those cabinets.

intermediate.m: The entire thing is the whole thing, every part of it; used for emphasis.
intermediate.e: The war wiped out entire families.

intermediate.m: When you mend something, you try to fix it.
intermediate.e: You can bring your torn scarf to him to get it mended.

intermediate.m: Arrangement is the manner of being arranged.
intermediate.e: The arrangement of furniture in the office was important for getting things done efficiently.

intermediate.m: When you tempt someone, you try to get someone to do something, perhaps something bad or immoral.
intermediate.e: She was tempted to kiss him.

intermediate.m: Politeness is how polite you are to someone else.
intermediate.e: I expect a high level of politeness from people I do not know well.

intermediate.m: A person that is cheerful is happy and optimistic.
intermediate.e: He is a very cheerful guy. He is always laughing and talking to the others.

intermediate.m: A motive is a reason to do something.
intermediate.e: What are the motives behind this change?

intermediate.m: If you are patriotic, you love, support, and believe in your country.
intermediate.e: It is your patriotic duty to vote in the election.

intermediate.m: A reasonable amount or number is not too much or too big.
intermediate.e: The hotel has good food, and the prices are reasonable.

intermediate.m: A graduate is someone who has graduated (usually from a school or university).
intermediate.e: Tom is a graduate of Yale University.

intermediate.m: If you condemn something, you say it is very bad.
intermediate.e: His actions were condemned.

intermediate.m: A fume is a gas or a vapor that has a strong smell, or is dangerous to inhale.
intermediate.e: A strong fume was coming from the car's exhaust.

intermediate.m: Fame is the state of being known to many people.
intermediate.e: That singer rose to fame due to his lovely voice.

intermediate.m: Protection is keeping something or someone safe.
intermediate.e: She ran away from her abusive husband to her brother for protection.

intermediate.m: If something is innate, it is present at birth. Often used of abilities and behaviours rather than structures.
intermediate.e: A cat's ability to draw in its claws is innate.

intermediate.m: When you utilize something, you make use of it.
intermediate.e: Our program will utilize bubblesort.

intermediate.m: An insult is a rude word or action.
intermediate.e: The protesters yelled insults at the police.

intermediate.m: A queue is a line, usually of people waiting for something. (mainly British; American English uses line [n.,3])
intermediate.e: We waited for a long time in the queue for our train tickets.

intermediate.m: A tuna is any one of several kinds of fish in the family Scombridae, of the genus Thunnus.
intermediate.e: The fishermen hauled the 120 pound tuna over the side of the boat.

advanced.e: Her toddler son threw a tantrum when he was told the bicycle was not his.

advanced.m: The act of living at a place.
advanced.e: The habitation of animals in that forest is currently threated by logging.

advanced.m: The character or fundamental values of a person, people, culture, or movement.
advanced.e: A dislike for the ways of the past was part of the ethos of the 1960s.

advanced.m: The trait of condescending to those of lower social status
advanced.e: The English class system is known for its snobbery.

advanced.m: A commodity is something that is bought or sold.
advanced.e: Margaret had regarded her body as a tradeable commodity.

advanced.m: To quarrel noisily, angrily or disruptively
advanced.e: The bar keeper threw them out, but they continued to wrangle on down the street.

advanced.m: Giving advice
advanced.e: The committee can only act in an advisory capacity.

advanced.m: Strive to equal or match, especially by imitating
advanced.e: He is emulating the skating skills of his older sister.

advanced.m: Exhibiting insight or clear and deep perception
advanced.e: The chapter is insightful and suggestive of new perspectives.

advanced.m: A flask is a container used in laboratories to hold, heat, or mix liquids.
advanced.e: The scientist poured the solution into the flask to start the experiment.

advanced.m: Pertaining to or involving or having the nature of space
advanced.e: The first dimension to concentrate on is the spatial one.

advanced.m: If something is done indefinitely, it has no defined end.
advanced.e: This license has been suspended indefinitely.

advanced.m: Characterized by extreme care and great effort
advanced.e: Each item was described in painstaking detail.

advanced.m: Bribery is the crime of paying someone in power to use their power to help you.
advanced.e: The company was under investigation for bribery in the awarding of a government contract.

advanced.m: Support oneself
advanced.e: Many people in the world have to subsist on $1 a day.

advanced.m: The time something takes, or how much time it takes.
advanced.e: The duration of this event will be three hours.

advanced.m: To treat with great respect and deference.
advanced.e: They wanted to venerate the spirit of the great man.

advanced.m: In physics, nuclear fusion is when the nuclei of two or more atoms come together to make one new, heavier nucleus.
advanced.e: Fusion reactions make a lot of energy.

advanced.m: Seemingly contradictory but nonetheless possibly true
advanced.e: It is paradoxical that standing is more tiring than walking.

advanced.m: If something or someone is elusive, they are difficult to find, catch, or achieve.
advanced.e: The elusive criminal was arrested.

advanced.m: Concerned with or comprehending only what is apparent or obvious
advanced.e: His thinking was superficial and fuzzy.

advanced.m: When an object (normally machines) malfunction, it functions badly or stop functioning.
advanced.e: The automobile malfunctioned yesterday.

advanced.m: A deceit is an act used to deceive someone.
advanced.e: Everything he wrote about the issue was just a deceit.

advanced.m: Unthinking
advanced.e: Offering to help was as instinctive as breathing.

advanced.m: A hypothesis is a guess about what will happen, usually in scientific experiments.
advanced.e: The results of the experiment support the hypothesis.

advanced.m: The time at which something is supposed to begin
advanced.e: You should have mentioned it at the outset.

advanced.m: Something that is standing straight is vertical. In a vertical direction means straight up or down.
advanced.e: A vertical shaft went down to the mine.

advanced.m: Your ego is your sense of your own importance or self-worth.
advanced.e: His big ego made it hard for him to admit he was wrong.

advanced.m: If someone obscures something, they hide it from sight; they put it out of sight.
advanced.e: The fog obscured the road ahead of Sherry while she was driving.

advanced.m: If something is marginal, it is not very large, important or central.
advanced.e: But this discussion is marginal to the real issue.

advanced.m: A subsidy is a type of financial support, especially the use of tax revenues to support things which might otherwise fail.
advanced.e: The government provides a subsidy for students that are in families not doing well financially.

advanced.m: If you are obliged to do something, a law, rule, or situation forces you to do it.
advanced.e: She felt obliged to make conversation before leaving.

advanced.m: Your characterization of someone or something is the way you describe them, especially when that description suggests an evaluation.
advanced.e: I think it's a fair characterization to say the government failed to live up to its promises.

advanced.m: If someone is apt, they have a natural ability to do something or learn something easily.
advanced.e: She is an apt student who picks up new concepts quickly.

advanced.m: If a sense, awareness, or risk heightens, it increases or becomes stronger.
advanced.e: Security was heightened before the meeting.

advanced.m: A formality is something done just to follow rules or customs, even though it may not be necessary.
advanced.e: Signing the contract was just a formality.

advanced.m: To be belligerent means to be very eager to fight; aggressive.
advanced.e: Do not offend that belligerent man or else he will beat you up!

advanced.m: Words found within a language that may be used quite commonly by a specific group of people.
advanced.e: Gangs on the street use their own jargon for communicating with each other.

advanced.m: To impede is to make some task, progress or action not to happen or difficult to happen.
advanced.e: The incompetent construction worker is impeding the progress of the construction project.

advanced.m: A reason, idea or writing is qualitative if it is about the way something is, or about the thing's qualities, but not about amounts.
advanced.e: I have a qualitative idea of what his work is like, but I don't know how much work he's done.

advanced.m: Based primarily on surmise rather than adequate evidence
advanced.e: It was just a hypothetical question.

advanced.m: If X dwarfs Y, X is much bigger than Y.
advanced.e: The elephant dwarfed the people with it.

advanced.m: If you forfeit a something you have, etc, you lose it because you broke a law or rule.
advanced.e: When he saw that he couldn't win, he forfeited the game.

advanced.m: If somebody or something is cleanly, a good hygiene has been practised.
advanced.e: This room is very cleanly.

advanced.m: Run or flow slowly, as in drops or in an unsteady stream
advanced.e: Reports began to dribble in.

advanced.m: When something is pertinent, it is relevant and important.
advanced.e: We should get pertinent details for our project work.

advanced.m: If you are brainwashed by something, you have been persuaded or convinced that something is real.
advanced.e: North Korean citizens are being brainwashed by the media in their country about the West being evil.

advanced.m: Express criticism towards
advanced.e: The president reproached the general for his irresponsible behavior.

advanced.m: When you bribe someone, you give a reward so that they do something they normally wouldn't.
advanced.e: Allegations that the police were bribed to cover up the investigation surfaced after the event.

advanced.m: Utter meaningless sounds, like a baby, or utter in an incoherent way
advanced.e: The old man is only babbling--don't pay attention.

advanced.m: Sentiments are thoughts or beliefs that are based on emotion more than on reason.
advanced.e: Yes, those are my sentiments exactly!

advanced.m: Move without being stable, as if threatening to fall
advanced.e: The drunk man tottered over to our table.

advanced.m: Mediation is the process of helping two people or groups who are not in agreement to come to an agreement.
advanced.e: When I was separated from my wife, we had mediation to help decide who got to keep the house.

advanced.m: An urge to do or say something that might be better left undone or unsaid
advanced.e: He felt a compulsion to babble on about the accident.

advanced.m: If you curate something, you act as a curator for someone or something.
advanced.e: She curated the traveling exhibition.

advanced.m: The clutch is the device in a car that changes gear.
advanced.e: The clutch pedal is controlled with the left foot in manual cars.

advanced.m: When you impersonate a person, you pretend to be him.
advanced.e: The thief managed to impersonate the staff in the supermarket.

advanced.m: If something or someone is agile, it is able to move quickly and easily.
advanced.e: Monkeys are agile climbers.

advanced.m: Ahead of the times
advanced.e: Is British industry innovative enough?

advanced.m: Still in existence
advanced.e: Specimens of graphic art found among extant barbaric folk.

advanced.m: If something is sprouting, it is growing from a seed.
advanced.e: The beans will be sprouting soon.

advanced.m: Put together out of artificial or natural components or parts
advanced.e: The company fabricates plastic chairs.

advanced.m: The dead body of a human being
advanced.e: The end of the police search was the discovery of a corpse.

advanced.m: Tediously repetitious or lacking in variety
advanced.e: Nothing is so monotonous as the sea.

advanced.m: A gem is anything beautiful, even if it is not a rock or mineral.
advanced.e: Randy Johnson's one-hitter against the Padres was a gem of a game.

advanced.m: An intense desire for some particular thing
advanced.e: I have a craving for fresh fruit.

advanced.m: If someone expires, they die.
advanced.e: The patient expired in hospital.

advanced.m: If you are altruistic, you help others, even when you do not benefit.
advanced.e: She helped Anne to carry her groceries to the taxi stand and was praised for her altruistic act.

advanced.m: If you disparage someone, you make fun of or degrade them.
advanced.e: The Constitution shall not disparage others and put them in a bad light.

advanced.m: Gymnastic apparatus consisting of a strong canvas sheet attached with springs to a metal frame
advanced.e: The kids jumped on the trampoline.
